CONFIDENTIAL.

June 22, 33.

Dear Burton,

I enclose herewith a copy of a
statement made by Vladimir Alexandrof Morison
accused by Centrocojus Ltd. with Misappropriation
of $25,000.

The case continues in the Shanghai
Special District Court on 28-6-33. Mrs. Morison
not charged also wishes to make a statement and,
if you ask Mr. Givens, he will, I have no doubt,
keep you informed.

Yours sincerely,

(Sd) A. M. Bourne.

J. Barton Squire,
H.B.M. Consulate-General,
Shanghai.

亲爱的伯顿：

兹附上弗拉基米尔·亚历山德罗夫·莫里森所作陈述的副本一份，他被中央消费合作有限公司（Centrocojus Ltd.）指控挪用25,000美元。

该案将于1933年6月28日在上海特区法院继续审理。莫里森夫人未被起诉，她也希望作出陈述，如果你询问吉文斯先生（Mr. Givens），我深信他会随时向你通报情况。

J. 巴顿·斯夸尔，
英国驻上海总领事馆，
上海。

B. REGISTRY
Translation from Russian 5024
29.6.1933

Korison V.A.

Kiev (Russia)
9.30 a.m.          15/VI 33

I, Vladimir Alexandrovich Korison, 31 years of age,
native of Kiev, arrived in Shanghai in January 1933 and
was employed with the "Centrosojus" in charge of the chemical,
confectionery and building goods departments. I was appointed
to the above work in Moscow by the O.G.P.U. Economic Bureau
through the People's Trade Commissariat by Mr. Rosenboltz
personally. On receiving this appointment to Shanghai, my
own wish was only to specialize in trade abroad and, therefore,
for about 5-6 months I did not carry out the points as outlined
in the mission assigned to me by the O.G.P.U. Economic Bureau.
These points were of the following nature:-(1) Political and
Economic observation of the situation in China, particularly
that of the Kiangsu Province (2) The attitude of the foreign
community and the press (3) The status of the Kuomintang Party,
the number of its members and its financial state (4) Dissension
in the Nanking Government, particularly in connection with
the conflict with Japan (5) whether Wang Ching Wei, member
of the Government, visited Shanghai often, where he stayed,
by whom he was guarded (the number of foreign or Chinese police),
where he took his meals and who cooked them for him. I was
told in Moscow that Wang Ching Wei was a worse enemy of the
Soviet than Chiang Kai Shek. (6) To ascertain the places of
residence of the Chinese going over from the Chinese Communist
Party to Kuomintang and to find out what they had then to relate.
(7) Also concerning other matters pertaining to the work of
the "active trio" in Shanghai, I was instructed to approach
Mr. Ivan Nikifirovich Babich, who was nick-named "Scarlet"
(?) and later re-nicknamed "little boy".
pages.zh:
B. 登记处
译自俄文 5024
1933年6月29日

科里松 V.A.

基辅（俄罗斯）
上午9:30          1933年6月15日

我，弗拉基米尔·亚历山德罗维奇·科里松，31岁，
基辅人，于1933年1月抵达上海，
受雇于“中央消费合作总社”，负责化学、
糖果和建筑货物部门。我是由
国家政治保卫局（O.G.P.U.）经济局
通过人民贸易委员，由罗森博尔茨先生
亲自在莫斯科任命从事上述工作的。接到这项
派往上海的任命时，我
自己的愿望只是专攻对外贸易，因此，
在大约5-6个月的时间里，我没有执行
国家政治保卫局经济局分配给我的任务中概述的要点。
这些要点的性质如下：-(1) 对中国局势的政治和
经济观察，特别是
江苏省的局势 (2) 外国
侨民界和新闻界的态度 (3) 国民党的地位、
党员人数及其财务状况 (4) 南京政府内部的纷争，
特别是与对日冲突有关的情况 (5) 政府成员汪精卫是否经常访问上海，他住在哪里，由谁警卫（外国或中国警察的人数），他在哪里用餐以及谁为他做饭。我在莫斯科被告知，汪精卫是比蒋介石更严重的苏联敌人。(6) 查明从中国共产党转投国民党的中国人的居住地，并了解他们随后透露的情况。(7) 此外，关于涉及上海“活跃三人组”工作的其他事项，我奉命接触伊万·尼基福罗维奇·巴比奇先生，他的绰号是“猩红”（？）后来又被改称为“小男孩”。

pages.en:
-2-

On arrival in Shanghai I first stopped at the Plaza
Hotel, but on instructions from Babich went to live in his
home, 374 Kiangse Road, flat 45 for reasons of more convenience
in the preparation of the work. 3-4 weeks later Babich's
flat came under observation and he suggested that I should
move into flat No. 44 next door, whilst he himself went to
live in Weihaiwei Road.

During the first 6 months of my sojourn in China-Shanghai
I did not apply any concret information as required in
accordance with the specifications laid down for me, consequently
instructions arrived from the said O.G.P.U. Economic Bureau
to the effect that I should immediately proceed with the real
work otherwise I will be recalled to Moscow and punished.
These instructions compelled me to begin the assigned work,
but its progress was slow and incomplete under the guidance
of Babich. Moscow seeing that the work did not advance
sent out to Shanghai a Mr. Markoff, who had previously worked
on similar lines in Persia and England. With Markoff's
arrival the "active group" was re-organized and included-
Markoff, Babich, myself and one Mr. Zanegin as a candidate.
At the same time a Bureau of Party Nucleus including one
Nemoudroff (who is now in Tientsin), Babich, Zanegin, Yakimoff
and myself was formed.

The first misunderstandings with Babich and Levin began
in August 1932 when it transpired that Levin was about to sell
100,000 cases of window panes at the cost of 6.8K.50 per case,
pages.zh:
-2-

抵达上海后，我最初住在汇中饭店（Plaza Hotel），但根据巴比奇的指示，为了工作准备更加便利，我搬到了他位于江西路374号45室的家中居住。3-4周后，巴比奇的公寓受到监视，他建议我搬到隔壁的44室，而他自己则搬到了威海卫路居住。

在我逗留中国-上海的前6个月里，我没有按照为我规定的具体要求提供任何具体信息，因此，上述国家政治保卫局经济局发来指令，要求我立即开展实际工作，否则我将被召回莫斯科并受到惩罚。这些指令迫使我开始执行分配的工作，但在巴比奇的指导下，进展缓慢且不完整。莫斯科看到工作没有进展，便派了一位马尔科夫先生前往上海，他此前曾在波斯和英国从事类似工作。随着马尔科夫的到来，“活跃小组”进行了重组，成员包括——马尔科夫、巴比奇、我自己以及一位扎内金先生作为候选人。同时，成立了一个党核心局，成员包括涅穆德罗夫（现居天津）、巴比奇、扎内金、亚基莫夫和我自己。

与巴比奇和列文的第一次误会发生在1932年8月，当时发现列文打算以每箱6.8K.50的价格出售10万箱窗玻璃，

pages.en:
-3-

at the time when the marked price was G.$I.85-I.90. A
telegram was, therefore, despatched to Moscow. When Moscow
did not confirm Levin and Babich sent a second telegram stating
that they could sell at G.$I.60 and this was taking place
when I had a Chinese firm the "Hwa Yu " Company offering me
G.$I.75 per case. After a lot of trouble with Levin and
Babich and my statement to them that I shall dispatch a
telegram on my own accusing them of bribery, they got a scare
and allowed me to conclude an agreement with my firm at G.$I.75
per case. All documents, certified telegrams and letters in
connection with this shady business are in possession of my
lawyer Mr. Franklin Chu.

The second trouble with them started when we had to sell
some cement, in which instance they wanted to act in a manner
similar to the first case. From this last transaction they
could have realised for themselves G.$IO,000.00 whilst from
the first transaction Levin and Babich could have got the sum
of G.$25,000.00. Babich in particular asked me not to raise
any objections, promising to give me a share from these profits
or a chance to make something on other sales. When I refused
to enter into any such agreements, they began to threaten me
with drowning, deportation to the Soviet Union or dealing
otherwise with the assistance of Mr. Kozlovsky, who, according
to Babich was going to be appointed Ambassador to China in
lieu of Mr. Bogomoloff.

In citing the above two instances, I want to point out
that I could have had a very large sum of money had I agreed
pages.zh:
-3-

而当时的标价为G.$I.85-I.90。因此，向莫斯科发送了一份电报。当莫斯科没有确认列文和巴比奇时，他们发送了第二份电报，声称他们可以以G.$I.60的价格出售，而此时我有一家中国公司“华裕”公司向我出价每箱G.$I.75。在与列文和巴比奇经过一番麻烦，并向他们声明我将自行发送电报指控他们受贿后，他们感到害怕，允许我以每箱G.$I.75的价格与我的公司达成协议。所有与此 shady business（原文不清/可疑交易）有关的文件、认证电报和信件均由我的律师朱富兰克林先生保管。

与他们的第二次麻烦始于我们必须出售一些水泥，在这种情况下，他们想采取与第一次案件类似的方式。从这最后一笔交易中，他们本可以为自己获利G.$IO,000.00，而从第一笔交易中，列文和巴比奇本可以获得G.$25,000.00的款项。特别是巴比奇要求我不要提出任何异议，承诺从这些利润中分给我一份，或者让我在其他销售中赚点钱。当我拒绝达成任何此类协议时，他们开始威胁要淹死我，或将我驱逐到苏联，或在科斯洛夫斯基先生的协助下以其他方式处理我，据巴比奇称，科斯洛夫斯基将被任命为驻华大使，以取代博戈莫洛夫先生。

在引用上述两个实例时，我想指出，如果我同意

pages.en:
to take part with Levin and Babich in the said transactions
and that without any risk of being accused of swindling,
fraud, theft or other offences. The documents pertaining
to the transactions mentioned were handed over by me to
Marhoff on his arrival in Shanghai, the latter making use of
them by immediately recalling Mr. Levin to the Soviet Union,
whilst Mr. Babich was to follow him shortly.

At the beginning Mr. Marhoff was very nice to me, but
latter when he had sent his wife to Moscow and remained alone,
he went almost daily to Babich, where I was often invited by
him too, but declined, firstly because I regarded Babich as
a briber and a dishonest man and secondly due to my ill-
health I could not take part in the revelries which were indulged
in at Babich's house, when his wife, like a drunken prostitute,
used to undress and appear naked.

All the foodstuff required for the above revelries such
as caviar, wines, vodka, confectionery supplies, etc. were
taken from the "Centrosojus" stocks without payment and when
Mr. A.S. Ribin, in charge of these stocks, not wishing to be
responsible for the goods taken free of charge, told Marhoff
about it, the latter dismissed him so that Ribin is no longer
connected with the "Centrosojus".

The chief cause of bad relations with me was that
Marhoff had every reason to anticipate that I might take his
place in the "Centrosojus" both in business and party matters
in view of the possibility that I might have been regarded
in Moscow as an honest worker.
pages.zh:
参与列文和巴比奇的上述交易，我本可以获得一大笔钱，而且没有任何被指控诈骗、欺诈、盗窃或其他罪行的风险。与上述交易有关的文件在我到达上海时已交给马尔霍夫，后者利用这些文件立即将列文先生召回苏联，而巴比奇先生不久也将跟随他回去。

起初，马尔霍夫先生对我非常友好，但后来当他把妻子送回莫斯科并独自留下后，他几乎每天都去巴比奇那里，我也经常被他邀请，但我拒绝了，首先是因为我认为巴比奇是一个行贿者和不诚实的人，其次是由于我健康状况不佳，我无法参加在巴比奇家中纵情享乐的狂欢活动，在那里，他的妻子像个醉酒的妓女一样，常常脱光衣服裸体出现。

上述狂欢活动所需的所有食品，如鱼子酱、葡萄酒、伏特加、糖果供应品等，都是从“中央消费合作总社”的库存中无偿拿取的，当负责这些库存的A.S.里宾先生不愿对免费拿走的货物承担责任并将此事告诉马尔霍夫时，后者解雇了他，因此里宾不再与“中央消费合作总社”有任何关联。

与我关系恶化的主要原因是，马尔霍夫有充分理由预期，鉴于我可能在莫斯科被视为一名诚实的工作人员，我可能会在业务和党务方面取代他在“中央消费合作总社”的位置。

pages.en:
-5-

The first thing Karhoff got against me was information
he had received that I had a brother in America (Philadelphia)
which information he utilized by advising the secret agency
that I was not intending to return to the Soviet Union. The
person to whom I expressed my indignation at being pursued
and the disorder and dishonesty reigning in the "Centrosojus"
by stating that in the face of this anyone might refuse to
go back to the Union, was a Mr. Kosloff, who the day after,
as a matter of discipline, reported this my statement to Karhoff.
The latter shortly afterwards called me in and said that having
received information from someone about my indignation and
intentions, by which he suspected desertion, I was to begin
getting ready to return to the Union.

The following case made me realize what might happen to
me should I go back to the Union. A certain Mr. Greenfeld,
sent to Shanghai from Moscow, was recalled supposedly to
Vladivostock in connection with extension of work in textile
trade, but was immediately arrested and sent to Moscow, where
he was tried and executed for the only reason that he was said
to have intended visiting relatives in London. This intention
of Mr. Greenfeld's was ascertained from his and his relatives'
letters, which had been secretly intercepted and read over.
These letters were brought to the "Centrosojus" by a Chinese,
were handed to Mr. Babich first and then to me for information
and were later returned in their original form to the same
Chinese who subsequently forwarded them to Greenfeld. For this
service Babich paid the Chinese in question and some others
pages.zh:
-5-

卡尔霍夫对付我的第一件事是他收到的情报，得知我在美国（费城）有一个兄弟，他利用这一情报向秘密机构建议，我无意返回苏联。我向科斯洛夫先生表达了我对受到迫害以及“中央消费合作总社”盛行的混乱和不诚实行为的愤慨， stating that in the face of this anyone might refuse to go back to the Union（面对这种情况，任何人都可能拒绝回到联盟），而科斯洛夫先生在第二天出于纪律原因，将我的这番话报告给了卡尔霍夫。后者不久后叫我进去，说既然从某人那里收到了关于我的愤慨和意图的情报，他怀疑我有叛逃行为，我要开始准备返回联盟。

接下来的案例让我意识到，如果我回到联盟，我可能会遭遇什么。一位格林菲尔德先生，从莫斯科派往上海，据称因扩展纺织品贸易工作而被召回符拉迪沃斯托克（海参崴），但随即被捕并被送往莫斯科，在那里他仅因据说打算去伦敦探望亲属而受审并被处决。格林菲尔德先生的这一意图是从他和其亲属的信件中查明的，这些信件被秘密拦截并阅读。这些信件由一名中国人带到“中央消费合作总社”，先交给巴比奇先生，然后交给我知悉，随后以原件形式归还给同一名中国人，该中国人随后将其转发给格林菲尔德。为此服务，巴比奇付钱给该中国人及其他一些人

pages.en:
$2,000.00 Mex.  had Greenfeld not gone to Vladivostock, where
he was summoned by a tricky telegram, a criminal case would
have been framed against him as follows:-
    A consignment of 400 cases of sweets were sold by Mr.
Greenfeld on instructions from Babich at prices considerably
below those on the market, resulting in a loss. These sweets
were bought by a Chinese named Mr. Hsia. Should Mr. Greenfeld
have refused to return to the Union an accusation was ready
against him for receiving bribery in connection with the sale
of goods at cheaper prices. On the grounds of this charge he
could have been sent to Moscow or put in gaol in Shanghai.
Mr. Wilhelm, the lawyer, took part in preparing the planned
accusation against Greenfeld by promising a bribe to the
Chinese, Mr. Hsia, so that the latter would confirm that he
paid Greenfeld a bribe. The above case and the instructions
given by Karhoff concerning my departure to Moscow, made me
decide not to go back to the Union as an accusation might have
been made against me too, if not by Babich then by Karhoff that
during the sale of soda worth $25,000, I had also received a
bribe as the buyer was the same Mr. Hsia.
    I had visited Mr. Karhoff's house only on two occasions -
the first time at the end of April when I attended a conference
those present being (Karhoff, myself and Waltman, the latter
having come from Moscow as an instructor in the party matters
and other questions although officially he had come in
connection with the Nephtesyndicate). The second time I went
to Karhoff's house was on May 9, when he called me on
pages.zh:
2,000.00 墨西哥元。如果格林菲尔德（Greenfeld）没有前往符拉迪沃斯托克（海参崴）——他是被一封诡诈的电报召往那里的——那么针对他的刑事案件本会按如下方式构陷：
    一批400箱糖果由格林菲尔德先生按照巴比奇（Babich）的指示，以远低于市场价格的价位售出，导致亏损。这些糖果是由一位姓夏（Hsia）的中国人购买的。倘若格林菲尔德先生拒绝返回苏联，一份现成的指控便已备好，称他在低价销售货物一事上收受贿赂。基于此项指控，他本可能被送往莫斯科，或在上海入狱。律师威廉先生（Wilhelm）参与了策划针对格林菲尔德的指控，他向那位中国人夏先生许诺给予贿赂，以便让后者证实他曾向格林菲尔德行贿。上述案件以及卡尔霍夫（Karhoff）关于我前往莫斯科的指示，使我决定不返回苏联，因为我也可能遭到指控，即便不是来自巴比奇，也是来自卡尔霍夫，称我在销售价值25,000美元的苏打粉期间也收受了贿赂，因为买家同样是那位夏先生。
    我只去过卡尔霍夫先生家两次——第一次是在四月底，当时我参加了一次会议，出席者有（卡尔霍夫、我自己以及瓦尔特曼（Waltman），后者虽官方身份是因“奈夫特辛迪加”（Nephtesyndicate）事务而来，但实际上是作为党务及其他问题的指导员从莫斯科前来的）。第二次去卡尔霍夫家是在5月9日，当时他打电话叫我

pages.en:
-7-

"Centrosojus" business, but the principal topic of conversation
then was that I should go back to the Union, Karhoff saying
that Losovsky wanted me with a view to an appointment to Turkey,
where Mr. Novikoff, formerly in Shanghai, had gone previously.
I agreed to Karhoff's orders to return to the Union,
but expressed my wish to go via Dairen and Harbin in lieu of
a Soviet steamer, intending thus to visit the Consul General
in Dairen and tell him of the real state of affairs in
Shanghai (Centrosojus) and of Karhoff's partial attitude
towards me, who for some reason or other was wanting to get
rid of me. Karhoff emphatically declined to comply with
my suggestion, which fact gave me still more reason to think
that a case of some sort had been framed against me and that
I might be arrested in Moscow for no cause whatsoever and
shot like Greenfeld had been. At the end of our interview,
when Karhoff asked whether I had made up my mind to travel
by Soviet steamer, I said I would think it over and this made
him suspect that I was not going back to the Union, but to
my brother in America, at which he hinted when seeing me off
to the stairs. On the morning of May 18 he called me again
to his office and said that he would be waiting for me at his
house at 9 p.m./the same day, to which I replied that it would
be better to talk to me right there and then as nobody else
was present in the room at the time. Karhoff, however,
raising his voice ordered me to come to his house and added
that the car would be sent for me either to my residence
or the "Centrosojus" to bring me. I strongly protested against
pages.zh:
-7-

去谈“中央消费合作总社”（Centrosojus）的事务，但当时谈话的主要议题是我应返回苏联，卡尔霍夫称洛佐夫斯基（Losovsky）希望我回去，意在任命我去土耳其，此前曾在上海的诺维科夫（Novikoff）先生已先期前往那里。我同意了卡尔霍夫关于返回苏联的命令，但表示希望能经由大连和哈尔滨前往，以代替乘坐苏联轮船，打算借此拜访驻大连总领事，向他告知上海（中央消费合作总社）的真实情况，以及卡尔霍夫对我抱有的偏颇态度，他出于某种原因想要摆脱我。卡尔霍夫断然拒绝了我的建议，这一事实让我更有理由认为，某种案件正被构陷于我，我可能会在莫斯科无缘无故被捕，并像格林菲尔德那样被枪决。在我们谈话结束时，当卡尔霍夫问我是否已决定乘坐苏联轮船旅行时，我说我会再考虑一下，这使他怀疑我并非要回苏联，而是要去美国找我兄弟，他在送我到楼梯口时暗示了这一点。5月18日上午，他又把我叫到办公室，说当天晚上9点他在家中等我，我回答说最好就在那里当场交谈，因为当时房间里没有其他人。然而，卡尔霍夫提高嗓门命令我去他家，并补充说车子会派到我的住处或“中央消费合作总社”来接我。我强烈抗议

pages.en:
-8-

this arrangement, having been twice before in Karhoff's house
and knowing his address very well. However, Karhoff's
instructions that I should come to his house were so insistent
and apparently of such importance to him that he wrote down
the address on a piece of paper and giving it to me said
that should nobody be at home I was to wait (this paper with
the address on it is now with Franklin Chu, the lawyer). I
did not go to Karhoff on the night instructed and had thereby
rendered myself liable to be sent forcibly back to the Union.

On the morning of May 19, I went back to work as usual
and the same day after lunch Mr. Kovaleff, one of the
"Centrosojus" employees came into my room and after calling
me out into the hall said that the Consul wished to see me on
important business, but if I did not wish to go to the
Consulate I may instead in fact must go to Karhoff's house.
Mr. Kovaleff also said that he would, after his English lesson,
wait for me to go together to the addresses mentioned. This
absolutely convinced me that there was something in store for me,
as I knew I could not have any urgent business with the Consul and
also in view of Kovaleff being rather vague in telling me where
and to whom to go in addition to his particular insistence to
accompany me. At 7.30 p.m., after the English lesson was over,
Kovaleff evidently not wishing to leave me alone, followed me
to my office room. Seeing that I could not do anything else
as Kovaleff was armed, I consented to go with him and only
asked him to wait for me downstairs near the car. When
Kovaleff left my room I took a few documents from my drawer
pages.zh:
-8-

这种安排，因为我之前已去过卡尔霍夫家两次，非常清楚他的地址。然而，卡尔霍夫要求我去他家的指令如此坚持，且显然对他至关重要，以至于他在一张纸上写下地址交给我，并说如果家里没人我就等着（这张写有地址的纸现在在律师富兰克林·朱（Franklin Chu）手中）。我在指定的那个夜晚没有去卡尔霍夫家，因此使自己面临被强行遣送回苏联的风险。

5月19日上午，我照常回去工作，当天午饭后，“中央消费合作总社”的一名雇员科瓦列夫（Kovaleff）先生走进我的房间，把我叫到大厅后说，领事因重要事务想见我，但如果我不愿去领事馆，我实际上必须去卡尔霍夫家。科瓦列夫先生还说，在他上完英语课后，他会等我，一同前往上述地点。这使我完全确信将有事情发生在我身上，因为我知道我与领事之间不可能有任何紧急事务，而且鉴于科瓦列夫在告诉我去哪里、见谁时相当含糊，加之他特别坚持要陪同我。晚上7点半，英语课结束后，科瓦列夫显然不愿让我独处，跟随我来到我的办公室。看到既然科瓦列夫持有武器，我别无选择，我便同意与他同去，只请他在楼下汽车旁等我。当科瓦列夫离开我的房间时，我从抽屉里拿了几份文件

pages.en:
-9-

(all of which have been handed to the lawyer) and my hat, I
left the "Centrosojus" with the intention of never returning
there again. On leaving, I saw Kovaleff standing downstairs
by the car waiting for me, but I quickly turned on the Bund
and looking back once more saw Kovaleff still standing near
the car. Whilst in my room at the "Centrosoju" I wrote a
few words to my wife to say that I had gone to Karhoff and
might possibly be delayed, handed this note to the office boy,
who delivered it to my wife. I knew that on May 19 a meeting
was to be held by the "active group" and the Bureau of Party
Nucleus at which my fate would be decided and that it depended
on them, should I voluntarily not go , to send me off by
steamer against my will. I quite believe in the possibility
of a man being sent back to the Union by force as I now know
what means are at the disposal of the "Centrosojus" to do so.

I once saw myself, when still in Moscow, a man in the
Butirska prison, who had been just then brought from Poland
in an unconscious state. I was told that this man was formerly
a chief of department and was brought from Poland by rail.
How much easier this could be done from Shanghai by Soviet
steamer. Having a knowledge of the organization and the
methods of working by Soviet Union agents in Shanghai, I felt
sure I could not hide myself from them anywhere here. Therefore,
the same night i.e within 2½ - 3 hours I left Shanghai by
the first steamer available irrespective of its destination.
I thus reached Hankow under the name of Morris. My first
concern on reaching Hankow was to secure a passport, which I
pages.zh:
-9-

（所有这些文件都已交给律师）和我的帽子，离开了“中央消费合作总社”，打算再也不回去。离开时，我看见科瓦列夫站在楼下的车旁等我，但我迅速转向外滩，回头再看一眼时，发现科瓦列夫仍站在车旁。在“中央消费合作总社”的房间里时，我给妻子写了几句话，说我去卡尔霍夫那里了，可能会耽搁，并将这张便条交给了勤杂工，由他转交给我妻子。我知道5月19日“活跃小组”和党团局将举行会议，我的命运将在会上决定；如果我不自愿前往，是否强行用轮船将我送走取决于他们。我完全相信有人会被强行遣送回苏联的可能性，因为我现在知道“中央消费合作总社”拥有这样做的各种手段。

我曾在莫斯科时亲眼见过一名男子，他刚从波兰被带到布提尔卡监狱（Butirska prison），处于昏迷状态。我被告知此人以前是一名部门主管，是通过铁路从波兰带来的。从上海通过苏联轮船做这种事要容易得多。由于了解苏联特工在上海的组织和工作方法，我确信在这里我无法在任何地方躲过他们。因此，就在当晚，即在2½至3小时内，我搭乘第一艘可用的轮船离开了上海，无论其目的地为何。我 thus 以莫里斯（Morris）的名字抵达汉口。抵达汉口后，我首要关心的是获取一本护照，我

pages.en:
-10-

obtained from the Emigrants' representative in Hankow in
my proper name i.e that of Shermak as the name of Morison
was only a pseudonym given me when I left Moscow for China-
Shanghai.

Soon after arriving in Hankow, I became aware that I was
watched first by a Korean and then by a foreigner; this compelled
me to seek protection from the Portuguese Consul, to whom I
explained who I was and why I had come to Hankow. I obtained
this protection and took up residence in the Consular building.

Shortly afterwards I learnt from the newspaper "Glove"
dated 2/VI/1933 that a charge of Embezzlement of Mex.$25,000.00
was being brought against me by the "Centrosojus". This
aroused my indignation and whilst still regarding my life
unsafe I immediately left for Shanghai and on arrival proceeded
straight to the Police with a view to rehabilitating myself
as far as possible in connection with the accusation launched
by the "Centrosojus" with regard to me.

I have to state the following about the sale of soda
value $25,000.00 Mex. The buyer for the above soda was found
by a Mr. Ivanoff, who was paid about Mex. $160.00 for this.
Negotiations concerning the above transaction had begun
already in April, the price of soda per ton having been asked
for at $140.00. The buyer, of the China Mercantile Society,
after a lot of discussion agreed to pay $180.00 on condition
that the "Centrosojus" would guarantee 62% strength of the
goods. "Centrosojus" for a long time refused to give one drum
so that an analysis could be made of the quality of the
pages.zh:
-10-

从汉口的移民代表处以我的真名，即谢尔马克（Shermak）的名义获得了护照，因为莫里森（Morison）这个名字只是我从莫斯科前往中国上海时给我的化名。

抵达汉口后不久，我意识到自己先是被一名朝鲜人，随后被一名外国人监视；这迫使我寻求葡萄牙领事的保护，向他解释了我的身份以及我来汉口的原因。我获得了这种保护，并居住在领事馆大楼内。

不久之后，我从1933年6月2日的《字林西报》（Glove，注：此处原文疑为North China Daily News之误译或特定指代，依原文保留Glove或译为相关报纸，考虑到语境通常指英文报刊，暂直译或保留，但根据历史常识多为《字林西报》或《大陆报》，此处严格遵循指令保留原文含义或音译，但Glove非标准报名，结合上下文及年代，极可能是OCR错误或特定简称，此处按原文译为《Glove》报）得知，“中央消费合作总社”正对我提出挪用25,000.00墨西哥元的指控。这激起了我的愤慨，同时鉴于我认为自己的生命仍不安全，我立即前往上海，抵达后直接前往警察局，以期就“中央消费合作总社”对我发起的指控尽可能恢复我的名誉。

关于价值25,000.00墨西哥元的苏打粉销售事宜，我必须陈述如下。上述苏打粉的买家是由伊万诺夫（Ivanoff）先生找到的，他为此获得了约160.00墨西哥元的报酬。关于上述交易的谈判早在四月就已开始，当时询问的苏打粉每吨价格为140.00美元。来自中国商业公会（China Mercantile Society）的买家在经过大量讨论后，同意支付180.00美元，条件是“中央消费合作总社”保证货物纯度为62%。“中央消费合作总社”很长一段时间拒绝提供一桶样品以便对

pages.en:
-II-

cocus, but when the above firm were going to refuse to buy,
one drum of soda was issued about April 24.
The Godown warrant was given to me after being signed by
Karhoff and handed by me to the buyer, who paid me the money
for one drum (about K.$26.00). After the analysis it proved
that the soda was of an inferior quality and contained only
45% strength in consequence of which the buyer offered a lower
price. The "Centrosojus", in the person of Karhoff, wanted
then $100.00 in lieu of the $14-130, but the buyer was offering
only K. $80 per ton in lieu of K.$130.00. The bargaining
went on for 2 weeks and only on May 12 an agreement was reached
at the cost of K.$85.00 per ton. Karhoff was immediately
informed of this and approved the transaction. On May 15 the
buyer came to the office so as to get the documents and the
agreement for the sale of soda, but the documents were not all
ready. The buyer , not wishing to wait, said that when every-
thing was ready it should be sent to his office. After the
agreement had been signed by Mr. Zanegin and me, it was handed
over to Mr. Karhoff. The latter approving the contents of the
agreement, asked the Bookkeeping Department for the godown
warrants which were always kept in the safe there, then the
agreement and the warrants were passed to the general office and
officially entered in the books. All the papers were later re-
turned to Karhoff, who called me in again and gave them to me
to be handed to the buyer, against payment. On giving me the
above documents Karhoff warned me to be careful when receiving
the Native Order cheques. The payment was effected by the
pages.zh:
-II-

纯碱质量进行分析，但当上述公司打算拒绝购买时，大约在4月24日发出了一桶苏打粉。
仓库提货单经卡尔霍夫签字后交给我，由我转交给买家，买家向我支付了一桶货物的款项（约26.00关平两）。分析结果表明，该苏打粉质量低劣，纯度仅为45%，因此买家提出了更低的价格。“中央消费合作总社”方面，即卡尔霍夫，当时要求以100.00美元代替130-140美元，但买家只愿意以每吨80.00关平两代替130.00关平两。讨价还价持续了两周，直到5月12日才以每吨85.00关平两的价格达成协议。此事立即通知了卡尔霍夫，他批准了这笔交易。5月15日，买家来到办公室索取文件和苏打粉销售协议，但文件尚未全部备齐。买家不愿等待，说等一切准备就绪后送到他的办公室。协议由扎涅金（Zanegin）先生和我签署后，移交给了卡尔霍夫先生。后者批准了协议内容，向会计部索要一直存放在那里保险箱中的仓库提货单，随后协议和提货单被转送到总务处并正式入账。所有文件后来都退还给卡尔霍夫，他再次叫我进去，将文件交给我，让我在收款后交给买家。在给我上述文件时，卡尔霍夫警告我在接收中式订单支票时要小心。付款是由

pages.en:
-12-
but in the presence of the Commission agent Mr. Ivanoff.
The cheques received were immediately handed over by me to
Karhoff personally. About one hour later, Karhoff called me
into his office again and instructed me to go to the Bank with
these cheques so as to get an assurance from the Bank that these
cheques were in order and would be met. This was carried out
and I got the Bank to chop the cheques, immediately after
returning them to Karhoff, who opened the safe and placed them
there in my presence. The following day, May 16, at about 10 a.m.
Karhoff called me again and asked whether it could be arranged
for the cheques to be cashed immediately i.e. before the
expiration of 10 days (the cheques were issued 10 days post
dated). I said I did not know how this could be done, but
would try and talk to the buyer. Karhoff then also said he
was agreeable to pay 1% interest. The buyer at first wanted
1%, then 3/4% and finally agreed on 1/2%. Prior to going to the
Bank for the money I asked Mr. Hsia (the buyer) if it were
possible, to lend me his car with the armed bodyguard for the
transportation of the money from the Bank to the "Centrosojus".
Mr. Hsia, the buyer, gave his consent and the Chinese bodyguard
and I went to the Bank in the car. Having cashed the money-
a big bundle wrapped in Chinese newspapers, the bodyguard and
I proceeded back to the "Centrosojus" in the same car. On
leaving the car together with the bodyguard, the latter
accompanied me to the lift and when I got in the he went home in
his master's car. It is noteworthy of mention that when we
reached the "Centrosojus" ( 2 Peking Road) the Chinese bodyguard
pages.zh:
-12-
但在佣金代理人伊万诺夫先生在场的情况下进行的。
收到的支票由我立即亲手交给卡尔霍夫。大约一小时后，卡尔霍夫再次把我叫进办公室，指示我带着这些支票去银行，以获得银行的保证，确认这些支票无误并将被兑付。此事照办，我让银行在支票上盖章，随即将其归还给卡尔霍夫，他打开保险箱，当着我的面将支票放入其中。第二天，5月16日，上午10点左右，卡尔霍夫再次叫我，询问是否可以安排立即兑现支票，即在10天期限届满之前（支票开具日期为远期10天）。我说我不知道这如何能做到，但会试着与买家谈谈。卡尔霍夫当时还表示他同意支付1%的利息。买家起初想要1%，然后是3/4%，最后同意为1/2%。在去银行取钱之前，我问买家夏先生是否有可能借给我他的车和武装保镖，以便将钱从银行运送到“中央消费合作总社”。买家夏先生同意了，我和中国保镖乘车前往银行。兑现了钱款——一大捆用中文报纸包裹的钱——后，我和保镖乘同一辆车返回“中央消费合作总社”。下车时，保镖陪我走到电梯口，当我进入电梯后，他便乘主人的车回家了。值得一提的是，当我们到达“中央消费合作总社”（北京路2号）时，那名中国保镖

pages.en:
-13-

wanted to remain in the car considering that his mission was
completed, but I asked him to see me further. On reaching the
2nd floor I met Zanegin at the entrance door to the
"Centrosojus", who expressed his surprise that I was carrying
such a big and heavy parcel. I then at once proceeded to
Karhoff's office and handed to him the whole package of money.
Whilst I was in Karhoff's office, Mr. Krassovsky, Chief
Accountant, came up to the door and looked through the glass,
at whom Karhoff waved his hand showing thereby that he was
engaged and Mr. Krassovsky went away. Karhoff did not give
me any receipt in acknowledgment of the money brought to him
as this had never been done on any previous occasion when I
used to give him either cash money or cheques. For example,
I once handed him without any receipt, a bearer's cheque for
the sum of about G.$5,600.00, which I had received in payment
for the glass sold to the Hwa Yu Company(Mr. Ho), as well as
the money I got for one drum of soda and about M.$1,400.00 for
the soap received from the "Centrosojus" compradores and in
many other cases in none of which had I obtained any receipts
from Karhoff.

I consider that the accusation brought against me of
embezzling or spending M.$25,000 was framed only for the
purpose that should I have failed to appear before the Police,
I would be apprehended by agents of the Union and forcibly
sent to the Union for trial etc. without the knowledge of
any authorities, whilst Karhoff would then appropriate the
money. This is evident from the fact that no official
pages.zh:
-13-

鉴于任务已完成，他本想留在车里，但我请他进一步与我见面。到达二楼时，我在“Centrosojus”（苏联消费合作社总社）的入口处遇到了Zanegin，他对我也携带如此巨大且沉重的包裹表示惊讶。随后我立即前往Karhoff的办公室，将整包钱款交给他。当我在Karhoff办公室时，首席会计师Krassovsky先生走到门口，透过玻璃向内张望，Karhoff向他挥手示意自己正忙，Krassovsky先生便离开了。Karhoff没有给我开具任何收据以确认收到我带来的钱款，因为在此前我向他交付现金或支票时，也从未开过收据。例如，我曾毫无收据地交给他一张金额约为规元5,600.00元的持票人支票，该款项是我向华裕公司（何先生）出售玻璃所得；此外还有我出售一桶苏打水所得的钱款，以及从“Centrosojus”买办处收到的肥皂款项约墨洋1,400.00元；在许多其他情况下，我也从未从Karhoff处获得任何收据。

我认为，针对我侵吞或花费墨洋25,000元的指控纯属捏造，其目的在于：若我未能出现在警方，工会代理人便会在我方当局不知情的情况下将我逮捕并强行送往工会受审等，而Karhoff则可借此侵吞这笔钱款。这一点从以下事实显而易见：直至5月24日，有关方面并未就失窃钱款向当局提交任何正式

pages.en:
FINGERS IN UPPER
LEFT ARE ON PHOTO'S
pages.zh: 左上角的手指在照片上

pages.en:
-14-
statement to the authorities concerned of the stolen money
was made up to May 24, whereas I had written and sent an
official letter to Yarhoff, explaining the reason which
compelled me to abandon Soviets, at 8.30-9 p.m. on May 19
i.e. prior to getting on board ship and the last day of my
employment with the "Centrosojus". It is, therefore, evident
that said case is an entire fabrication and prompted by a desire
to avenge me for not returning to the Soviet Union. Although
being under arrest at present I feel at least that my life is
safe, whereas were I free I could not say the same. Thanks
to my close knowledge of what the local Soviet agents are
capable of as well as the means, money and persons at their
disposal, I also know all the possibilities of their dealing
with me either on the spot or by secretly taking me back to
the Soviet Union.
I shall make another detailed statement on the general
working of the Soviets and their organizational methods on
condition of my safety being guaranteed.
The above is a true statement signed by me in confirmation
thereof.
Vladimir Alexandrovich Barmash-Zorin
There is a total of twenty two written pages in this statement.
V. A.
Shanghai June 15, 1933.
pages.zh:
-14-
声明，而我已于5月19日晚上8:30至9:00，即在我登船之前以及我在“Centrosojus”任职的最后一天，写信给Yarhoff，解释了迫使我离开苏维埃机构的原因。因此，显然该案完全是捏造的，是出于对我未返回苏联的报复心理。尽管目前我处于被捕状态，但我至少感到生命安全无虞；反之，若我身处自由之中，则不敢作此保证。由于我深知当地苏维埃代理人的能力，以及他们可支配的手段、资金和人员，我也清楚他们可能就地处置我，或秘密将我遣返苏联的各种可能性。
在保证我人身安全的前提下，我将就苏维埃机构的总体运作及其组织方法另作详细陈述。
以上陈述属实，由我签字确认。
Vladimir Alexandrovich Barmash-Zorin
本陈述共计二十二页手写稿。
V. A.
上海，1933年6月15日。

23rd June 1933.）

Dear Bourne,

Very many thanks for your letter No.D.5024 of
22nd June 1933 and its most interesting enclosure.

I am writing to Mr.Jivens and asking him to let
me have copies of any statements by Mrs.Morison, as you
suggest.

I notice in Morison's statement that he is
prepared to make another detailed statement on the Soviet
Organisation if his safety is guaranteed. If he does make
any further disclosures I hope I may be kept informed.

Yours sincerely,
（签名）

Major K.M.Bourne,M.C.
Deputy Commissioner,
S.M.P.

（批：For Gomme
A.C.(Sp Br)
