Translation from Russian.

Mrs. A. Y. Morison

Russia
20th June, 1933

Wishing to assist my husband, Vladimir Alexandrovich
Morison, whom the heads of "Centrosojus", a Soviet institution
under the cover of the British flag, want to accuse of
embezzling $25.000.00, I consider it my duty to make the
following statement to show that my husband did not take the
money and to reveal the real reasons which compelled him to
escape from his former colleagues and join the ranks of White
emigrants, never to return:-

As an honest man, who loves his country, and having
become convinced how people who call themselves the "Labourers'
and Peasants' Government" trample down the people's interests,
and also how Soviet bureaucrats, who have attached themselves
to various Soviet institutions in the people's name, are doing
their "business", he left them. He had to run away in order
that they would not take the law into their own hands. With a
view to explaining all that happened, I, Adelina Yakovlevna
Morison, residing at 436 Avenue Joffre, find it necessary to
give below the history of our life.

I met my husband in Moscow in 1928 quite accidentally,
never thinking then that this man would be my saviour, at a time
when, two months later, I was threatened with deportation to
Narim, as a class enemy of the Soviet Rulers. I am an
architect's daughter and my first husband was an officer. I
was retreating with him with the White troops in Siberia when
he was killed between Petropavlovsk and Cheliabinsk. I then
proceeded, together with many others, into the interior of
Siberia and eventually reached Harbin where I remained until
1924. Whilst in Harbin I got married a second time and, having
obtained permission, we both went to Moscow. My husband came
pages.zh:
俄文译文。

A. Y. Morison夫人

俄罗斯
1933年6月20日

为了协助我的丈夫Vladimir Alexandrovich Morison——“Centrosojus”（一家在英国国旗掩护下的苏维埃机构）的负责人欲指控其侵吞25,000.00美元——我认为我有责任作出如下陈述，以证明我丈夫并未拿走这笔钱，并揭示迫使他逃离前同事、加入白俄移民行列且永不返回的真正原因：

作为一个热爱祖国的人，在确信那些自称为“工农政府”的人如何践踏人民利益，以及那些以人民名义依附于各种苏维埃机构的苏维埃官僚如何经营他们的“生意”之后，他离开了他们。他不得不逃跑，以免他们私自执法。为了解释所发生的一切，居住在霞飞路436号的我，Adelina Yakovlevna Morison，认为有必要在下文中叙述我们的生活经历。

1928年，我在莫斯科偶然结识了我的丈夫，当时我从未想到这个人会成为我的救星。两个月后，作为苏维埃统治者的阶级敌人，我面临被流放到纳雷姆（Narim）的威胁。我是一名建筑师的女儿，我的第一任丈夫是一名军官。在西伯利亚，我随他跟随白军撤退，他在彼得罗巴甫洛夫斯克和车里雅宾斯克之间阵亡。随后，我与许多人一起深入西伯利亚内陆，最终抵达哈尔滨，并在那里停留至1924年。在哈尔滨期间，我第二次结婚，并在获得许可后，我们两人前往莫斯科。我的丈夫一到那里

pages.en:
- 2 -

there at once under the observation of G.P.U., who per-
secuted him for two years, subsequently cruelly doing away
with his family and deporting him for 10 years, only for
being a member of a wealthy family. I was hiding for nearly
two years under various assumed names, as my fate would
have been the same were it not for Morison. When the time
came that I should at any moment be apprehended, I came to
him and told him everything; he showed great solicitude
towards me, protected me for a time from deportation, found
me work, made me a member of the Union and in about a
year's time married me. He was taking a great risk then.
The more I got to know Morison, the more I became convinced
that he was not like other Soviet workers. He always tried
to make things easier for others and I noticed, on several
occasions, how he suffered under the terrible circumstances
which surround everybody out there. I once told my husband
that I wanted to run away over the border, but he disadvised
me to do that. Shortly afterwards, however, he told me
that he would try and do so legally.

In January 1932 my husband V.A.Morison and I arrived
in Shanghai where he was appointed to Centrosojus. We came
from Moscow via Harbin and Dairen, stopping over for half
a day in Harbin, where my husband had to report at the
Soviet Consulate. In Dairen he also visited the Soviet
Consul according to instructions received. When leaving
Moscow Morison was appointed to take charge in the Shanghai
Branch of Centrosojus of several departments:- (1) Textile
(2) Wines (3) Chemical (4) Miscellaneous (the sale of glass-
ware, medicines, gramophone records, etc.) However, after
having visited the Harbin Soviet Consulate, he was released
from having charge of all other departments except the
Chemical in view of the special political work with which
he was entrusted.

My husband is a Chemist by profession. Two years prior
pages.zh:
- 2 -

便受到国家政治保卫局（G.P.U.）的监视，他们迫害了他两年，随后残酷地毁掉了他的家庭，并将他流放十年，仅仅因为他出身富裕家庭。在近两年的时间里，我使用各种化名躲藏，若非Morison，我的命运也将如此。当随时可能被捕的时刻来临时，我找到他并告知了一切；他对我表现出极大的关怀，暂时保护我免受驱逐，为我找到工作，让我加入工会，并在大约一年后与我结婚。当时他承担了巨大的风险。我对Morison了解越深，就越确信他与其他苏维埃工作人员不同。他总是尽力为他人提供便利，我多次注意到，他在那边人人面临的可怕环境中遭受痛苦。我曾告诉丈夫我想越境逃跑，但他劝我不要这样做。然而不久后，他告诉我他会尝试合法地这样做。

1932年1月，我丈夫V.A.Morison和我抵达上海，他被任命到Centrosojus任职。我们从莫斯科经哈尔滨和大连前来，在哈尔滨停留了半天，我丈夫必须向苏联领事馆报到。在大连，他也按照收到的指示拜访了苏联领事。离开莫斯科时，Morison被任命负责Centrosojus上海分行的几个部门：(1) 纺织品 (2) 酒类 (3) 化学品 (4) 杂项（销售玻璃器皿、药品、留声机唱片等）。然而，在拜访哈尔滨苏联领事馆后，鉴于委托给他的特殊政治工作，他不再负责除化学品以外的所有其他部门。

我丈夫的职业是化学家。在出国前两年

pages.en:
- 3 -
to going abroad he graduated in Chemistry from the Moscow
Technical School. The term in the Technical School was 3
years; it was an intermediary educational institution be-
tween a school of 2nd grade and a high school. Graduates
from the Technical School, after a practical course, joined
the High School.
We arrived in Shanghai together with one V.I. Holin,
a cotton thread specialist, also sent to the Shanghai Cen-
trosojus office. He was recalled to U.S.S.R. two months
later i.e. in March 1932 for having got corrupted in the
bourgeois surroundings and maintained relations with the
Whites. On arrival in Shanghai we were met at the wharf by
the following Centrosojus representatives:- Ivan Nikifir-
vich Babich, assistant manager of the Tea Department, Albert
Yakovlevich Weinerman, member of the Textile Department,
Alexander Sergeevich Ribin, also employed by the Centrosojus
and a specialist in fur and other lines, which I do not
remember. We stopped at the Plaza Hotel in Rue Montauban,
where we remained for two months. From there we moved into
I.N. Babich's flat in No.374 Kiangse Road, flat 45, Bank
Apartments. Babich's flat consisted of 3 rooms, of which
we occupied one having a joint dining room. Babich was
officially known to be assistant manager of the Centrosojus
Tea Department, but did not conceal the fact that he had
charge of more important political work. In the course of
conversation with Sergei Semenovich Tseluhoff - assistant
manager of the Dalbank, who was also engaged on political
work, and was a member of the Dalbank only as a screen,
Babich said: "You know that I have more important work
than tea. It is noteworthy that Babich's official pay is
G.$185.00 whereas actually he drew G.$230.00, his real pay
as well as that of other important communist workers not
being made known to the general Centrosojus staff. We stayed
with Babich for about a month, when they sold the flat on
pages.zh:
- 3 -
他从莫斯科技术学校化学系毕业。技术学校的学制为3年；它是介于二年级学校和高中之间的中等教育机构。技术学校的毕业生在完成实践课程后进入高中。

我们与V.I. Holin一同抵达上海，他是一位棉线专家，也被派往上海Centrosojus办事处。两个月后，即1933年3月，他因在资产阶级环境中腐化并与白俄保持联系而被召回苏联。抵达上海时，我们在码头受到了以下Centrosojus代表的迎接：Ivan Nikifirvich Babich，茶叶部副经理；Albert Yakovlevich Weinerman，纺织品部成员；Alexander Sergeevich Ribin，也是Centrosojus雇员，皮草及其他线路专家，具体线路我已记不清。我们住在蒙托邦路（Rue Montauban）的汇中饭店（Plaza Hotel），在那里住了两个月。之后我们搬进了江西路374号银行公寓45室I.N. Babich的公寓。Babich的公寓有三间房，我们占用其中一间，共用餐厅。Babich公开的身份是Centrosojus茶叶部副经理，但他并不隐瞒自己负责更重要的政治工作。在与Dalbank（远东银行）副经理Sergei Semenovich Tseluhoff交谈过程中——Tseluhoff也从事政治工作，仅是以Dalbank成员身份作为掩护——Babich说：“你知道，我有比茶叶更重要的工作。”值得注意的是，Babich的官方薪水是规元185.00元，而实际上他领取规元230.00元，他的实际薪水以及其他重要共产主义工作者的薪水并未向Centrosojus一般职员公开。我们在Babich处住了约一个月，当时他们卖掉了这套公寓

pages.en:
- 4 -
the grounds that police employees were living in the
building and they were afraid of being watched, as it
was difficult, under the circumstances, to engage in cons-
piracies. The flat had been bought by Babich for about
$700.00, but sold by his wife for $1100.00 to a Chinese,
when most of the valuable articles marked on the list
were replaced by her with specially purchased cheaper
articles. Mrs. Babich comes from an ecclesiastical fami-
ly, she is about 36 years of age, but usually tries to
appear younger and to conceal her real age. She has been
a member of the Party since 1919 or 1922 and often boasts
of the fact that she had been shooting Whites herself.
She is said to have graduated from a Teacher's Institute.
Mrs. Babich has the reputation of being a "Soviet Messa-
lina"; she is found of drinking and being wicked and is
said to report all those who do not respond to her ad-
vances of affection. She keeps her husband in terror and
on occasions, when angry, is known to have locked him up
for the whole night in the kitchen. Babich put up with
it all because his wife knew a lot about his financial
tricks, which she could have revealed to the Communist
Party. Mrs. Babich always tried to have the leading part;
she and Mrs. V.A. Rover, whose husband was former local
representative of the Tass News Agency, 19 Museum Road and
at present 38 Avenue Edward VII, were at the head of the
local Women's Department. Mrs. Babich made efforts to
include me in the Communist nucleus, but I declined taking
any part in active work, giving the excuse that I had to
cook myself owing to my husband's ill health and the need
of good food, to which she always replied: "That is of no
importance, engage a cook". In her opinion, wives of
Soviet employees - Party members - had to help their hus-
bands by watching others and reporting them just like other
members of the "Section".
pages.zh:
- 4 -
理由是警务人员居住在该大楼内，他们担心受到监视，因为在这种情况下很难进行阴谋活动。该公寓由巴比奇（Babich）以约700美元购入，但其妻子以1100美元的价格卖给了一名中国人，此时清单上标注的大部分贵重物品已被她替换为特意购买的廉价物品。巴比奇夫人出身于神职人员家庭，年约36岁，但通常试图显得更年轻并隐瞒其真实年龄。自1919年或1922年以来，她一直是党员，并经常吹嘘自己曾亲自枪杀白俄分子。据说她毕业于师范学院。巴比奇夫人素有“苏维埃梅萨利纳”（Soviet Messalina，意指淫乱女人）之名；她嗜酒且品行恶劣，据说会告发所有不回应其求爱之人。她令丈夫生活在恐惧之中，众所周知，她在生气时曾将他锁在厨房里整整一夜。巴比奇忍受了这一切，因为他的妻子知晓他许多财务上的诡计，她本可以向共产党揭露这些。巴比奇夫人总是试图占据主导地位；她与V.A.罗弗（V.A. Rover）夫人共同主持当地妇女部的工作，罗弗先生的丈夫曾是塔斯社（Tass News Agency）的当地代表，地址原为博物馆路19号，现为爱德华七世大道38号。巴比奇夫人曾努力将我纳入共产主义核心小组，但我拒绝参与任何积极工作，借口是因丈夫健康状况不佳且需要良好的饮食，我必须亲自做饭，而她总是回答说：“那不重要，雇个厨师就行。”在她看来，苏维埃职员——即党员——的妻子必须通过监视他人并进行举报来协助丈夫，就像“科”（Section）的其他成员一样。

pages.en:
- 5 -

When making suggestions that I should work as a member
of the "Section", Mrs. Babich used to say that under those
circumstances alone I could and should make friends with
the Whites with a view to finding things out. Generally
speaking Soviet employees abroad are prohibited from asso-
ciating with the Whites and all foreigners, as well as to
read Emigrants' newspapers, have clothes made in Emigrants'
shops or buy things in them with the exception of a few
such as Shainin, for instance, who deals in Soviet goods.
Other stores allowed to be used were those of Klebanoff,
Polonsky and a few more. We were also advised to consult
only our own doctors such as Dr. S.S. Shpilberg, 49 Nanking
Road, Room 17, residing at 65 Dennis Apartment, Bubbling
Well, and Dr. A.A. Shishlo, Hankow Road and Dr. I.G. Lob-
zovsky, 7 Peking Road, as Dentist. When my husband was
operated on by Dr. Rosensweig, who was not one of our own
physicians, he was reprimanded.

The other active women of the "Section" in addition to
Mrs. Babich were Mihereva, the wife of A.V. Mihereff, a non-
party member and a tea specialist. As a result of her re-
ports on him to the effect that he might get "corrupt" here,
he was transferred from Shanghai to London, they said, al-
though he was innocent of any offence. The wife of Oshanin,
Secretary of Soviet Embassy, also an ardent member of the
"Section". She was entrusted, apparently on the grounds of
reports despatched to the Centre, to keep an eye on the lives
of the wives of Soviet employees, so as to see which of them
had got corrupted under the influence of living abroad as
the bourgeois class, etc. Mrs. Oshanin, in carrying out her
task, used to visit Soviet wives and openly search their
possessions on the pretext of mere curiosity. Sometimes a
blanket cover or any other trifle were given as an excuse
to prevent this by the owner. It is of interest that Mrs.
pages.zh:
- 5 -

在建议我作为“科”的成员工作时，巴比奇夫人常说，只有在这种情况下，我才能且应该与白俄分子交朋友，以便探听消息。一般而言，驻外苏维埃职员被禁止与白俄分子及所有外国人交往，也被禁止阅读流亡者报纸、在流亡者开设的店铺定制衣物或购买物品，但有少数例外，例如沙伊宁（Shainin），他经营苏维埃商品。其他允许光顾的商店包括克莱巴诺夫（Klebanoff）、波隆斯基（Polonsky）等几家店。我们还被告知只咨询我们自己的医生，如住在静安寺邓尼斯公寓65号、南京路49号17室的S.S.什皮尔伯格（S.S. Shpilberg）博士，汉口路的A.A.希什洛（A.A. Shishlo）博士，以及北京路7号的牙医I.G.洛布佐夫斯基（I.G. Lobzovsky）博士。当我的丈夫由非我方医生的罗森斯韦格（Rosensweig）博士进行手术时，他受到了斥责。

除了巴比奇夫人外，“科”的其他活跃女性成员还包括米赫列娃（Mihereva），她是A.V.米赫列夫（A.V. Mihereff）的妻子，后者是非党员且为茶叶专家。据称，由于她向组织报告说米赫列夫在这里可能会变得“腐化”，尽管他没有任何过错，仍被从上海调往伦敦。苏联大使馆秘书奥沙宁（Oshanin）的妻子也是“科”的热心成员。显然基于发往中心的报告，她受命监视苏维埃职员的妻子们的生活，以观察她们中有哪些人在国外生活的影响下，受资产阶级阶级等因素影响而变得腐化。奥沙宁夫人在执行任务时，会拜访苏维埃职员的妻子们，并以单纯的好奇心为借口公开搜查她们的财物。有时，屋主会以赠送一条毯子罩或其他小物件为借口，来阻止这种搜查。有趣的是，L.奥沙宁夫人

pages.en:
- 6 -

L. Oshanin is wife by appointment of the Communist Party,
Oshanin's real wife and child being in Moscow as evidently
his former wife was not sufficiently active in Party
matters. Babich's wife was a cowardly member of the "Sec-
tion". On one occasion she had to hand a parcel, containing
secret papers, to one Timofeeff, a Soviet courier, officially
employed as cargo supervizer on Soviet Commercial Fleet
steamers. When in Shanghai Timofeeff stays at 10 Hankow
Road, Mrs. Goversall's English Boardinghouse. Babich then
said to me that she was being followed and asked me to
take the parcel, but I refused. Next morning Babich took
the parcel to the market and passed it on to someone there.

Not so long ago at a meeting held by Soviet wives
including Mrs. Oshanin, Kovaleff, Weisman, Lifanoff, Kor-
loff and others - a total of 8 or 9 - the case of one Mrs.
Silantieff-Tsiman, wife of J.S. Tsiman, an employee of the
"Sousneft", was discussed. She was blamed for complaining
of her husband's treatment of her as she was not a Jewess,
of relating about his sadism and sexual perversity, etc.
At first they wanted to advise her to go away to U.S.S.R.
and decided to send Mrs. L. Oshanin and me to talk to her,
but I disadvised them. Mrs. Silantieff-Tsiman remained in
Shanghai when in May 1935 her husband was transferred to
U.S.S.R.

Whilst watching Soviet wives against possible
"corruption", Mrs. Oshanin herself, dressed beautifully,
like all other wives of Soviet diplomats. This was called
"special dressing", which term was introduced by Mrs.
Kolontai, the Soviet Ambassador, when at one of the meet-
ings in answer to an enquiry with regard to her expensive
clothes, diamonds and other valuables, she explained that
it was all only "special dressing" similarly to long coats
and top hats of Soviet male diplomats.

The female members of the "Section" which met every
pages.zh:
- 6 -

是共产党指派的妻子，奥沙宁真正的妻子和孩子都在莫斯科，这显然是因为他的前妻在党务工作中不够积极。巴比奇的妻子是“科”中一名胆小的成员。有一次，她不得不将一个装有秘密文件的包裹交给季莫费耶夫（Timofeeff），一名苏维埃信使，他在苏维埃商船队轮船上正式担任货物监督员。季莫费耶夫在上海期间住在汉口路10号戈弗索尔（Goversall）夫人的英式寄宿公寓。当时巴比奇对我说她被人跟踪了，并请求我收下那个包裹，但我拒绝了。第二天早上，巴比奇将包裹带到市场，并在那里转交给了某人。

不久前，在一次由苏维埃职员妻子参加的会议上，包括奥沙宁夫人、科瓦列夫（Kovaleff）夫人、魏斯曼（Weisman）夫人、利法诺夫（Lifanoff）夫人、科尔洛夫（Korloff）夫人等——总共8或9人——讨论了J.S.齐曼（J.S. Tsiman）的妻子西拉季耶夫-齐曼（Silantieff-Tsiman）夫人的案件，齐曼是“苏斯涅夫特”（Sousneft，苏维埃石油公司）的职员。她因抱怨丈夫对待她的方式（因为她不是犹太人）、讲述他的施虐狂倾向和性变态行为等而受到指责。起初他们想建议她返回苏联，并决定派L.奥沙宁夫人和我去与她谈话，但我劝阻了他们。1935年5月，当她的丈夫被调往苏联时，西拉季耶夫-齐曼夫人留在了上海。

在监视苏维埃职员妻子以防可能“腐化”的同时，奥沙宁夫人自己也打扮得漂漂亮亮，就像所有其他苏维埃外交官的妻子一样。这被称为“特殊着装”，该术语是由苏维埃大使科伦泰（Kolontai）夫人提出的，当时在一次会议上，有人询问她昂贵的衣服、钻石和其他贵重物品，她解释说这些都只是“特殊着装”，类似于苏维埃男性外交官的长外套和高顶礼帽。

“科”的女性成员每次聚会

pages.en:
- 7 -
emigrants, but Soviet employees and their families as well.
Mesdames Rover and Babich at one time kept a watch on Mrs.
Kovaleff, wife of A.P. Kovaleff, in charge of the Fish
Department of Centrosojus because she was taking English
lessons, whilst residing in Srulevich boarding house, from
a man named Ivanoff, I think a lawyer, who was not very
reliable and was suspected of being purposely sent by the
Whites. She was forbidden to continue taking lessons from
him.
Mrs. Kovaleff is a Cossack woman by origin, a Party
member, very coarse and immoral. At one time her name was
associated with one S.S. Tseluhoff. During the civil war
she was in the ranks of the Red Army.
There are women members of the "Section" amongst the
Emigrants too; one a Jewess or an Armenian, 36 years of age,
was pointed out to me as such; she often leaves Shanghai.
Heads of the local Soviet institutions who are active mem-
bers carry on extensive work in corrupting Russian emigrants
by bribing them, thereby making use of the poverty of one
kind and lack of scruples of the other. Active members are
informed of everything that is discussed at any time at the
meetings of emigrant organizations, when junior agents at-
tend under the guise of commission agents. The more prominent
members of these, I remember, are one Dobrishman, employed
by a large foreign firm; he is a Russian Jew and bought
fish from Centrosojus for that firm through Kovaleff and
was also on good terms with Babich and Levin, to whom he
made extensive presents. Another ardent member of the
"Section" is one named Sheikman - the owner of Globe Com-
pany in the Continental Building, Nanking Road.
The Emigrants' Committee is regarded by Soviet agents
as the most powerful of all emigrant organizations, whilst
the newspaper "Slovo" is considered the most hostile of
White newspapers, but at the same time also genuinely
pages.zh:
- 7 -
不仅针对流亡者，也针对苏维埃职员及其家属。罗弗夫人和巴比奇夫人曾一度监视科瓦列夫（A.P. Kovaleff）的妻子科瓦列夫夫人，科瓦列夫负责中央消费合作总社（Centrosojus）的鱼类部门，因为她住在斯鲁列维奇（Srulevich）寄宿公寓期间，跟随一名名叫伊万诺夫（Ivanoff）的男子学习英语，我认为他是一名律师，此人不太可靠，并被怀疑是白俄分子故意派来的。她被禁止继续跟随他上课。
科瓦列夫夫人出身于哥萨克家庭，是一名党员，非常粗俗且不道德。她的名字曾与S.S.采卢霍夫（S.S. Tseluhoff）联系在一起。在内战期间，她曾在红军队伍中服役。
流亡者中也有“科”的女性成员；其中一名犹太人或亚美尼亚人，36岁，被指认为此类成员；她经常离开上海。当地苏维埃机构中担任积极成员的负责人开展大量工作，通过贿赂来腐蚀俄罗斯流亡者，从而利用一方的贫困和另一方的缺乏廉耻。积极成员会获知流亡者组织会议上讨论的一切内容，此时下级特工以佣金代理人的 guise（伪装/身份）出席。我记得其中较突出的成员有多布里什曼（Dobrishman），受雇于一家大型外国公司；他是一名俄罗斯犹太人，通过科瓦列夫为该公司从中央消费合作总社购买鱼类，并与巴比奇和莱文（Levin）关系良好，向他们赠送了大量礼物。“科”的另一名热心成员是谢克曼（Sheikman），他是南京路大陆大楼环球公司（Globe Company）的老板。
苏维埃特工认为流亡者委员会是所有流亡者组织中最强大的，而《言论报》（Slovo）则被视为最具敌意的白俄报纸，但同时也确实是

pages.en:
- 8 -
idealistic. It was mentioned that in Harbin, Lembich at
one time used to receive a subsidy from the Soviet and
utilised this money to build a country house. When an ar-
ticle of anti-Soviet nature, appeared, people laughed and
said "they have not been oiled". The Soviet opinion is
that emigrants will never get united owing to the egoism
of some and the provocation of others in the pay of the
Soviet. There are in Shanghai, according to Soviet in-
formation, over a hundred White emigrants well off finan-
cially, who only live for their own pleasure and do not
contribute towards the military active White organisations
operating in Soviet Russia. Provocateurs exist everywhere.
Chekists at first always allow the Whites to arrange their
plans within the territory of U.S.S.R. and then cruelly
punish them. Sometimes Chekists come under the guise of
refugees from the concentration camps of exiles and then
begin their provocative work here.

The care Soviet employees have to exercise is shown
by the fate which befell Michael Borisovich Greenfeld, who
on false report of a "Section" member was recalled to U.S.
S.R. supposedly to discuss matters in connection with the
extension of the Textile Department in the Shanghai Cen-
trosojus, of which he had had charge. On arrival in Vladi-
vostock he was arrested and was rumoured to have been shot.
He was accused of planning to join the ranks of deserters
and of corresponding with his brother residing in London.
The "Section" member who reported him, was a wealthy emigrant
merchant. One of the accusations brought against him was
the fact that he lived in the house of the divorced wife
of Vidumsky, manager of the Nanking Theatre, at 26 Park
Apartments, 455 Rue Lafayette. Vidumsky, according to
Soviet information, was employed by the French Police. This
was discovered when his daughter once said that her father
pages.zh:
- 8 -
理想主义的。有人提到，在哈尔滨，伦比奇（Lembich）曾一度接受苏维埃的津贴，并利用这笔钱建造了一座乡间别墅。当出现反苏维埃性质的文章时，人们会嘲笑说“他们没有上油”（意指未收到贿赂）。苏维方面的观点认为，由于一些人的自私和另一些受苏维埃雇佣者的挑衅，流亡者永远不会团结起来。根据苏维埃方面的情报，上海有一百多名经济宽裕的白俄流亡者，他们只为个人享乐而活，并不向在苏维埃俄罗斯境内活动的白俄军事组织提供资助。挑衅者无处不在。契卡人员（Chekists）起初总是允许白俄分子在苏联领土内安排他们的计划，然后残酷地惩罚他们。有时，契卡人员伪装成来自流放集中营的难民，然后在此开始他们的挑衅工作。

苏维埃职员必须保持谨慎，这一点从米哈伊尔·鲍里索维奇·格林菲尔德（Michael Borisovich Greenfeld）的遭遇中可见一斑。他因一名“科”成员的虚假报告而被召回苏联，据称是为了讨论与他负责的上海中央消费合作总社纺织部扩展相关的事宜。抵达符拉迪沃斯托克（海参崴）后，他被捕，并有传闻称他被枪决。他被指控计划加入逃兵行列，并与居住在伦敦的兄弟通信。举报他的那名“科”成员是一名富有的流亡商人。对他提出的指控之一是他住在维杜姆斯基（Vidumsky）离婚妻子的家中，维杜姆斯基是南京大戏院的经理，住址为拉斐特路455号公园公寓26号。根据苏维埃方面的情报，维杜姆斯基受雇于法国警察。这一情况是在他女儿有一次说她父亲

pages.en:
- 9 -

had a revolver in him and was working in the French
Police. Kozloff, manager of the Economic Department
of Centrosojus and Lifanoff, his assistant, also lived
there and were asked to leave. In view of conspiracy
the departure of Greenfeld was postponed to Spring, when
the wives would be gone to summer resorts. Kozloff and
Lifanoff both have perfect knowledge of the Chinese
language, having graduated from the Lazareff Institute
in Moscow. Kozloff in particular speaks it well. They
both receive frequent visits of and have meetings with
Chinese communists, many of whom speak Russian well as
they studied in U.S.S.R. On the occasion of a visit
to Kozloff's house I met 2 such Chinese and was intro-
duced to them. Kozloff was later reprimanded for this
breach of conspiracy. Meetings with Chinese Communists
often took place in public places such as Cinemas and
Hai Alai. Lifanoff is a very active and reliable commu-
nist worker; he utilises even meal times to meet agents
in the different restaurants. A Chinese, 28 or 30 years
of age, who looks like a Japanese, with a narrow face,
small eyes, very pale and worn out, wearing foreign
clothes, is working in the Economic Department under
Kozloff. This Chinese is a worker on political lines.
I remember when I was leaving Centrosojus after the
running away of my husband, he was instructing the other
Chinese to keep a watch on me.

When Babich and his wife moved to 155 Wei Hai Wei
Road, flat 15-C, they asked us to come and stay with
them again, but my husband declined the offer fearing
the bad, corrupting influence of Babich's wife and also
because that place was one of the centres of communist
work. The group of "active" members - leaders of local
political work namely V.A. Bever, G.J. Garbunoff, S.M.
Goffer, manager of the local Chinese Eastern Railway
pages.zh:
- 9 -

身上带有一把手枪，并在法国警察部门工作时被发现的。中央消费合作总社经济部经理科兹洛夫（Kozloff）及其助理利法诺夫（Lifanoff）也住在那里，并被要求搬离。鉴于保密需要，格林菲尔德的离境被推迟到春季，届时妻子们将前往避暑胜地。科兹洛夫和利法诺夫都精通中文，因为他们毕业于莫斯科的拉扎列夫学院（Lazareff Institute）。特别是科兹洛夫，中文说得很好。他们两人经常接待中国共产党员的来访并与他们会面，其中许多人俄语说得很好，因为他们曾在苏联学习。在一次拜访科兹洛夫家时，我遇到了两名这样的中国人，并被介绍给他们。科兹洛夫后来因这一违反保密规定的行为受到斥责。与中国共产党员的会面经常发生在电影院和海爱理（Hai Alai，即大光明电影院或类似场所，音译）等公共场所。利法诺夫是一名非常积极且可靠的共产主义工作者；他甚至利用用餐时间在各个餐厅与特工见面。一名28或30岁的中国人，长相像日本人，脸型狭长，眼睛小，脸色非常苍白且憔悴，穿着西式服装，在科兹洛夫领导的经济部工作。这名中国人从事政治线的工作。我记得在我丈夫逃跑后我离开中央消费合作总社时，他正在指示其他中国人监视我。

当巴比奇及其妻子搬至威海卫路155号15-C室公寓时，他们邀请我们再次去与他们同住，但我丈夫拒绝了这一提议，既是因为害怕巴比奇妻子不良的腐化影响，也是因为该地是共产主义工作的中心之一。“积极”成员小组——即当地政治工作的领导人，包括V.A.贝弗（V.A. Bever）、G.J.加尔布诺夫（G.J. Garbunoff）、S.M.戈费尔（S.M. Goffer，当地中东铁路经理

pages.en:
- 10 -
Agency, A.I. Levin, Manager of Centrosojus, and M.N.
Markoff, his successor usually met at Babich's. Such
meetings were, as a rule, disguised as parties at which
eating and drinking was indulged. They avoided meeting
too often. Sometimes they met in the theatres as if by
chance. When we stayed with Babich in Kiangse Road va-
rious meetings were very often held there. Visitors came
in different lifts and some through the courtyard and by
the back stairs. My husband used to ask me to leave the
house about one hour before, without saying anything, but
I knew very well myself what was happening. On returning
home I was always prepared that I might find everybody
under arrest. When under the influence of fear for my
husband's fate, I used to say "What if you get arrested"
he always answered back "Well, let it be so, a good thing
too" apparently hoping thereby to get rid of the oppressive
Soviet work. Owing to the conspiracy we kept the servants
half a day only. When Semedroff arrived and there was
some urgent work to be done, meetings were often held at
10 Hankow Road under the guise of parties. On these occa-
sions we, the non-party women, were told to enjoy ourselves
whilst the men conversed.

Heads of Centrosojus; Babich, Levin, Kovaleff and
others recklessly spent the people's property entrusted to
them on service for their own needs. Wine, caviar, furs,
perfumes, etc. in large quantities were taken and used by
the Party leaders for Soviet parties. The tables were
literally laden with wines, caviar, and other expensive
eatables sent down by the suffering Russian people in order
that communists may obtain therefrom the required foreign
currency.

Meetings are also often arranged in the Parks, Alex-
ander Park being a favourite spot. They come there sometimes
as if by coincidence with their wives and children.
pages.zh:
- 10 -
机构，A.I. Levin，Centrosoujus（苏联消费合作社中央联社）经理，以及他的继任者 M.N. Markoff，通常在 Babich 处会面。这类会面通常伪装成聚会，席间大吃大喝。他们避免过于频繁地见面。有时他们会在剧院假装偶然相遇。当我们与 Babich 同住在江西路时，各种会议经常在那里举行。访客乘坐不同的电梯进入，有些人则穿过庭院走后楼梯。我丈夫通常会让我提前一小时离开家，什么都不说，但我自己很清楚正在发生什么。回到家时，我总是做好心理准备，可能会发现所有人都已被捕。当我因担心丈夫的命运而处于恐惧之中时，我会说：“如果你被捕了怎么办？”他总是回答说：“好吧，那就这样吧，也是件好事”，显然希望以此摆脱令人压抑的苏联工作。由于阴谋活动，我们只让仆人工作半天。当 Semedroff 抵达且有紧急工作需要处理时，会议经常在汉口路 10 号以聚会的名义举行。在这些场合，我们这些非党员女性被告知要自娱自乐，而男人们则进行交谈。

Centrosoujus 的负责人；Babich、Levin、Kovaleff 等人肆无忌惮地将托付给他们服务于自身需要的人民财产挥霍一空。大量的葡萄酒、鱼子酱、皮草、香水等被党魁们拿走并用于苏联式的聚会。餐桌上简直堆满了受苦受难的俄罗斯人民送来的葡萄酒、鱼子酱和其他昂贵食品，以便共产党人从中获取所需的外汇。

会议也经常在公园举行，亚历山大公园（Alexander Park）是一个受欢迎的地点。他们有时带着妻子和孩子去那里，假装是巧合。

pages.en:
- 11 -

meetings of the Political Bureau are often held in the
office during business hours, when important questions
are decided. Meetings are also held on board Soviet
steamers including Chinese communists when many of the
latter come as cargo coolies.

Having refused to go and stay with Babich we took
up residence at 3 Carter Road, a boarding house, under
the management of Mrs. Glushkoff. We very quietly there
and had meals served in our own room, but still in about
one and a half month's time we were told to leave the
place "as it was not considered suitable". We, Soviet
employees, were recommended to live in foreign boarding
houses such as Mrs. I.Gomersall's at 10 Hankow Road,
M-me M. Pasche, 47 Rue Amiral Courbet and II Yuen King
Yuen Road. Formerly we were not allowed to live in the
French Concession at all, but were always advised to have
our own homes. We took flat No.44 at 374 Kiangsu Road,
with the assistance of Babich, who had lived in that
building before. We bought our furniture at auctions.

After we arrived in Shanghai a change took place in
my husband, he became nervous, lost in thought most of
the time, and showed displeasure with his comrades seeking
as much as possible to avoid them. This intrigued them
and they began to watch him. My husband began to neglect
his political work. Although he talked little of busi-
ness to me, I knew that Babich especially was a source of
worry to him after he had prevented Babich and Levin to
steal a large sum of money, being interest from the sale
of a consignment of glass. The "active group" then de-
creed to remove Morison, but shortly afterwards someone
else had arrived from the Centre and stopped the whole
affair. However, in September 1935 when Michael Markelovich
Nemudroff, an employee of the "Sovneft" and a prominent
communist, had arrived in Shanghai and became
pages.zh:
- 11 -

政治局会议经常在办公时间的办公室内举行，届时会决定重要问题。会议也在苏联轮船上举行，包括中国共产党员，其中许多人作为货物苦力前来。

在拒绝去和 Babich 同住后，我们搬进了卡特路 3 号的一家寄宿公寓，由 Glushkoff 太太管理。我们在那里非常安静，饭菜都在我们自己的房间里享用，但大约一个半月后，我们被告知离开该处，“因为被认为不合适”。我们作为苏联雇员，被建议住在外国人的寄宿公寓，如汉口路 10 号的 I. Gomersall 太太处、Amiral Courbet 路（高乃依路）47 号的 M. Pasche 夫人处，以及元锦园路 11 号。以前我们根本不被允许住在法租界，但总是被建议拥有自己的住所。我们在 Babich 的帮助下租下了江苏路 374 号的 44 号公寓，Babich 以前曾住在那栋楼里。我们在拍卖会上购买了家具。

到达上海后，我丈夫发生了变化，他变得神经质，大部分时间陷入沉思，并对他的同志表示不满，尽可能避免与他们接触。这引起了他们的兴趣，他们开始监视他。我丈夫开始忽视他的政治工作。虽然他很少跟我谈公事，但我知道，特别是 Babich 让他感到担忧，因为他曾阻止 Babich 和 Levin 窃取一大笔钱，那是一批玻璃销售所得的利息。“活跃小组”随后决定撤换 Morison，但不久后有人从中心来到上海，制止了整个事件。然而，1935 年 9 月，当“Sovneft”（苏联石油公司）的员工、著名共产党员 Michael Markelovich Nemudroff 抵达上海并成为

pages.en:
- 12 -
the local Party Bureau, my husband and he disagreed.
Nemudroff came to the fore from amongst factory workers,
and had previously served in the Red Army. At present
he is working in Tientsin office of the "Sousneft".
The trouble with Nemudroff began in the following way.
The Babich couple, who hated my husband for his revela-
tions of the fraudulent transactions by Babich and Levin
entertained Nemudroff and gave him presents with a view
to putting him up against Morison. Lately they were
joined in their campaign against Morison by one Efim Ale-
xeevich Zanegin, a prominent employee of Centrosojus, an
ambitious, but not very clever man, who always wanted to
be first. His quarrel with my husband was chiefly due
to employment competition; he resented Mr. M.M. Markoff's
good attitude towards my husband. Mark Natanovich Markoff
(a pseudonym) is a Jew, native of Riga or Vilna and a
professional revolutionary. At one time he was engaged
in subversive work in Latvia and was later employed in
London and Persia, later still holding an important post
in Turkestan. His wife is German and a cinema operator.
She went to Moscow recently in connection with communist
matters. Markoff trusted my husband and sought his ad-
vice on party matters when he first came. He used to vi-
sit us sometimes on business. My husband asked me to go
out for a walk on those occasions. Upon Markoff's arrival
Soviet institutions began being cleared of fairly unreliable
and insufficiently well classed elements. The following
were dismissed:- Grisha Dribensky, one of the accusations
against him being that his sister married a wealthy mer-
chant named Epstein; Ribin for being an alleged ex White
army officer; Hartman from the Dalbank for having a German
passport in his possession in addition to the Soviet.
Several more are still due for dismissal. Gabernak is
holding his position only because there is no substitute
pages.zh:
- 12 -
当地党局成员时，我丈夫与他产生了分歧。Nemudroff 出身于工厂工人，此前曾在红军服役。目前他在天津的“Sousneft”办事处工作。与 Nemudroff 的麻烦始于以下方式。Babich 夫妇因我丈夫揭露了 Babich 和 Levin 的欺诈交易而憎恨他，他们款待 Nemudroff 并赠送礼物，意在挑拨他反对 Morison。最近，一位 Efim Alexeevich Zanegin 加入了他们反对 Morison 的运动，他是 Centrosoujus 的一名重要员工，一个有野心但不太聪明的人，总是想争第一。他与我的丈夫争吵主要是由于就业竞争；他对 M.M. Markoff 先生对我丈夫的良好态度感到不满。Mark Natanovich Markoff（化名）是犹太人，原籍里加或维尔纳，是一名职业革命家。他曾在拉脱维亚从事颠覆工作，后来在伦敦和波斯受雇，再后来在突厥斯坦担任重要职务。他的妻子是德国人，是一名电影放映员。她最近因共产主义事务前往莫斯科。Markoff 信任我丈夫，刚来时曾就党务问题征求他的建议。他有时因公务拜访我们。我丈夫在这些场合会让我出去散步。随着 Markoff 的到来，苏联机构开始清理相当不可靠和阶级成分不够好的分子。以下人员被解雇：Grisha Dribensky，对他的指控之一是他的姐姐嫁给了一位名叫 Epstein 的富商；Ribin，据称是前白军军官；Dalbank（远东银行）的 Hartman，除了苏联护照外还持有德国护照。还有几人即将被解雇。Gabernak 之所以保住职位，只是因为没有替代人选

pages.en:
- 13 -
available.
S.S. Tseluhoff is head of the Shanghai MOPR. Last
year he went for six months to Moscow with a report.
Tseluhoff graduated in Moscow after serving in the Red
Army. He is a member of the local "active group" and
Communist Party. In 1932 whilst residing in the house of
an Englishwoman in Yu Yuen Road he lived with her, being
reprimanded in connection with this matter he had to
change residence. He is known to be, although not a very
clever man, an exceptionally reliable and hard worker.
Ivan H. Babich is a native of Ukraine, he was formerly
a political instructor in the Red Army. He is a graduate
of Middle School and went through a diplomatic course of
the People's Commissariat of Foreign Affairs in Moscow.
He is a member of the active group of Communist Party, and
a great patriot of Ukraine. Taking advantage of his po-
sition, Babich accepts bribes in money, expensive gifts
such as watches, cigarette cases and pens. After gra-
duating from the diplomatic course he was appointed Con-
sul to Mongolia, but not wishing to go to an isolated spot
he sought Koslovsky's protection, the latter being formerly
Soviet Consul in Shanghai. Babich is fond of boasting of
his connections. He is under the influence of his wife
who instigates him to commit service abuses.
Zanegin comes from the ranks of railway workers; has
lately been connected with Textile business, but is not
much of a worker. His wife comes from a better family
of Railway people.
Kozloff is said to be of good class; he graduated
from the Lazareff Institute of Languages in Moscow and
prior to coming to Shanghai had lived in Harbin. Here
he is in charge of the Economic Department. His wife is
a prominent communist worker, she speaks Chinese but
conceals the fact. It is said that she was, when in
pages.zh:
- 13 -
可用。
S.S. Tseluhoff 是上海国际革命战士救济会（MOPR）的负责人。去年他带着一份报告去莫斯科呆了六个月。Tseluhoff 在红军服役后在莫斯科毕业。他是当地“活跃小组”和共产党的成员。1932 年，当他住在余荫路（Yu Yuen Road）一位英国妇女家中时，他与她同居，因此事受到训斥，他不得不搬家。众所周知，虽然他不是个很聪明的人，但异常可靠且工作勤奋。Ivan H. Babich 是乌克兰人，曾是红军的政治指导员。他中学毕业，并在莫斯科完成了外交部外交课程的学习。他是共产党活跃小组的成员，也是乌克兰的强烈爱国者。Babich 利用其职位收受金钱贿赂和贵重礼物，如手表、烟盒和钢笔。完成外交课程后，他被任命为驻蒙古领事，但因不愿去偏远地区，他寻求 Koslovsky 的庇护，后者曾任苏联驻上海领事。Babich 喜欢吹嘘他的人脉。他受妻子的影响，妻子唆使他滥用职权。
Zanegin 出身于铁路工人阶层；最近与纺织业有关联，但工作能力不强。他的妻子出身于较好的铁路职工家庭。
据说 Kozloff 阶级成分良好；他毕业于莫斯科 Lazareff 语言学院，来上海之前住在哈尔滨。在这里，他负责经济部。他的妻子是一名著名的共产主义工作者，她会讲中文但隐瞒这一事实。据说她在

pages.en:
- 14 -
Harbin, connected with Chinese Communists in Party work.
Lifanoff is also a graduate of the Lazareff Insti-
tute of Eastern Languages and is a reliable communist
worker.
Yakimenko comes from a family of industrials of
small category. He studied in Moscow. Here he is an
assistant in the Timber Department and a member of the
Bureau.
Kovalcff comes from a family of fishermen. He was
a commissar in the Red Army. He graduated from the Tea-
chers' Institute in Moscow and was working in connection
with food supplies. At first he took an important part
in Party matters locally, but his position was undermined
as a result of disagreement with Levin.
Levin, according to his own statement, is a former
printer and book-binder. He has been engaged in subversive
work in Harbin and later connected with Centrosojus in
Shanghai. After leaving Shanghai he has now lived for
3 years in Moscow, where he has a home in which his mother
resides. He will not return to Shanghai.
Everyone of the Soviet employees, even a non-Party
member, is compelled to do some work or other in the in-
terests of the Soviet, sometimes even being ignorant of
the fact such as making casual enquiries, etc.
During the past few months Markoff's attitude to-
wards my husband changed because of the latter standing
aside in Party work and as a result of the intrigues
against him by Babich and Zanegin. Markoff evidently had
offered him to return to U.S.S.R. to give explanations,
but then the matter seemed dropped. The last two months
my husband was very nervous, as if he feared something
and the last few days he was in a terrible state, some
constant fear pursuing him. I once hinted that I noticed
what was happening with him and he then replied that he
pages.zh:
- 14 -
哈尔滨期间，曾与中国共产党员在党务工作中有联系。
Lifanoff 也是莫斯科东方语言 Lazareff 学院的毕业生，是一名可靠的共产主义工作者。
Yakimenko 出身于小资产阶级工业家庭。他在莫斯科学习。在这里他是木材部的助理，也是局务委员会成员。
Kovalcff 出身于渔民家庭。他曾是红军的政委。他毕业于莫斯科师范学院，曾从事粮食供应相关工作。起初他在当地党务中发挥重要作用，但由于与 Levin 的分歧，他的地位受到削弱。
Levin 自称曾是印刷工和装订工。他曾在哈尔滨从事颠覆工作，后来与上海的 Centrosoujus 有联系。离开上海后，他已在莫斯科生活了 3 年，在那里有一个家，他的母亲住在那里。他不会回到上海。
每一位苏联雇员，即使是非党员，也被迫为了苏联的利益做这样或那样的工作，有时甚至不知道自己在做什么，比如进行随意询问等。
在过去的几个月里，由于我丈夫在党务工作中置身事外，以及 Babich 和 Zanegin 对他的阴谋诡计，Markoff 对我丈夫的态度发生了变化。Markoff 显然曾提议让他返回苏联做出解释，但随后此事似乎不了了之。最后两个月，我丈夫非常紧张，仿佛害怕什么，最后几天他的状态糟糕透顶，某种持续的恐惧追随着他。我曾暗示我注意到了他身上发生的变化，他当时回答说他会

pages.en:
- 15 -
would gladly run away, but was afraid of them, as they,
the beasts, gave him no peace.
On May 19, 1933, I was waiting for my husband to
come back from his English lesson; he was studying in a
group at Centrosojus, 2 Peking Road, with Miss Fletcher.
The group included my husband, Kovaleff, Bykoff and Ribin.
At 8 p.m. he was not back. I waited for him till 9.15p.m.
and decided that he must have been detained on business.
It was raining so I took his coat to him. When I came up
to Centrosojus I found it all in darkness and closed; I
then went to the Garden, which he often frequented, but
did not find him there either. I again waited for him
until 2 a.m. and then feeling very nervous and almost go-
ing crazy, I went to Kovaleff and woke him up. He told
me to be calm saying that my husband was probably either
at Markoff's or at the Centrosojus. I eventually succeeded
in persuading him to accompany me to Centrosojus; we woke
up the Boys and they said that my husband had left following
Kovaleff about 8 p.m. We then phoned Markoff although it
was after 2 a.m. and were told that he was not at home.
However, we went there ourselves and the proprietress also
told us he was out. I asked Kovaleff to come with me to
the Police. Although he at first emphatically refused, he
finally agreed on condition that I would not mention it
to anyone that he had been to the Police. I promised him
that and we went to the Central Station and reported
Morison's disappearance from May 19 to 20. Kovaleff
then took me home and told me not to worry, but I went
round alone to all the principal hospitals enquiring after
my husband and in the state of excitement lost my hat and
shoes. When I returned home about 6 a.m. on May 20, and
opened the front door I found a letter from my husband in
which he told me that he was going to Markoff on business
after the English lesson. The letter was evidently written
pages.zh:
- 15 -
很高兴逃跑，但他害怕他们，因为这些野兽让他不得安宁。
1933 年 5 月 19 日，我在等我丈夫上完英语课回来；他在北京路 2 号的 Centrosoujus 与 Fletcher 小姐一起在一个小组学习。小组成员包括我丈夫、Kovaleff、Bykoff 和 Ribin。晚上 8 点他还没回来。我一直等到晚上 9 点 15 分，断定他一定因公务被耽搁了。当时下着雨，所以我拿着他的外套去找他。当我来到 Centrosoujus 时，发现里面一片漆黑，大门紧闭；然后我去了他常去的花园，但也没找到他。我又一直等到凌晨 2 点，感到非常紧张，几乎要发疯，于是我去找 Kovaleff 并叫醒了他。他让我冷静下来，说我丈夫可能在 Markoff 那里或在 Centrosoujus。我最终说服他陪我去 Centrosoujus；我们叫醒了男孩们（服务员），他们说我的丈夫大约在晚上 8 点跟着 Kovaleff 离开了。随后我们给 Markoff 打电话，虽然已是凌晨 2 点多，但被告知他不在家。然而，我们还是亲自去了那里，女房东也告诉我们他出去了。我请 Kovaleff 陪我去警察局。虽然他起初坚决拒绝，但最终同意，条件是我不能向任何人提及他去过警察局。我向他保证了这一点，然后我们去了中央捕房，报告了 Morison 从 5 月 19 日至 20 日的失踪情况。Kovaleff 随后送我回家，告诉我不要担心，但我独自走访了所有主要医院寻找我丈夫的下落，在激动中弄丢了帽子和鞋子。当我在 5 月 20 日早上 6 点左右回到家，打开前门时，我发现了我丈夫的一封信，信中告诉我，英语课后他要因公务去 Markoff 那里。这封信显然是写的

pages.en:
- 16 -

into the letter box, but I did not notice it the night
before through being so excited and only made the discovery
around 6 a.m. on May 20. Taking the letter I went to Weis-
man in Honan Road waking him up about 7 a.m. Having heard
that I had been to the Police, he was horrified as to how
I dared do so especially in view of the letter telling me
that my husband had gone to Markoff.

At about 9 a.m. Weisman, Zanegin and I went to the
Centrosojus. Everyone there expressed indignation at my
report to the Police. When Markoff arrived he was mad with
me and shouting said how could I make a report to the Police
the "fool and a non-Soviet woman" that I was. He then added
that nothing had happened to my husband and said that Mori-
son evidently went to Nanking to see Bogomoleff with a com-
plaint against the Centrosojus and tried to comfort me
with this. I did not believe him and was still nervous
begging them to have pity on me and tell me what happened
to my husband as I remembered that my husband was lately
suffering from a depression and feared something. I, there-
fore, had reason to think they had done him some harm and
consequently begged to be told the truth. Markoff in
reply scolded me calling me crazy and finally told me to
go away. I left his office in tears and was taken into
another room, where I wept bitterly. Some time having
passed, I don't quite remember how long, I was called
again to Markoff's office where, sitting at his desk and
waving some letter in the air he said:- "Here, you idiot
and crazy woman, is a letter from your husband. He has
left for Vladivostock". I asked him to show me that
letter, but he bluntly refused and was swearing all the
time. He then said: "The letter is not for you", and we
will not show it to you". I then asked why did I not have
anything and Markoff said that my husband left me and
won't have anything more to do with me. I continued
pages.zh:
- 16 -

投入信箱，但由于当时过于激动，我前一晚并未察觉，直到5月20日早上6点左右才发现。拿到信后，我去河南路找魏斯曼（Weisman），大约在早上7点叫醒了他。听说我去了警察局，他感到震惊，问我怎敢如此行事，尤其是考虑到信中告诉我，我的丈夫已去找马科夫（Markoff）。

上午9点左右，魏斯曼、扎涅金（Zanegin）和我去了苏联消费合作社中央联社（Centrosojus）。那里的人都对我向警方报案表示愤怒。马科夫到达时，对我大发雷霆，高声喊道，像我这样的“蠢货和非苏维埃女人”怎么能向警察报案。接着他又说，我丈夫并没有发生什么事，并说莫里森（Morison）显然是去南京见博戈莫列夫（Bogomoleff），投诉苏联消费合作社中央联社，并试图以此安慰我。我不相信他，仍然感到紧张，恳求他们可怜我，告诉我丈夫发生了什么事，因为我记得丈夫最近情绪低落，担惊受怕。因此，我有理由认为他们对他施加了伤害，因而恳求告知真相。马科夫回答时责骂我，叫我疯子，最后让我离开。我含泪离开他的办公室，被带到另一个房间，在那里痛哭了一场。过了一段时间，我不太记得具体多久，我又被叫到马科夫的办公室，他坐在办公桌前，在空中挥舞着一封信，说道：“喂，你这个白痴和疯女人，这是你丈夫的信。他已经前往符拉迪沃斯托克（海参崴）。”我要求他给我看那封信，但他断然拒绝，并且一直咒骂。然后他说：“这信不是给你的”，我们不会给你看”。于是我问为什么我什么消息都没有，马科夫说我丈夫抛弃了我，不再与我有任何关系。我继续

pages.en:
- 17 -
begging Markoff and even went down on my knees but he
pushed me and I fell between the chairs. Serebroff and
somebody else lifted me. I then got hysterical and in
this state screamed that they had killed my husband and
that was why they refused to show me his letter, which he
had probably written prior to his death. Markoff approa-
ched me and waving his hand before my face shouted: "If
you are not quite mad yet we will make you so and you
will be quiet then". I was led away from Markoff's office
by force and brought home in Kiangse Road accompanied by
Yakimenko, Moiseeff and someone else in the Centrosojus
car. This happened about 12 noon or 1 p.m. From ner-
vousness my left leg and arm got numb. I was given a
bath and then put into bed. Latter on Mrs. Zanogin, Weis-
man, Kovaleff and Bykoff came to see me and trying to
comfort said that I should get calm and go to Vladivostock.
They also said: "He is a scoundrel, don't you see, you
will meet him there and have it out". I got hysterical
again. I could not believe that my husband had left for
Vladivostock as there was no steamer going there and he
could not have gone by any other way. I again recalled
my husband's recent state of depression. The fact that
they refused so persistently to show me the letter seemed
only to emphasize that something had happened to him. I
got frightened at the mere thought of it and said that
until I see that letter myself and will not be convinced
that my husband really went to Vladivostock I will not go
anywhere. They continued to say "We assure you that he
has left for Vladivostock and you must go there immediately".
I refused to do so until I saw that letter. They went
away at that leaving me with only two of the women:
(Moiseeff, Markoff's secretary and a Party worker) and
Bykoff. These two remained with me until late at night.
On Monday, May 22, I went to see Markoff again, at
pages.zh:
- 17 -
向马科夫哀求，甚至跪了下来，但他推了我一把，我摔倒在椅子之间。谢列布罗夫（Serebroff）和其他人把我扶起来。随后我变得歇斯底里，在这种状态下尖叫说他们杀害了我的丈夫，这就是他们拒绝给我看他信件的原因，而那封信可能是他在死前写的。马科夫走近我，在我面前挥着手喊道：“如果你还没有完全疯，我们会让你疯掉，那样你就会安静了”。我被强行带离马科夫的办公室，由苏联消费合作社中央联社的亚基缅科（Yakimenko）、莫伊谢耶夫（Moiseeff）和其他人陪同，乘坐该社的汽车送回家中江西路住所。这大约发生在中午12点或下午1点。由于神经紧张，我的左腿和手臂麻木了。有人给我洗了澡，然后把我安置在床上。后来，扎诺金夫人（Mrs. Zanogin）、魏斯曼、科瓦列夫（Kovaleff）和贝科夫（Bykoff）来看望我，试图安慰我，说我应该冷静下来，前往符拉迪沃斯托克。他们还说道：“他是个无赖，你没看出来吗，你在那里见到他，把事情说清楚”。我又变得歇斯底里。我无法相信丈夫去了符拉迪沃斯托克，因为没有轮船去那里，他也不可能有其他途径前往。我再次回想起丈夫最近的抑郁状态。他们如此固执地拒绝给我看信，这一事实似乎只更加强调了他出了事。仅仅想到这一点我就感到恐惧，并表示除非我自己看到那封信，并确信丈夫真的去了符拉迪沃斯托克，否则我哪里也不去。他们继续说：“我们向你保证他已经前往符拉迪沃斯托克，你必须立即去那里”。在见到那封信之前，我拒绝这样做。他们随即离开，只留下两名女性陪我：（莫伊谢耶夫，马科夫的秘书，以及一名党务工作者）和贝科夫。这两人一直陪我到深夜。5月22日星期一，我去

pages.en:
- 18 -
Centrosojus, and told him that I would not go to Vla-
divostock until I am shown that letter. He got angry
again and striking the table with his fists shouted at
me that the letter was not for me and he will not show
it. I then again told him I won't go anywhere and will
try and find out by other means my husband's whereabouts,
not believing that he has gone to Vladivostock.
The same thing happened again, Markoff swore and I was
finally led away from his office into that of Mrs. Moi-
seeff (the Secretary), when soon after almost all my
husband's colleagues came in there. I told them that
Markoff's and their behaviour made me think that they
had done something to my husband, or else they locked
him up somewhere prior to being sent away, if not killed
already. I also added that I would ascertain myself as
to where they got him to. They became alarmed then and
began to calm me. I was called again into Markoff's
office when he promised to show me the words in the letter
which would prove to me that he (my husband) really left.
Having calmed down somewhat, I agreed to wait until the
letter was brought, as they said, from the Embassy. I
was sent meanwhile to the house of Serebroff accompanied
by Mr. & Mrs. Moiseeff and Mr. Kovaleff. Serebroff came
in shortly and brought the letter. It looked a long
one - about 2-3 sheets - but was rolled up so that I
could only see the words "I have gone back". I could not
see any other words as Serebroff showed me the letter
from far. The words "I have gone back" were not in my
husband's handwriting, I am certain of that. Having asked
him to, he showed me the letter closer, but I still had
the same opinion; the writing was not that of my husband.
After some conversation, when I had asked him to show
me my husband's signature and the form of address,
Serebroff thinking for a long time first then went away
pages.zh:
- 18 -
苏联消费合作社中央联社再次见马科夫，告诉他除非给我看那封信，否则我不会去符拉迪沃斯托克。他又生气了，用拳头敲着桌子，对我大喊说信不是给我的，他不会给我看。于是我又告诉他，我哪里也不去，并将尝试通过其他手段查明丈夫的下落，因为我不相信他去了符拉迪沃斯托克。
同样的情况再次发生，马科夫咒骂不已，最后我被带离他的办公室，进入莫伊谢耶夫夫人（秘书）的办公室，不久之后，几乎我丈夫的所有同事都进了那里。我告诉他们，马科夫和他们的行为让我觉得他们对丈夫做了手脚，或者在送走他之前把他关在某处，如果不是已经杀害他的话。我还补充说，我要亲自查明他们把他弄到哪里去了。他们顿时惊慌起来，开始安抚我。我又被叫进马科夫的办公室，他答应向我展示信中的文字，以向我证明他（我丈夫）确实离开了。稍微平静下来后，我同意等待他们所说从大使馆取来的信件。与此同时，我被送到谢列布罗夫家中，由莫伊谢耶夫夫妇和科瓦列夫先生陪同。谢列布罗夫很快进来，带来了那封信。信看起来很长——大约2-3页——但卷了起来，所以我只能看到“我已回去”这几个字。我看不到其他文字，因为谢列布罗夫是从远处给我看的。“我已回去”这几个字不是我丈夫的笔迹，对此我确信无疑。在我要求下，他把信拿近了一些，但我仍持相同看法；字迹不是我丈夫的。经过一番交谈，当我要求看我丈夫的签名和称呼格式时，谢列布罗夫先是思考了很久，然后离开

pages.en:
- 19 -
as if to consult someone, and returning showed me my
husband's signature: "Yours faithfully, V.Morison".
This time it was my husband's handwriting and signature.
This letter did not console me; on the contrary it made
me think still more that something had actually happened
to my husband and that he was not in Vladivostock. Mr.
and Mrs. Moiseeff soon took me home in a car; this was
about 8 p.m. May 22. (I forgot to mention that on Sunday,
May 21, I lay all day ill in bed). During that time from
morning to night almost everyone of the Centrosojus em-
ployees and their wives came to see me expressing their
sympathy, consoling me and packing up my things for the
journey to Vladivostock. The Moiseeff couple stayed
with me until 10.30 p.m. when three more men came in
i.e. Yakimento, Kovaleff and a fair haired man, an em-
ployee of the Dalless", whose name I do not know. Yaki-
menko came alone into my room and said: "I want to talk
to you". I got up with great difficulty and we went
into the bathroom. "Well, have you calmed down?" asked
Yakimenko and I answered "How can I get calm when I do
not know what is what?" He then said: "That's enough,
believe us we are not fooling you, but wish you your own
good. To-morrow we will come and take your furniture
away to be sent to auction and then you can get ready
yourself. Should the Police come and ask after Morison
you must say that he has gone to Vladivostock and that
you too are going there. If the Police ask how do you
know that he is in Vladivostock you must say that there
is a letter from him to that effect. Should you, however,
let your tongue loose as you did in Markoff's office, I
have been instructed to tell you"......At this point
Yakimenko significantly touched his pocket. I promised
him not to tell the Police anything but what he instructed
me to do. Staying with me a little while longer they all
pages.zh:
- 19 -
好像去咨询某人，回来后给我看了我丈夫的签名：“您忠实的，V.莫里森”。这次是我丈夫的笔迹和签名。但这封信并没有安慰我；相反，它让我更加认为丈夫确实出了事，而且他并不在符拉迪沃斯托克。莫伊谢耶夫夫妇很快用车送我回家；这时大约是5月22日晚上8点。（我忘了提到，5月21日星期日，我病卧在床整整一天）。在此期间，从早到晚，几乎苏联消费合作社中央联社的所有员工及其妻子都来看望我，表达同情，安慰我，并为我收拾前往符拉迪沃斯托克的行李。莫伊谢耶夫夫妇陪我到晚上10点半，这时又来了三个人，即亚基缅托（Yakimento）、科瓦列夫和一名金发男子，他是“Dalless”（音译）的员工，名字我不知道。亚基缅科独自走进我的房间说：“我想和你谈谈”。我很艰难地站起来，我们走进浴室。“好了，你冷静下来了吗？”亚基缅科问道，我回答说：“我不知道到底是怎么回事，怎么能冷静？”然后他说：“够了，相信我们，我们没有骗你，而是为你好。明天我们会来把你的家具搬走送去拍卖，然后你自己做好准备。如果警察来问起莫里森，你必须说他去了符拉迪沃斯托克，你也正要去那里。如果警察问你怎么知道他在符拉迪沃斯托克，你必须说有他的信为证。但是，如果你像在马科夫办公室里那样乱说话，我奉命告诉你”……说到这里，亚基缅科意味深长地摸了摸口袋。我向他承诺，除了他指示的内容外，不向警察透露任何信息。他们又陪了我一会儿，然后全都

pages.en:
- 20 -
left. When I remained alone I began to think more than
more than ever that they had done something to my hus-
band or that he had done something to himself as the
letter was written by him except the words shown to me,
I am positive about that.
On the morning of May 23, Detectives Boloshenko and
an Englishman came to me. Asked by them where my husband
was I answered in the terms of Yakimenko, adding that a
letter had been received from my husband to say he had
gone to Vladivostock and that I was following him. The
Police appeared surprised at my going away so soon, but
soon left. Really I did not intend to go away at all,
I only told them that. On the same day my furniture was
taken away from the flat by the auctioneers. Yakimenko
took charge of all the papers concerning the furniture.
I was being prepared as fast as possible for departure
by the s.s. "Lazovsky". When the s.s. "Lazovsky" arrived
on May 24, I asked Yakimenko and others not to take my
baggage on board the s.s. "Lazovsky" until the following
day. At dawn of the following day, however, I left my
house for 436 Avenue Joffre, where I am still staying.
I wanted to run away before, but could not do so because
almost daily up to 1 a.m. I was being watched by all the
Centrosojuz employees and their wives in turn. Even now,
from time to time, they look for opportunities to meet
me. When we do meet they try either amiably or under
threats still to convince me that I should leave for
Vladivostock. When I refuse they say that I shall not
see my husband in any case as he will be theirs anyhow;
they also still reproach me for seeing the Police and
tell me to leave off that as both the foreign and Chinese
Police can be "bought" and "sold" by them as all detectives
are prone to bribery. Then again: "Don't you be silly
and harm yourself for a scoundrel like your husband".
pages.zh:
- 20 -
离开了。当我独自一人时，我开始比以往任何时候都更强烈地认为，他们对丈夫做了手脚，或者他做了傻事，因为除了给我看的那几个字外，信是他写的，对此我深信不疑。
5月23日上午，侦探博洛申科（Boloshenko）和一名英国人来到我这里。当他们问我丈夫在哪里时，我按照亚基缅科的指示回答，并补充说收到丈夫来信，称他已前往符拉迪沃斯托克，我正追随他而去。警方对我这么快就要离开感到惊讶，但很快就离开了。实际上我根本无意离开，只是那样告诉他们而已。同一天，拍卖商从公寓搬走了我的家具。亚基缅科负责处理所有与家具有关的文件。我正尽快准备乘“拉佐夫斯基号”（s.s. "Lazovsky"）轮船离开。当“拉佐夫斯基号”于5月24日抵达时，我请求亚基缅科和其他人不要将我的行李带上“拉佐夫斯基号”，等到第二天再说。然而，次日黎明，我离开家前往霞飞路436号，至今仍住在那里。我之前就想逃跑，但未能做到，因为直到凌晨1点，苏联消费合作社中央联社的员工及其妻子几乎每天都轮流监视我。即使现在，他们仍不时寻找机会与我见面。当我们见面时，他们要么友好地，要么通过威胁，试图说服我应该前往符拉迪沃斯托克。当我拒绝时，他们说反正我见不到丈夫，因为他无论如何都是他们的人；他们还继续责备我去见警察，并让我停止这样做，因为中外警察都可以被他们“收买”和“出卖”，所有侦探都容易受贿。接着又说：“别犯傻了，为了像你丈夫那样的无赖害了自己”。

pages.en:
- 21 -

"Go home - nothing will be done to you for not submitting
to instructions right away. If you stay here you will
perish because you can't even go to a bar like the White
officers' wives. In the Union, however, you can be use-
ful", etc. etc.

On the morning of June 12, I called at Centrosojus
to find out whether anything was further known about my
husband. When I came into Kovaleff's office, I hardly
had time to say two words when Babich came in and upon
inquiring how I was, asked me when I was going away. When
I answered that I did not as yet intend to go away he
said: "That's foolish. You have caused enough trouble,
it is time for you to get sensible and go home". Several
other employees then came in one after another and began
to advise me to go and stay at the Embassy, where a room
with bath attached would be provided for me, so that after
I had rested there, I could go home. When I absolutely
refused to agree to the above, saying that I will not go
anywhere until I know something about my husband, I was
again scolded and threatened that if I continue having
anything to do with the Police, it will mean no good to me.

On the morning of June 13, I learnt that my husband
had voluntarily come to the Police so as to rehabilitate
himself vis a vis the charge of embezzlement brought
against him by Centrosojus. My last meeting was with Mrs.
Bykoff on June 17; the latter undoubtedly acting on ins-
tructions.. The same things were said again:- friendly
advices, warnings, threats of starvation, etc. etc. also
phrases such as "Why don't you have pity on yourself, Ada,
by remaining here. The Police will be questioning you
closely and you do know a lot." I promised her not to tell
the Police anything, adding also that I was not going
anywhere and wished to be left alone and in peace, so asked
her please not to come and see me anymore.
pages.zh:
- 21 -

“回家吧——你不立即服从指令也不会对你怎么样。如果你留在这里，你会完蛋，因为你甚至不能像白俄军官的妻子们那样去酒吧。然而在联盟（指苏联/苏维埃体系），你可以发挥作用”，等等等等。

6月12日上午，我去苏联消费合作社中央联社打听是否有关于我丈夫的进一步消息。当我走进科瓦列夫的办公室时，还没来得及说两句话，巴比奇（Babich）就进来了，询问我情况后，问我什么时候走。当我回答说我目前还不打算走时，他说：“真愚蠢。你惹的麻烦够多了，是时候清醒一点，回家了”。随后其他几名员工陆续进来，开始劝我去大使馆住，那里会为我提供一个带浴室的房间，以便我休息后可以回家。当我坚决拒绝上述提议，并表示在得知丈夫消息之前哪里也不去时，我再次遭到责骂和威胁，称如果我继续与警方有任何接触，对我没有好处。

6月13日上午，我得知丈夫自愿前往警局，以便就苏联消费合作社中央联社对他提出的挪用公款指控恢复名誉。我最后一次见面是在6月17日与贝科夫夫人；后者无疑是在执行指令。同样的话又被重复了一遍：友好的建议、警告、饥饿威胁等等，还有诸如“阿达（Ada），你留在这里怎么不可怜可怜自己。警察会严密审问你，而你知道很多内情”之类的话。我向她承诺不向警察透露任何信息，并补充说我不打算去任何地方，希望得到安宁，不被打扰，因此请她不要再来看我。

pages.en:
- 22 -

this, but not as friends.

I became calmer and was able to breathe freely only
when I knew that my husband was alive and not in the claws
of the Chekists, but had given himself up to the Police
voluntarily in order to clear up the falseness of accu-
sations brought against him. It is the usual custom of
the Chekists to "blacken" the character of the person who
leaves them.

I firmly trust that the Court and the Russian and
Foreign Public will understand and acquit my husband, who
is not a criminal as the Communists are trying to make
him out, but a long suffering human being, who, although
rather late, has understood the peril for Russia and the
whole of humanity of Soviet communist rule and teaching.
He has consequently broken away from the past associations
on the grounds of real conviction.

Signed: A. Y. Morison
Shanghai, June 30, 1933.
pages.zh:
- 22 -

这一点，但并非以朋友身份。

只有当我得知我的丈夫还活着，并未落入契卡人员（Chekists）的魔掌，而是为了澄清针对他的虚假指控而自愿向警方投案时，我才平静下来，能够自由呼吸。契卡人员的惯常做法是“抹黑”那些离开他们的人的名誉。

我坚信，法庭以及俄国和外国公众会理解并宣判我的丈夫无罪。他并非共产党人试图塑造的那种罪犯，而是一个长期受苦的人，尽管为时已晚，但他已认识到苏维埃共产主义统治和教义对俄国及全人类的危害。因此，基于真正的信念，他已与过去的关联决裂。

签署人：A. Y. Morison
上海，1933年6月30日。

pages.en:
MEMORANDUM ON V.A. MORISON AND HIS CASE AGAINST THE
CENTROSOJUS.

Vladimir Alexandrovitch Morison, Soviet citizen of
Jewish origin, born 1901 at Kiev. He first came to
the notice of the Municipal Police in January, 1938, follow-
ing his arrival in Shanghai from Dairen together with his
wife, Mrs. A. Ya. Morison. He is reported to have
graduated in Chemistry from the Moscow Technical School in
1929 or 1930. In Shanghai he was appointed manager of
the Chemical Department of the local branch of the
Centrosojus (England), Ld., No. 2 Peking Road. Following
their arrival in Shanghai the Morison couple resided at
the Plaza Hotel for about two months, after which they
removed to Flat 45, No. 374 Kiangsi Road. This flat
they shared with I. M. Babitch, assistant manager of the
Centrosojus. In the beginning of May, 1933, they went
to live at No. 3 Carter Road, from which address they soon
removed to Flat 44, No. 374 Kiangsi Road where they resided
until the time when Morison decided to sever his connections
with the Centrosojus.

Early in the morning of May 19, 1933, Mrs. Morison
came to the Central police station and reported that her
husband had been missing since the evening of May 18.
From her statement to the press made at a later date it
appears that she did so being under the impression that
something untoward had happened to her husband and that
the local Soviet authorities had something to do with the
affair. It seems also that her action in reporting the
matter to the police aroused the indignation of Mr. M. N.
Markoff, manager of the local branch of the Centrosojus,
and that efforts were made by him immediately to place
Mrs. Morison on board a Soviet steamer, which was scheduled
to leave Shanghai for Vladivostock within a few days.
pages.zh:
关于 V.A. Morison 及其起诉 Centrosojus 一案的备忘录。

Vladimir Alexandrovitch Morison，犹太裔苏联公民，1901年生于基辅。他于1938年1月与妻子 A. Ya. Morison 夫人从大连抵达上海后，首次进入工部局警方的视线。据报他于1929或1930年毕业于莫斯科技术学校化学专业。在上海，他被任命为位于北京路2号的 Centrosojus（英国）有限公司当地分行的化学部经理。Morison 夫妇抵达上海后，在 Plaza Hotel（华懋饭店）居住了约两个月，随后搬至江西路374号45室公寓。该公寓由他们与 Centrosojus 副经理 I. M. Babitch 合租。1933年5月初，他们搬至卡特路3号，不久后又搬至江西路374号44室公寓，并在此居住，直到 Morison 决定切断与 Centrosojus 的联系为止。

1933年5月19日清晨，Morison 夫人来到中央捕房报案，称其丈夫自5月18日晚起失踪。从她后来向媒体发表的声明来看，她之所以这样做，是因为她以为丈夫遭遇了不测，且当地苏联当局与此事有关。似乎她的报警行为激怒了 Centrosojus 当地分行经理 M. N. Markoff 先生，后者立即试图将 Morison 夫人送上一艘苏联轮船，该船计划在几天内离开上海前往符拉迪沃斯托克（海参崴）。

pages.en:
-2-

Mrs. Morison, however, refused to obey Markoff's order
pending some definite information regarding the whereabouts
of her husband, and on May 23 secretly removed to No. 436
Avenue Joffre.

On May 24, Mr. Markoff reported at the Central
police station that V. A. Morison had absconded taking
with him the sum of $25,000., property of the Centrosojus.

Nothing was heard of Morison until June 13 when
he came to the Central Police station and stated that while
in Hankow he had learned from newspapers of the charge of
misappropriation brought against him by Markoff and that,
therefore, he had returned to Shanghai in order to
surrender to the police and rehabilitate himself in
connection with the charge referred to above. He also
stated that while in Hankow he had taken out emigrant's
papers.

Morison was brought before the Shanghai Special
District Court on June 14 on a charge of misappropriation.
The case was remanded until June 28 when he was acquitted.

The reasons why Morison so suddenly severed his
connections with the Centrosojus and repudiated his Soviet
citizenship are not clear. The management of the
Centrosojus were unable to prove their allegation regarding
Morison having misappropriated their money and, on the
other hand, Morison's general attitude towards the
Centrosojus during the whole period following his open
breach with that concern contradicts his declaration that
in breaking his relations with the Centrosojus and becoming
an emigrant he was inspired by motives of a political
nature.

In the introductory part of Morison's statement,
which he made to detectives of the Central police station
on June 15 ( Appendix " A "), as well as in Mrs. Morison's
pages.zh:
-2-

然而，Morison 夫人拒绝服从 Markoff 的命令，坚持要获得关于丈夫下落的明确信息，并于5月23日秘密搬至霞飞路436号。

5月24日，Markoff 先生向中央捕房报告称，V. A. Morison 已潜逃，并带走了属于 Centrosojus 的25,000美元款项。

直到6月13日才有关于 Morison 的消息，当天他来到中央捕房，陈述称他在汉口时从报纸上得知 Markoff 对他提出的挪用公款指控，因此他返回上海向警方自首，以洗清上述指控带来的嫌疑。他还表示，他在汉口期间办理了移民证件。

6月14日，Morison 因挪用公款罪被提审至上海特区法院。案件延期至6月28日审理，当时他被宣判无罪。

Morison 如此突然地切断与 Centrosojus 的联系并放弃其苏联公民身份的原因尚不清楚。Centrosojus 管理层无法证明其关于 Morison 挪用公款的指控；另一方面，Morison 在与该机构公开决裂后的整个期间内对其的一般态度，与他所宣称的断绝关系并成为移民是出于政治动机的说法相矛盾。

在 Morison 于6月15日向中央捕房侦探所作的陈述（附录“A”）的引言部分，以及 Morison 夫人的

pages.en:
-3-
statement to the press on June 20 (Appendix " B "), their
endeavours to represent the whole affair as a purely
political one, are evident. According to them, Morison
was charged with a certain secret political work in
Shanghai, which he was reluctant to carry out. He also
came into conflict with certain employees of the Centro-
sojus on account of his opposition to their dishonest
handling of business transactions to the detriment of
the interests of the Soviet government. Therefore, he was
first made the subject of persecution on the part of
Markoff and finally was ordered to return to the USSR
where, he was sure, a severe punishment awaited him solely
on the strength of the accusations made against him by his
enemies. Consequently, he refused to obey the order
and, as a revenge, a false criminal charge was brought
against him by the Centrosojus in order to blacken his
character. The nature of the secret political work, with
which Morison was entrusted, was described in his statement
in very vague terms. However, he stated that he was
prepared to make a detailed statement on the general working
of the Soviet organizations, if his safety was guaranteed.
As soon as members of the Special Branch were
allowed to interview Morison, the matter of the statement
he intended to make was taken up, but he showed a stubborn
reluctance to discuss the subject. At first he demanded
a guarantee that a visa would be granted to him to enable
him to proceed to a certain country. His next excuse was
that he had been advised by a certain party to keep his
mouth shut. Finally, he said that he was under no
obligation whatever to supply to the police any information
on the subject in question. After much reasoning he was
persuaded to make a statement on what he knew about the
alleged political activities of the local branch of the
pages.zh:
-3-
6月20日向媒体发表的声明（附录“B”）中，他们试图将整个事件描绘成纯粹的政治事件，这一点显而易见。据他们称，Morison 被指派在上海从事某项秘密政治工作，但他不愿执行。此外，由于反对 Centrosojus 某些员工以损害苏联政府利益为代价进行不诚实的商业交易，他与这些员工发生了冲突。因此，他首先成为 Markoff 迫害的对象，最后被命令返回苏联，他确信，仅凭敌人对他的指控，等待他的将是严厉的惩罚。因此，他拒绝服从命令，作为报复，Centrosojus 对他提出了虚假的刑事指控，以抹黑他的名誉。Morison 在其陈述中以非常模糊的措辞描述了委托给他的秘密政治工作的性质。然而，他表示，如果保证他的安全，他准备就苏联组织的一般运作情况作出详细陈述。
一旦特别支部（Special Branch）成员获准会见 Morison，便着手处理他打算作出的陈述事宜，但他表现出顽固的抵触情绪，不愿讨论该主题。起初，他要求保证向他签发签证，以便他能前往某个特定国家。他接下来的借口是，某一方建议他保持沉默。最后，他说他没有任何义务向警方提供有关该问题的任何信息。经过多方劝解，他被说服就其所知的 Centrosojus 当地分行所谓政治活动

pages.en:
-4-
Centrosojus and their individual employees. However,
after this statement had been taken from him verbatim in
the course of two interviews during the period of his
detention (June 25 and 26 respectively), he refused to
sign it.
The statement consisted of information of a general
character and of details of various Soviet employees'
past life, which may or may not be true. It did not
contain a single fact of interest, which could be verified
or serve as a starting point for investigation. The
following detail shows how much this statement could be
relied upon:-
On being asked if agents of the Comintern of the
Houlens type were in contact with local Soviet employees
engaged in secret political work, Morison replied in the
affirmative and added that on one occasion I. E. Babitch,
when hastily leaving the premises of the Centrosojus, said
that he had to keep an appointment with Houlens who was
waiting for him in the Public Gardens. Asked if he
could remember the date, Morison, after some deliberation,
replied that he was certain it was late during the autumn
of 1932. It will be recalled that Houlens was arrested
on June 15, 1931, and that Morison arrived in Shanghai
on January 18, 1932.
Following his acquittal on June 28, 1932, Morison
put aside the matter of the "revelations" and paid his
full attention to the business side of the affair.
According to his own statement, he sent about the middle
of July, through his legal adviser, a letter to the
manager of the Centrosojus, which contained a demand to
return him the sum of G.$11,470 and $700-0-0, which, he
alleged, had been unlawfully taken away from his house by
certain employees of the Centrosojus during his absence
to Hankow. In addition, a compensation for bringing
pages.zh:
-4-
及其个别员工的情况作出陈述。然而，在他被拘留期间（分别为6月25日和26日）进行的两次面谈中，逐字记录了他的陈述后，他拒绝签字。
该陈述包含一般性信息以及各种苏联员工过去生活的细节，这些信息可能属实，也可能不属实。其中不包含任何可核实或可作为调查起点的确切事实。以下细节显示了该陈述的可信度有多低：
当被问及共产国际（Comintern）的 Houlens 类型特工是否与从事秘密政治工作的当地苏联员工有联系时，Morison 给予了肯定回答，并补充说，有一次 I. E. Babitch 匆忙离开 Centrosojus 办公场所时，说他要去赴 Houlens 的约，Houlens 正在公共花园（Public Gardens）等他。当被问及是否记得日期时，Morison 思考片刻后回答说，他确定那是1932年秋末。需要指出的是，Houlens 于1931年6月15日被捕，而 Morison 于1932年1月18日抵达上海。
在1932年6月28日被宣判无罪后，Morison 搁置了“揭露”一事，将全部注意力转向该事件的商业方面。根据他自己的陈述，他在7月中旬通过其法律顾问向 Centrosojus 经理发送了一封信，要求归还11,470金元和700美元，他声称这些钱是他去汉口期间，被 Centrosojus 的某些员工非法从其家中拿走的。此外，他还要求赔偿因对他提出

pages.en:
-5-
a false accusation against him was also demanded, the total
sum amounting to about $70,000.
A period of correspondence and negotiations between
the legal advisers of the parties concerned ensued, which
terminated some time during the earlier part of August with
the refusal on the part of the manager of the Centrosojus to
comply with Morison's demand. The latter then instituted
private criminal proceedings at the Shanghai Special District
Court against N.N. Markoff and five other employees of the
Centrosojus: I.N. Babitch, A.Z. Yakimenko, E.A. Sanegin,
N. Krassovsky, Mrs E. Bykoff and Mrs A.G. Moiseeff, the
charges being false accusation, illegal detention and robbery.
On August 21 Morison's letter to the Editors of local
Russian newspapers was published in which he ridiculed Markoff's
statement to the press on the subject of the activities of the
Centrosojus. The letter (Appendix "C") also contained a
series of allegations of a very serious nature regarding the
subversive political activities of employees of the local
branch of the Centrosojus. With the exception of a statement
to the Chinese press made by Markoff on September 3, in which
he denied the allegations regarding the political activities
of the Centrosojus, no action was taken by that concern against
Morison in connection with the matter.
The case against the employees of the Centrosojus came
up for hearing in the Shanghai Special District Court on
September 7, was continued on September 18 and October 23 and
was concluded on October 25, when all accused were acquitted.
At the same time a counter charge of false accusation filed by
the accused against Morison was also dismissed.
According to our information Morison during the period
from September 7 to October 25 made two statements (Appendices
"D" and "E") to the Chinese Military Authorities on the
subject of the political activities of the Soviet Government
institutions in China.
pages.zh:
-5-
虚假指控造成的损失，总金额约为70,000美元。
随后，双方律师之间进行了一段时间的信函往来和谈判，最终在8月上旬以 Centrosojus 经理拒绝满足 Morison 的要求而告终。随后，Morison 在上海特区法院对 N.N. Markoff 及 Centrosojus 的其他五名员工提起私人刑事诉讼，这五人分别是：I.N. Babitch、A.Z. Yakimenko、E.A. Sanegin、N. Krassovsky、E. Bykoff 夫人和 A.G. Moiseeff 夫人，指控罪名包括诬告、非法拘禁和抢劫。
8月21日，Morison 致当地俄文报纸编辑的信被刊登，信中嘲讽了 Markoff 就 Centrosojus 活动向媒体发表的声明。该信（附录“C”）还包含一系列关于 Centrosojus 当地分行员工从事颠覆性政治活动的严重指控。除了 Markoff 于9月3日向中文媒体发表声明否认有关 Centrosojus 政治活动的指控外，该机构未就此事对 Morison 采取任何行动。
起诉 Centrosojus 员工的案件于9月7日在上海特区法院开庭审理，并于9月18日和10月23日继续审理，最终于10月25日结案，所有被告均被宣判无罪。同时，被告对 Morison 提出的反诉诬告罪也被驳回。
据我方掌握的信息，Morison 在9月7日至10月25日期间，就苏联政府机构在中国的政治活动问题，向中国军事当局作了两次陈述（附录“D”和“E”）。

pages.en:
-6-
This he did in order to ensure what he termed "an
impartial trial" of his case against the Centrosojus, as he
was under the impression that certain Chinese officials had
fallen under the influence of that concern.
Another item of interest relating to the same period
is the incident which occurred shortly after midnight of
October 19-20, when some mysterious person, alleged to be a
Russian, penetrated into the room occupied by the Morison
couple at No.362 Avenue du Roi Albert. On being discovered
the intruder made good his escape, several revolver shots
fired at him by Morison having missed their target. According
to Morison, it was an attempt on the part of the local Soviet
agents either to assassinate him or to steal certain documents
compromising the Centrosojus.
Morison filed an appeal against the judgment of the
Shanghai Special District Court above referred to. The
hearing of the appeal commenced in the Second Branch Kiangsu
High Court on November 27 and was continued on December 8,
after which it was for various reasons adjourned for indefinite
periods on several occasions. It was during this period that
information was received indicating the existence of secret
negotiations between Morison and representatives of the
Centrosojus with a view to the settling of the matter outside
the court. Apparently, these negotiations resulted in an
agreement having been reached and, consequently, Morison
withdrew his appeal.
Although no details of this agreement are available,
it is understood that on the condition that Morison would
withdraw his appeal and abstain from creating further troubles
to the Centrosojus, he was promised to be paid a certain sum.
There are good reasons to believe that Morison's
decision to sever his connections with the Centrosojus was an
outcome of a series of quarrels between him and his former
colleagues over money "earned" by them on certain business
pages.zh:
-6-
他这样做是为了确保他所称的针对苏联消费合作总社（Centrosojus）一案的“公正审判”，因为他认为某些中国官员已受到该机构的影响。

同一时期另一件值得关注的事项是10月19日至20日午夜过后不久发生的事件，当时一名据称为俄罗斯人的神秘人物潜入了居住在阿尔伯特国王路（Avenue du Roi Albert）362号的莫里森（Morison）夫妇的房间。入侵者被发现后成功逃脱，莫里森向其开枪数发，但均未击中。据莫里森称，这是当地苏维埃特工企图暗杀他，或窃取某些使苏联消费合作总社陷入困境的文件。

莫里森就上述上海特区地方法院的判决提出了上诉。上诉听证于11月27日在江苏高等法院第二分院开始，并于12月8日继续审理，此后因各种原因多次无限期休庭。在此期间，收到情报显示莫里森与苏联消费合作总社代表之间存在秘密谈判，旨在庭外解决此事。显然，这些谈判达成了协议，因此莫里森撤回了上诉。

虽然无法获得该协议的细节，但据悉，条件是莫里森撤回上诉并停止给苏联消费合作总社制造进一步麻烦，作为交换，承诺向他支付一定款项。

有充分理由相信，莫里森决定切断与苏联消费合作总社的联系，是他与前同事之间因他们在某些商业

pages.en:
-7-
transactions. There also seems to be very little room for
doubt that throughout the whole period of his controversies
with the Centrosojus Morison has been guided exclusively by
motives of personal interest, which have nothing to do with
his alleged disillusionment in the Communist doctrine.
As it was already mentioned, Morison at various times
during the period from June 15 to October 20, 1933 made
altogether five statements:- two to the Municipal Police, one
to the press and two to the Chinese Military Authorities. The
statement to the press (Appendix "C") is, perhaps, of more
interest than the remaining four, insofar as it includes the
main points contained in his other statements and also because
it may be assumed that while openly making serious allegations
regarding the subversive political activities of the employees
of the local branch of the Centrosojus, Morison was prepared
to take full responsibility for his words.
These allegations are, briefly, as follows :-
1.- The firm "Centrosojus, Ltd." is only a mask under which
communist party disguises its activities. The majority
of the employees of the local branch of the Centrosojus
were appointed by the Bureau of Foreign Communist Cells,
Moscow, directly subordinated to the Central Committee of
the Communist Party. They are selected from among trusted
members of the Communist Party, the commercial qualifications
being of no importance. In addition to their legitimate
occupation the majority of the employees of the Centrosojus
are engaged in secret political work in China on behalf of
the communist party.
2.- Centrosojus supplied funds to the Chinese Red Armies in
1933.
3.- Plans for "removal" (assassination) of Mr. Wang Ching Wei
and Mr. A.T. Belchenko (former Russian Consul in Hankow)
were in preparation under instructions from Markoff and
Babitch in 1932-1933.
pages.zh:
-7-
交易中“赚取”的钱款而发生的一系列争吵的结果。此外，几乎毫无疑问的是，在他与苏联消费合作总社争执的整个期间，莫里森完全受个人利益动机的驱使，这与他声称的对共产主义学说感到幻灭毫无关系。

如前所述，莫里森在1933年6月15日至10月20日期间共发表了五次声明：两次向工部局警务处发表，一次向新闻界发表，两次向中国军方当局发表。向新闻界发表的声明（附录“C”）可能比其余四次更令人关注，因为它包含了他其他声明中的主要要点，而且可以假定，莫里森在公开对苏联消费合作总社当地分支机构员工的颠覆性政治活动提出严重指控时，准备对自己的言论承担全部责任。

这些指控简述如下：

1. “苏联消费合作总社有限公司”（Centrosojus, Ltd.）只是共产党掩盖其活动的幌子。苏联消费合作总社当地分支机构的大部分员工是由莫斯科外国共产党细胞局直接任命的，该局隶属于共产党中央委员会。他们是从值得信赖的共产党员中挑选出来的，商业资格并不重要。除了合法职业外，苏联消费合作总社的大部分员工还代表共产党在中国从事秘密政治工作。

2. 苏联消费合作总社在1933年向中国红军提供资金。

3. 1932年至1933年间，根据马尔科夫（Markoff）和巴比奇（Babitch）的指示，正在策划“清除”（暗杀）汪精卫先生和前俄国驻汉口领事A.T.贝尔琴科（A.T. Belchenko）先生的计划。

pages.en:
-8-

4.- Communist literature in Chinese was brought in Shanghai
from the U.S.S.R. in the Soviet steamer "Nevastroy" in
April 1933.

It is very significant that no action was taken against
Morison by representatives of the Centrosojus in connection with
the above allegations.

Mrs Morison's statement to the press (Appendix "B") is
also not without interest as it describes the inner life of
the local Soviet "ghetto" in 1932-1933, where mutual fear,
suspicion and espionage prevailed and the possibility was
abhorred to be ordered to return into the Soviet paradise.
pages.zh:
-8-

4. 1933年4月，中文共产主义文献通过苏联轮船“涅瓦斯特罗伊”号（Nevastroy）从苏联运抵上海。

值得注意的是，苏联消费合作总社代表并未因上述指控对莫里森采取任何行动。

莫里森夫人向新闻界发表的声明（附录“B”）也颇有意思，因为它描述了1932年至1933年间当地苏维埃“隔都”的内部生活，那里弥漫着相互恐惧、猜疑和间谍活动，人们极度害怕被命令返回苏维埃天堂。

APPENDIX * *
Translation of V.A. Morison's first statement to the Chinese
Military Authorities.
-------------
Resolution of the Plenary Session of the Central Committee of
the Russian Communist Party, held in December 1932 - January
1933, on reports of Comrades Manuilsky and Bluhar on the
Chinese question.
(Resolution was subsequently approved by the Politbureau).

"The Chinese Section of the Comintern should pay special
attention to the directing of activities of the Chinese Red
Armies and to the rendering material and financial aid to them,
especially to the strengthening of the Chinese Red Armies by
providing them with a new and reliable commanding staff and
political instructors. At the same time a series of reforms
should be carried out in the Soviet Districts of China with
the aim of improving the living conditions of the proletarian
and toiling elements. This will not only strengthen the ideas
underlying the existence of the Soviet Districts, but also will
facilitate the spreading of these ideas in non-Soviet districts,
mainly in the direction towards the industrial regions of China.

The realisation of this aim is necessary for the
increase of the strength of the Chinese Red Armies - the future
reserves in the struggle against the aggressive plans of Japan,
with her imperialist tendencies of expansion in China and of
provoking an armed conflict with the U.S.S.R. This means that
at the present stage of Japan's aggressive policy the Chinese
Red Armies must not only exercise their influence in China, but
also must defend the U.S.S.R. In the event of an armed conflict
between Japan and U.S.S.R. the Chinese Red Armies should be
ready to be transferred into the rear of the Japanese zone of
military occupation in China.

In view of the above the Plenary Session of the Central
Committee decided :-
A.- To call from the Chinese Red Armies certain agents of the
Comintern whose work has proved to be unsatisfactory; to
delegate new, carefully selected workers having good
experience in military and political affairs.

V.A.莫里森向中国军方当局所作第一次声明的译文。
-------------
1932年12月至1933年1月举行的俄国共产党中央委员会全体会议关于马努伊尔斯基（Manuilsky）和布卢哈尔（Bluhar）同志关于中国问题的报告的决议。
（该决议随后经政治局批准）。

“共产国际中国部应特别注意指导中国红军的活动，并向其提供物质和财政援助，特别是通过提供新的且可靠的指挥 staff 和政治指导员来加强中国红军。同时，应在中国苏区进行一系列改革，旨在改善无产阶级和劳动群众的生活条件。这不仅将加强苏区存在的思想基础，还将促进这些思想在非苏区的传播，主要是向中国工业区方向传播。

实现这一目标对于增强中国红军的力量是必要的——中国红军是反对日本侵略计划（其在中国扩张的帝国主义倾向及挑起与苏联武装冲突）的未来后备力量。这意味着，在日本侵略政策的当前阶段，中国红军不仅必须在中国发挥影响力，还必须保卫苏联。一旦日本与苏联发生武装冲突，中国红军应准备好转移到日本在中国军事占领区的后方。

鉴于上述情况，中央委员会全体会议决定：
A. 召回共产国际在中国红军中工作证明不称职的某些特工；委派新的、经过仔细挑选且在军事和政治事务方面有良好经验的工作人员。

pages.en:
( 2 )

The Comintern is of the opinion that notwithstanding the
present conflict between the two countries, Japan and
China, both being Asiatic countries, will eventually come
to some agreement. Only the existence of strong Chinese
Red Armies can prevent such agreement and the possibility
of China siding with Japan in the event of an armed
conflict between that country and the U.S.S.R. The
success of the Red Movement in China will also stimulate
the revolutionary movement in all countries of the Far
East.

B.- In view of the present Sino-Japanese conflict, in which
China is the loser, slogans of the national defence against
the Japanese aggression should be temporarily adopted in
the Chinese Red Armies, and at the same time the struggle
against the Nanking Government as betraying the national
cause, should be intensified.

C.- To select the best students of the Oriental Institute and
to send them to the military schools for training, after
which they will be sent to the Soviet Districts of China.
This task to be carried out by Comrade Bluhor.

D.- To appoint 45 reliable members of the communist party who
have experience in the guerilla warfare: 20 from the
Moscow Military Academy and 25 capable and reliable workers
from the Special Department (Military Gendarmerie). Within
the period of 8 months these men have to receive training
and be organized in one group, following which they will
be secretly transferred to the Soviet and non-Soviet
districts of China. In addition, 6 military experts
selected on Comrade Bluhor's recommendation will be
despatched to China.

E.- To make Comrade Bluhor responsible for the supply of arms
and ammunition to the Chinese Red Armies. The arms
supplied should be of non-Russian make. At the same time
our Military Intelligence Service should investigate the
pages.zh:
( 2 )

共产国际认为，尽管中日两国目前存在冲突，但作为亚洲国家，日本和中国最终会达成某种协议。只有强大的中国红军才能防止这种协议，并防止在中日与苏联发生武装冲突时中国站在日本一边。中国红色运动的成功也将刺激远东所有国家的革命运动。

B. 鉴于当前的中日冲突中中国处于失利地位，中国红军应暂时采用抵御日本侵略的民族防御口号，同时应加剧反对南京政府背叛民族事业的斗争。

C. 挑选东方学院的最佳学生，送往军事学校受训，之后将他们派往中国苏区。此项任务由布卢霍尔（Bluhor）同志负责。

D. 任命45名有游击战经验的可靠共产党员：20名来自莫斯科军事学院，25名来自特别部（军事宪兵队）的能干且可靠的工作人员。这些人必须在8个月内接受训练并编为一个小组，随后将被秘密转移到中国的苏区和非苏区。此外，将根据布卢霍尔同志的推荐，派遣6名军事专家前往中国。

E. 由布卢霍尔同志负责向中国红军供应武器弹药。所供武器应为非俄制。同时，我军事情报部门应调查
