possibility of supplying to the Chinese Red Armies arms of
Russian make by agents of Japan and other foreign countries.
F.- The maximum of the credits required for 1933 to be fixed
by Comrades Bluhar and Grinko.*

In connection with paragraph "B" of the above
resolution the following may be mentioned :-

Towards the end of April 1933 handbills purporting
to have emanated from the "Association of Comrades in the North
East" were brought from Habarovsk not only into the Soviet
Districts of China but also to Tientsin and other districts.
These handbills were entitled "Traitors of the National China
in the Nanking Government" and a summary of their contents is
as follows :-

(a) Chiang Kai Shek, the leader of the Nationalist Government,
raided and plundered North China, killing defenceless
workers and peasants sympathising with the U.S.S.R.
Directed by Japan, he instigated Mukden to the conflict
with the U.S.S.R. in 1929. He was not satisfied with the
defeat of Mukden, but continued to assist the Japanese
invasion of China. During the recent Sino-Japanese conflict
in Manchuria he adopted the policy of non-interference in
Manchurian affairs, thus supporting Japan. After the loss
of the Three Eastern Provinces 350,000 of Mukden troops
were available, but he continued his policy of non-resistance
thus assisting Japan in the seizure of the Chinese territory.

(b) Chiang sent General Dai Hsia (?) to Japan in order to tell
the Japanese that they could go ahead with the occupation
of the Chinese territory; that in order to divert the
attention of the people from the Japanese action, he would
organize a front against the Reds. All this proves that he
is a traitor.

(c) If Chiang is not exterminated, this territory will not be
recovered and Japan will seize the whole of China. We must
pages.zh:
( 3 )

通过日本和其他外国代理人向中国红军供应俄制武器的可能性。
F. 1933年所需的最大信贷额度由布卢哈尔（Bluhar）和格林科（Grinko）*同志确定。

关于上述决议的“B”段，可提及以下内容：

1933年4月底，据称出自“东北同志协会”的传单从哈巴罗夫斯克（Habarovsk）不仅被带入中国苏区，还被带至天津及其他地区。这些传单的标题为《南京政府中的中国国家叛徒》，其内容摘要如下：

(a) 国民政府领袖蒋介石劫掠华北，杀害同情苏联的无辜工人和农民。他在日本的指使下，于1929年煽动沈阳（奉天）与苏联发生冲突。他对沈阳的失败并不满意，而是继续协助日本入侵中国。在最近的中国东北中日冲突中，他采取不干涉满洲事务的政策，从而支持日本。在丢失东北三省后，仍有35万沈阳部队可用，但他继续采取不抵抗政策，从而协助日本夺取中国领土。

(b) 蒋介石派遣戴夏（Dai Hsia，音译）将军前往日本，告知日本人他们可以继续占领中国领土；为了转移民众对日本行动的注意力，他将组织一条反红战线。这一切证明他是叛徒。

(c) 如果不消灭蒋介石，这片领土就无法收复，日本将占领整个中国。我们必须

pages.en:
( 4 )

rise against the Nanking traitors and against Japan and
punish the traitors with death.

The above mentioned handbills were brought to Shanghai
and Tientsin in a Norwegian boat chartered by the U.S.S.R. and
also in goods imported via Mongolia.

Simultaneously, an intensive work is being carried out
in the Chinese Red Armies under the direction of a number of
political instructors who arrived from the U.S.S.R.

In connection with paragraph "C" it is of interest to
note that the institutions for training of commanding and
political staff for the Chinese Red Armies include :-
(a) Institute for Oriental Peoples, Moscow.
(b) Parimonov's Eastern Institute, Moscow.
(c) Central Committee of the Communist Party's School for
Training Secretaries, Moscow. Prepares secretaries for
communist cells in the Chinese Red Armies and Soviet
Districts of China.
(d) Special Chinese Section for training of highly qualified
workers for the Chinese Communist Party. Attached to the
Institute of the Red Professional Unions.

The yearly "output" from these and other schools is
about 400 men. About 65% of the Chinese students are then
sent to various military schools (infantry, cavalry, artillery,
etc) for training, after which they are despatched to China
through the Bureau of Foreign Cells of the Central Committee.
Chinese students receiving training in the schools of the C.P.U.
proceed to China independently through the organisations of the
Foreign Service.

Apart from the above mentioned schools there are
several more in Habarovsk, Blagoveschensk and Vladivostock.
About 350 students received training in the agitation and
propaganda work at these schools during 1932, after which they
were smuggled into Manchuria.

起来反对南京叛徒和日本，并以死刑惩罚叛徒。

上述传单是通过苏联租用的挪威船只以及经由蒙古进口的货物运至上海和天津的。

与此同时，在若干名从苏联抵达的政治指导员的指导下，中国红军内部正在进行密集的工作。

关于决议的“C”段，值得注意的是，为中国红军培训指挥和政治工作人员的机构包括：
(a) 莫斯科东方劳动者共产主义大学（Institute for Oriental Peoples）。
(b) 莫斯科帕里莫诺夫东方学院（Parimonov's Eastern Institute）。
(c) 莫斯科共产党中央委员会秘书培训学校。为中国红军和中国苏区的共产党细胞培养秘书。
(d) 为中国共产党培养高素质工作人员的特别中国部。附属于红色工会国际学院。

这些学校及其他学校的年“产出”约为400人。约65%的中国学生随后被送往各种军事学校（步兵、骑兵、炮兵等）受训，之后通过中央委员会外国细胞局被派往中国。在联共（布）学校受训的中国学生则通过外事组织独立前往中国。

除上述学校外，在哈巴罗夫斯克、布拉戈维申斯克（Blagoveschensk）和符拉迪沃斯托克（Vladivostock）还有几所学校。1932年，约有350名学生在这几所学校接受了宣传鼓动工作的培训，随后被偷运进入满洲。

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Saturday, July 1, 1933

The Morrison Case
To the Editor.
As one amongst those present yes-
terday at the trial of Morrison (a
Russian), accused by his former
firm Centrosoyous of appropriating
$25,000.00, I was perplexed by one
detail
How and why should it be that
this purely Soviet firm bearing a
Russian name, with a whole So-
viet staff, acting under directions
and instructions from Moscow...is
registered as a British Firm with
its head office stated in London?
Morrison, who previously changed
his Soviet's passport for a Rus-
sian Emigrant's passport, himself
surrendered to the police, after the
charge was brought up against him.
He affirmed that the Charge was a
frame up as political vengeance re-
sulting from his refusal to proceed
to Moscow, where he was recalled,
and where, he felt sure, his life
would have been in danger.

The representatives of this
"British" firm blundered in the
court, giving contradictory testi-
mony, so that at last they were
reminded by the judge that they
had to speak the truth or other-
wise they would be prosecuted
themselves for giving false testi-
mony.
It seems that the Britishers had
ample opportunity to realize for
themselves the ways and methods
of the Soviet's so-called "Com-
mercial" firm, in which politics is
not only interwoven with com-
merce, but predominating it. One
has only to remember the grue-
some trial of British Engineers in
Moscow and the scandal around the
"Commercial" Arcos House in
London, which proved to be a
purely political (Communist)
organization.
One only can wonder how after
such experience, the Soviets are
permitted to work under British
cover and protection.
In the interest of our city and
the British local community is it
not a case for them to look into?
ANOTHER OBSERVER.
Shanghai, June 30, 1933.

《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1933年7月1日，星期六

莫里森案
致编辑：

作为昨日出席莫里森（一名俄国人）审判的在场者之一，莫里森被其前雇主“全苏消费合作社中央联社”（Centrosoyous）指控侵吞25,000.00美元，我对其中一个细节感到困惑：

为何这家纯粹的苏维埃企业，拥有俄罗斯名称，全体员工均为苏维埃人员，并在莫斯科的指示和指令下行动……却注册为一家英国公司，且总部设在伦敦？

莫里森此前将其苏维埃护照更换为俄国流亡者护照，在被指控后主动向警方投案。他声称该指控是出于政治报复的构陷，起因是他拒绝前往莫斯科应召回国，而他确信若前往那里，他的生命将面临危险。

这家“英国”公司的代表在法庭上失误连连，提供相互矛盾的证词，以至于法官最后提醒他们必须如实陈述，否则他们将因作伪证而受到起诉。

看来，英国人有充分的机会亲自了解苏维埃所谓“商业”机构的手段和方法，在这些机构中，政治不仅与商业交织在一起，而且占据主导地位。人们只需回想一下英国工程师在莫斯科受到的可怕审判，以及围绕伦敦“阿尔科斯商行”（Arcos House）的丑闻，后者被证明是一个纯粹的政治（共产主义）组织。

人们不禁要问，在有了这样的经历之后，为何还允许苏维埃人员在英国的掩护和保护下活动。

为了本市及英国侨民社区的利益，这难道不是他们应当调查的案件吗？

另一位观察者
上海，1933年6月30日

（批：6843）
（手写签名：档案 1933年7月）

July 12, 1933.

It has been learned from the Police Authorities
of the French Concession that one Leon Manevitch, an
official of the Vneshtorg (U.S.S.R. Foreign Commerce)
has arrived in Shanghai from Moscow. It is reported
that Manevitch was formerly the immediate superior of
V.D. Morrison, ex-employee of the Centrosojuz who was
recently charged with embezzlement and acquitted, and
was responsible for the recommendation which resulted
in Morrison being sent to China. It is believed
Manevitch has come to Shanghai to persuade Morrison
to return to U.S.S.R. in order to clear himself,
as Manevitch will be held responsible if Morrison
acts otherwise.

Translation of V.A. Morison's letter to the Editor of the
"Shanghai Zaria" and other local newspapers (21.8.33).

Sir,

Local newspapers have recently published interview with
Mr. Markoff concerning "the great commission organisation functioning
quitely, efficiently in promoting the exchange of products between
China and Russia, Messers Centrosoyus", of which Mr. Markoff is local
manager. ("Centrosoyus" means : Central Union of the Russian Coope-
rative Societies"). Mr. Markoff further says about "a beneficial work,
which is being accomplished by "Messrs Centrosoyus" to Great Britain
and China.

I should be much obliged if you will kindly permit me,
through the columns of your esteemed paper, to rectify, on the one
hand, numerous misleading statements contained in the above interview
and, on the other, to give your readers some facts, which may throw
quite a different light on the activities of this institution in
China and elsewhere, the facts which Mr. Markoff is anxious to keep un-
der silence. To this I may add that I am in a position to have an inti-
mate knowledge about the management of this company as only recently
I have been member of its staff as director of one of its departments.

"From its inception the aim of Centrosoyus, according to
Mr. Markoff, was the promotion of trade. The firm represents on a pu-
rely commission basis the Russian trusts of the Soviet Government".
Purely commission concern, quite clear. Russian Trusts send goods.
Centrosoyus sells them, draws commission, and that is all. Centrosoyus,
if only to believe Mr. Markoff, has nothing to do with Soviet Government
political aims or activities. The main object of the Shanghai Branch
continued Markoff, is "furtherance of trade and the strengthening
of commercial ties between the USSR and China".

Then Mr. Markoff gives what he thinks is undeniable proof
that their endeavours in that direction were crowned with a success;
pages.zh:
V.A.莫里森致《上海霞光报》及其他当地报纸编辑的信的译文（1933年8月21日）。

先生，

当地报纸最近刊登了对马尔科夫先生（Mr. Markoff）的采访，内容涉及“一个在促进中俄产品交换方面安静、高效运作的大型佣金组织，即‘全苏消费合作社中央联社’先生们”（Messers Centrosoyus），马尔科夫先生是该组织的本地经理。（“Centrosoyus”意为：俄罗斯合作社中央联盟）。马尔科夫先生进一步谈到“‘全苏消费合作社中央联社’先生们”为大英帝国和中国所做的“有益工作”。

如果您能允许我通过贵报的专栏，一方面纠正上述采访中包含的许多误导性陈述，另一方面向您的读者提供一些事实，从而以截然不同的视角揭示该机构在中国及其他地方的活动——这些事实是马尔科夫先生急于保持沉默的——我将不胜感激。此外，我可以补充说，我有能力深入了解该公司的管理情况，因为就在不久前，我还担任其员工，任其中一个部门的主任。

“据马尔科夫先生称，‘全苏消费合作社中央联社’自成立之初的目标就是促进贸易。该公司以纯佣金方式代表苏联政府的俄罗斯托拉斯。”纯佣金业务，非常清楚。俄罗斯托拉斯发送货物。“全苏消费合作社中央联社”出售货物，抽取佣金，仅此而已。如果只相信马尔科夫先生的话，“全苏消费合作社中央联社”与苏联政府的政治目标或活动毫无关系。马尔科夫接着说，上海分部的主要目标是“促进贸易并加强苏联与中国之间的商业联系”。

随后，马尔科夫先生给出了他认为无可辩驳的证据，证明他们在这方面的努力取得了成功；

pages.en:
This success the representative of the Russian Cooperative Societies
sees in the fact that "the trade balance between China and Soviet Russia,
two of the largest consumer countries in the world, has been for the
last decade much in favour of.......China". Of course Mr.Markoff is at
liberty to see Russian profit there, where other persons, not proletarian
minded, would find a loss; it is a matter of opinion, so I would
have no objections to this, provided his conclusion were based on the
facts. But it is here that I am going to have a quarrel with Mr.Markoff.
In order to give some idea of the amount of the favourable balance
for China, Markoff sets forth a table showing an excess of Chinese export
over import for the last five years(1928-1932). This table, which would
make Cheshire cat laugh, is characteristic of the psychology of the
soviet people and utmost contempt with which they treat public reading
newspapers. The returns shown by Markoff were, according to his state-
ment, taken from the "Chinese Economic Journal". I do not know whether
the above journal has ever published such returns, or where they
were taken from. But the main point is not there. Why it is that Markoff
looks into Chinese Journal for the information, which contained in
the files of his own office? Would it not be far more convenient,
and convincing too, to publish his own accounts, duly audited by char-
tered accountants (is not it British firm)? I will answer this
question : because the files would say quite a different story from that
told by Markoff. I am in a position, as former manager of one of the
Sovtorgsnyus departments, to state that not only there was no favourable
balance for China, but, on the contrary, soviet import into China is a
real dumping, hundred times exceeding the export from this country.
Let us examine the soviet trade plan with China for the
current year, which is on the way of realisation. It was planned by
soviet government to import into China :

| Item | Amount |
| :--- | :--- |
| Timber | 11,000,000 |
| Cotton goods | 4,000,000 |
| Chemicals, construction materials, cement, glass, | 5,000,000 |
| Fish | 3,000,000 |
| Furs, medicine, wines fruits etc. | 2,000,000 |
| **TOTAL** | **25,000,000** |

This is import. Export of tea from China (the only item of ex
pages.zh:
这位俄罗斯合作社的代表认为，这一成功体现在“中国与苏维埃俄罗斯这两个世界上最大的消费国之间的贸易平衡，在过去十年里极大地有利于……中国”。当然，马尔科夫先生有权在其他非无产阶级思维的人会发现亏损的地方看到俄罗斯的利润；这是一个观点问题，因此只要他的结论基于事实，我对此没有异议。但正是在这里，我要与马尔科夫先生争论。为了让人了解对中国有利的顺差数额，马尔科夫列出了一张表格，显示过去五年（1928-1932年）中国出口超过进口的差额。这张能让柴郡猫发笑的表格，典型地反映了苏维埃人的心理以及他们对公众阅读报纸的极度蔑视。据马尔科夫称，表中数据取自《中国经济杂志》（Chinese Economic Journal）。我不知道上述杂志是否曾发布过此类数据，或者这些数据是从哪里获取的。但重点不在于此。为什么马尔科夫要从中国杂志中寻找他自己办公室档案中就包含的信息呢？公布由特许会计师审计过的自家账目（这不是一家英国公司吗？）难道不是更方便、也更具说服力吗？我来回答这个问题：因为档案所讲述的故事与马尔科夫所说的截然不同。作为前苏联贸易机构（Sovtorgsnyus）部门经理之一，我有资格声明，不仅不存在对中国的贸易顺差，相反，苏联对中国的进口是真正的倾销，其规模超过该国出口的一百倍。让我们审视一下正在实施中的本年度苏联对华贸易计划。苏联政府计划向中国进口：

| 项目 | 金额 |
| :--- | :--- |
| 木材 | 11,000,000 |
| 棉织品 | 4,000,000 |
| 化学品、建筑材料、水泥、玻璃 | 5,000,000 |
| 鱼类 | 3,000,000 |
| 皮草、药品、酒类、水果等 | 2,000,000 |
| **总计** | **25,000,000** |

这是进口额。据马尔科夫称，从中国出口的茶叶（来自该国的唯一出口项目）

pages.en:
from this country) according to Markoff's statement, has dropped to
3.187.840 for 1932. Returns of 1933 are even below this figure
for 35%. Then where is the balance favourable for China ? How serious
is soviet dumping in China may be judged by the fact that Chinese Ce-
ment Production Association has recently sent, through Chinese Ambas-
sador in Moscow, a protest against soviet dumping, menacing their
trade and which would force them to close their business.

"Messrs Centrosoyuz" is a British firm and probably that is
why they are trying to undermine a British firm Brunner and Mond by
systematically lowering prices for Caustic Soda and Ash Soda, imported
by this firm. It was even planned first to kill, with the assistance
of Brunner and Mond, Chinese soda manufacture at Tientsin and then under-
mine Brunner and Mond. This plan was worked out by Markoff and Rabitch
and in its realisation I should have participated.

However the importance of the interview, granted by Markoff,
lies not in the commercial activities of his office only; two points
are being stressed by Markoff : that Centrosoyuz is a British firm, on
the one hand, and that it is "purely commercial organisation having
no political function of any whatsoever".

Now, Centrosoyuz was registered in London under the Joint Stock
Companies Trade Act. Therefore in spite the possibility of Soviet link.
This constantly must be kept in mind because by this fact British Ad-
ministration is, to some extent, responsible for the activities of the
company protected by them. As to the point "purely commercial enter-
prise", this I will most emphatically deny. In order to prove the
contrary allow me to remind Markoff certain facts, well known both
to him and to me.

1.) All members of Centrosoyuz staff in Shanghai and Tientsin
selected and appointed by Moscow. Shanghai Branch appoints employees
for Tientsin and Dairen branches on the recommendation of Moscow and
with the approval of the Bureau of Foreign Commercial Affairs (directly
subordinated to C.C. of the Communist Party) and of Foreign Intelligence
Section. Qualifications, to which every candidate should comply, are:
a) thorough knowledge of the conditions of Trade in China; b) ability
pages.zh:
在1932年已降至3,187,840。1933年的数据甚至比这一数字低了35%。那么，有利于中国的贸易平衡在哪里呢？苏联在华倾销的严重程度，可以从中国水泥生产协会最近通过中国驻莫斯科大使提出抗议一事中看出，抗议针对的是威胁其贸易并迫使其关闭业务的苏联倾销行为。

“全苏消费合作社中央联社”先生们（Messrs Centrosoyuz）是一家英国公司，这可能就是为什么他们试图通过系统地降低由卜内门公司（Brunner and Mond）进口的烧碱和纯碱的价格，来削弱这家英国公司。甚至最初计划是在卜内门公司的协助下，先扼杀天津的中国苏打制造业，然后再削弱卜内门公司。该计划由马尔科夫和拉比奇（Rabitch）制定，而我本应参与其实施。

然而，马尔科夫接受的采访的重要性不仅在于其办公室的商业活动；马尔科夫强调了两点：一方面，“全苏消费合作社中央联社”是一家英国公司，另一方面，它是“纯粹的商业组织，没有任何政治职能”。

现在，“全苏消费合作社中央联社”是根据《股份公司法》在伦敦注册的。因此，尽管存在与苏联联系的可能性。这一点必须时刻牢记，因为凭借这一事实，英国行政当局在某种程度上要对受其保护的公司的活动负责。至于“纯粹商业企业”这一点，我将最坚决地予以否认。为了证明相反的情况，请允许我向马尔科夫提醒某些他和我都熟知的事实。

1.) “全苏消费合作社中央联社”在上海和天津的所有员工均由莫斯科选拔和任命。上海分部根据莫斯科的推荐，并经对外商业事务局（直接隶属于共产党中央委员会）和对外情报处的批准，为天津和大连分部任命员工。每位候选人应符合的资格条件是：a)  thoroughly knowledge of the conditions of Trade in China（彻底了解中国的贸易状况）；b) ability（能力）

pages.en:
commercial training, or knowledge of things Chinese, as one could
reasonably expect. No, every candidate should previously distinguish
himself in other soviet administrative departments, having nothing to do
with commerce, mostly as members or G.P.U. or by having participated
in punitive expeditions. Commercial qualifications are of secondary im-
portance, or rather of no importance at all. It this way were appointed:
you, Mr. Markoff, Babitch, Yakimenko, Mihailoff, Zaneguine, Sereguine, Mrs.
Moiseeva, Kozloff, Usmanoff, Tselyhnoﬀ and others. I should be glad also
to refresh in Markoﬀ's memory respective qualiﬁcations of the above
"commercial" agents:

a) I.N.Babitch is member of the Communist Party since 1918. From
1919 to 1925 he served in diﬀerent sections of Cheka and G.P.U. From
1925 to 1930 Babitch was attached to Foreign Espionage Section of the
commissariat of foreign aﬀairs. Probably Babitch can tell you, Mr.Markoﬀ
how many Chinese residents in Moscow and other places were arrested by
Babitch and ordered by him to be shot during the period of Sino-Soviet
conﬂict of 1929, if he had only kept record of them? Anyway there is
no doubt it is only owing to these qualiﬁcations and particularly his
expert knowledge how to fabricate forged passports and signatures that he
was appointed assistant manager of the Shanghai Branch of Centrosoyus.

b) N.F. Mihailoﬀ was investigator and night commandant of G.P.U.
Later on he directed espionage section in Asia, is member of the communist
party. In Shanghai he is disguised as cotton goods expert.

c) Zaneguin distinguished himself by suppressing counter revolution
in Ivanovo-Vosnessensk region; disguised also as cotton goods specialist.

d) Yakimenko. Organiser of communist youths in Petrograd. Served
in a Special Branch of G.P.U. In Shanghai is disguised as expert in
timber trade. In order to make Shanghai business people believe in his
knowledge of timber trade, the soviet government supplied him with a
document, signed by Director of Forest Institute in Moscow, certifying that
Yakimenko was graduated by that Institute. Yakimenko told me once, that
if necessary, he can have a certiﬁcate of engineer constructor, or
that of mechanician. "With such a timber expert one can easily sell all
pages.zh:
商业训练，或是对中国事务的了解，达到人们可以合理预期的程度。不，每一位候选人都应此前在其他苏联行政部门中表现出色，这些部门与商业毫无关系，大多是作为契卡（Cheka）或国家政治保卫局（G.P.U.）的成员，或是通过参与惩罚性远征行动。商业资格是次要的，或者更确切地说，根本无关紧要。以此方式任命的有：你，马尔科夫先生（Mr. Markoff），巴比奇（Babitch），亚基缅科（Yakimenko），米哈伊洛夫（Mihailoff），扎涅金（Zaneguine），谢列金（Sereguine），莫伊谢耶娃女士（Mrs. Moiseeva），科兹洛夫（Kozloff），乌斯马诺夫（Usmanoff），采利赫诺夫（Tselyhnoﬀ）等人。我也很乐意让马尔科夫回忆一下上述“商业”特工的相关资历：

a) I.N.巴比奇自1918年起即为共产党员。从1919年到1925年，他在契卡和国家政治保卫局的各个部门服役。从1925年到1930年，巴比奇隶属于外交部外国间谍处。也许巴比奇能告诉你，马尔科夫先生，在1929年中苏冲突期间，如果他有记录的话，有多少居住在莫斯科和其他地方的中国人被巴比奇逮捕并下令枪决？无论如何，毫无疑问，正是凭借这些资历，特别是他伪造护照和签名的专业知识，他才被任命为苏联消费合作总社（Centrosoyus）上海分社的副经理。

b) N.F.米哈伊洛夫曾是国家政治保卫局的调查员和夜间指挥官。后来他主管亚洲地区的间谍部门，是共产党员。在上海，他伪装成棉纺织品专家。

c) 扎涅金因镇压伊万诺沃-沃兹涅先斯克地区（Ivanovo-Vosnessensk）的反革命活动而崭露头角；同样伪装成棉纺织品专家。

d) 亚基缅科。彼得格勒共产主义青年团组织者。曾在国家政治保卫局特别处服役。在上海，他伪装成木材贸易专家。为了让上海商界人士相信他的木材贸易知识，苏联政府向他提供了一份由莫斯科林业学院院长签署的文件，证明亚基缅科毕业于该学院。亚基缅科曾告诉我，如有必要，他可以弄到工程师或机械师的证书。“有了这样的木材专家，人们可以轻易地以250美元的价格卖掉所有的

pages.en:
Siberian forests for $ 250" once said about him Sorebreff, manager
of the Lumber Department.
e) Kozloff was graduated by Moscow Oriental Communistic Institute.
Shortly after his arrival in Shanghai Centrosoyus was benefited by
special Economic Bureau.
The same may be said about other members of Centrosoyus staff.They
were sent here not to carry on honest trade, but to do secret
political and spying work, of which they are experts.
Now a few words about Markoff's contention that Centrosoyus is
"purely commercial concern and is not engaged in politics."
1) Could not Mr. Markoff tell us something about the special
mission of comrade Mikhailoff when he early in April last went to
Tientsin, carrying with him U.$35.000 ? Were not these money
destined to two Chinese gentlemen who were waiting for him? If
Markoff forgot it then I would call to his mind that Mikhailoff, on
his return from Tientsin, made detailed report about that mission
to a special committee ("Fighting team of three") consisting of his
Superior and me. It was to the effect that the Chinese red army
is successfully advancing and That Army was to be taken shortly.
2) Could not Markoff inform us, what was the real object of his
voyage to Hankow, at the end of March last, made by request of he
has a short memory, then I will remind him was it not to make out
some plan for the "removal" of Mr. Borodin, if he refuses to
cooperate with Soviet government? Surely "commercial" enterprise,
was not it?
3) Then Mr. Markoff must remember, or I shall be obliged to remind
that he is a man of exceptionally short memory, that when he and
Zaitch reprimanded me for my refusal to organize the "expedition"
to translate this soviet jargon into a common language - to
assassinate Mr. Tang Ching Wei, the chairman of the Chinese Govern-
ment, who is being regarded as strongest opponent to sovietism, and
Zaitch put it-worse than General Chiang Kai Shek himself, all what
kind of reports were sent about me for not having executed this
order?
pages.zh:
西伯利亚森林”，木材部经理索布雷夫（Sorebreff）曾这样评价他。
e) 科兹洛夫毕业于莫斯科东方共产主义劳动者大学。他抵达上海后不久，苏联消费合作总社便受益于一个专门的经济局。
苏联消费合作总社的其他职员情况也是如此。他们被派到这里不是为了进行诚实的贸易，而是从事秘密的政治和间谍工作，对此他们是专家。
现在谈谈马尔科夫关于苏联消费合作总社是“纯粹的商业机构，不参与政治”的说法。
1) 马尔科夫先生能否告诉我们，去年4月初，米哈伊洛夫同志携带35,000美元前往天津时的特殊使命是什么？这笔钱难道不是 destined for 两位正在等候他的中国绅士吗？如果马尔科夫忘记了，我会提醒他，米哈伊洛夫从天津回来后，向一个特别委员会（“三人战斗小组”）详细报告了那次使命，该委员会由他的上级和我组成。报告大意是，中国红军正在顺利推进，该军队很快将被接管。
2) 马尔科夫能否告知我们，去年3月底他应要求前往汉口的真正目的是什么？如果他记性不好，我会提醒他，难道不是为了制定一项在鲍罗廷先生（Mr. Borodin）拒绝与苏联政府合作的情况下将其“清除”的计划吗？这确是“商业”行为，不是吗？
3) 那么，马尔科夫先生必须记住，否则我将不得不提醒他这个记性极差的人，当他及扎伊奇（Zaitch）因我拒绝组织“远征”——用通俗语言翻译这句苏联行话就是——刺杀被视为苏维埃主义最强对手的中国政府主席唐精卫先生（Mr. Tang Ching Wei，注：原文如此，疑指唐生智或其他人，但按指令保留原文音译或直译，此处Tang Ching Wei对应唐精卫/唐生智等，鉴于历史背景及Chiang Kai-shek对比，暂按字面译为唐精卫，或保留英文加注，依指令不确定保留原文加括号，此处Tang Ching Wei非常见标准译名，故处理为唐精卫(音译)），且扎伊奇称其比蒋介石将军本人更糟糕时，关于我未执行此命令发送了什么样的报告？

pages.en:
4) What preparations have been made by Babitch for the
"removal" of Greenfeld, if he refuses to return to Soviet Russia?
Markoff was well informed about these preparations after his
return from Russia, preparations, which, by the way, have been
worked out in cooperation with the legal adviser of this "purely
commercial" enterprise.

5) Does Markoff remember one nice cool evening in the second
part of April last, when we, that is Markoff, Zamaguin and I, made a
trip to soviet steamer "Novostroy" where we have examined communist
literature, brought by this steamer. Part of this "purely commercial
cargo" contained communist tracts in Chinese language; the other part
was to be sent to Cuba ( Oh, yes, the same Cuba.....). The steamer,
beside communist literature, brought to this port 4,500 tons of
cement and several thousand boxes of glass.

I could cite more facts about subversive activities of the
commercial enterprise directed by Markoff. As a reply to his
interview it is enough. Later on, I hope, I shall be able to give
more detailed outline of the activities of "Messrs. Centrosoyuz Ltd."
in China. -
pages.zh:
4) 如果格林菲尔德（Greenfeld）拒绝返回苏联俄罗斯，巴比奇为“清除”他做了哪些准备？马尔科夫从俄罗斯回来后对这些准备知之甚详，顺便说一句，这些准备是与这家“纯粹商业”企业的法律顾问合作制定的。

5) 马尔科夫是否记得去年四月下旬的一个凉爽宜人的夜晚，我们，即马尔科夫、扎马金（Zamaguin，注：前文为Zaneguine，此处拼写略有不同，依原文译）和我，乘坐苏联轮船“新建筑号”（Novostroy）进行了一次旅行，在那里我们检查了由该船运来的共产主义文献。这部分“纯粹商业货物”中包含中文版的共产主义小册子；另一部分则要送往古巴（哦，是的，就是那个古巴……）。除了共产主义文献外，该船还为本港带来了4,500吨水泥和数千箱玻璃。

我可以列举更多关于马尔科夫领导的这家商业企业颠覆活动的事实。作为对他访谈的回应，这些已经足够了。我希望以后能更详细地概述“苏联消费合作总社有限公司诸位先生”在中国的活动。 -

Translation of the leading article entitled "MASKS OFF!"
which appeared in the "KOPEIKA" of August 21, 1933.

Revelations contained in Morison's statement have
dealt a crushing blow to Red activities in China.
Morison's statement, every word of which, we presume, he
can prove at any time, has torn the mask off the
Centrosojus which, according to him, is the citadel of
communist propaganda and espionage.

By reading his letter with attention we gradually
become acquainted with the true nature of the Soviet
"Commercial" establishments and begin to understand
why the Comintern has succeeded in extending its
tentacles over the whole world.

Practically the whole apparatus of the U.S.S.R.
foreign representation is directed towards the object
of setting the whole world ablaze. We had known this
before Morison published his statement but only now has
this knowledge taken a concrete form locally.

Members of the staff of the Centrosojus, "a British
commission institution", are appointed by G.P.U.,
Razvedupr and C.P.R. - i.e. by the centre of political
intelligence, the centre of espionage and the party
fostering the world revolution respectively.

Naturally, the principles in accordance with which
members of the staff are selected are of a somewhat
special character : persons who received special
training in conducting subversive work fill the posts
of employees of a commercial institution.

In his letter Morison gives the details of the records
of service of his former colleagues. They are all
marked with blood, treachery and sound of the "music of
the Cheka whips".

According to Morison the employees of the

翻译1933年8月21日《KOPEIKA》报上发表的题为“摘下面具！”的社论。

莫里森声明中所包含的揭露内容，对在华红色活动造成了毁灭性打击。莫里森的声明，据我们推测，他随时可以证明其中的每一个字，已经撕下了苏联消费合作总社的面具，据他称，该社是共产主义宣传和间谍活动的堡垒。

通过仔细阅读他的信，我们逐渐了解了苏联“商业”机构的真实性质，并开始理解为什么共产国际能够将其触角延伸到全世界。

实际上，苏联对外代表机构的整个 apparatus 都旨在点燃整个世界。在莫里森发表声明之前我们就知道这一点，但直到最近，这一认识才在当地具体化。

苏联消费合作总社这家“英国佣金机构”的职员是由国家政治保卫局（G.P.U.）、军事情报局（Razvedupr）和共产党中央委员会（C.P.R.）任命的——即分别由政治情报中心、间谍中心和培育世界革命的政党任命。

自然，选拔职员的原则具有某种特殊性：接受过颠覆工作专门训练的人员担任商业机构员工的职位。

在他的信中，莫里森提供了他前同事的服务记录细节。他们都沾染着鲜血、背叛和“契卡鞭子的音乐声”。

根据莫里森的说法，

pages.en:
(2)

Centrosojus are trusted communist workers who have proved
their loyalty to the Soviet power by having committed
a series of crimes.

The Soviet government supplies with great care China
as well as far distant Cuba with propaganda matter,
preparing unexpected blows, fostering hatred and fratricidal
war.

The value of the statement in question is increased in
view of the fact that the blow it deals is very timely.
The whole activity of the Red underworld has been
denounced at the time when, in connection with the
staging of the Anti-Imperialist Conference, Red Moscow
expects maximum of energy and efforts on the part of its
agents.

To-day the Comintern has suffered a serious defeat.

Regarding the Centrosojus itself we must admit the
masterly work of the bolsheviks in camouflaging their
subversive activities. The true nature of the institutions
above referred to is hidden behind several covers. First
you see a solid British firm dealing in Soviet goods on
a commission basis; then the firm becomes a Soviet owned
one, all members of the staff being appointed from Moscow
and not from London; only by removing this latter cover
we understand the true nature of this organization, which,
Morison asserts, is not a commercial, not even a political
institution, but a branch of the Comintern functioning
under the British flag in the territory of the International
Settlement.

It is the task of the Russian emigrants to utilize
fully all the material contained in Morison's statement,
in order to know their enemy, as only the full knowledge
of one's enemy secures victory over him.
pages.zh:
(2)

苏联消费合作总社的员工是值得信赖的共产主义工作者，他们通过犯下一系列罪行证明了对苏维埃政权的忠诚。

苏联政府非常小心地向中国以及遥远的古巴提供宣传材料，策划意外打击，煽动仇恨和兄弟阋墙式的战争。

鉴于此次打击非常及时，该声明的价值得以增加。红色地下世界的所有活动都在此时被揭发，正值红色莫斯科因筹备反帝国主义会议而期望其代理人付出最大精力和努力之际。

今天，共产国际遭受了严重失败。

关于苏联消费合作总社本身，我们必须承认布尔什维克在伪装其颠覆活动方面的高超手段。上述机构的真实性质隐藏在几层掩护之下。首先，你看到的是一家稳固的英国公司，以佣金方式经营苏联商品；然后，该公司变成了一家苏联所有的公司，所有职员均由莫斯科而非伦敦任命；只有揭开这最后一层掩护，我们才能理解该组织的真实性质，莫里森断言，它不是一个商业机构，甚至不是一个政治机构，而是共产国际的一个分支，在国际租界领土上在英国国旗下运作。

充分利用莫里森声明中所包含的所有材料，以了解他们的敌人，这是俄国流亡者的任务，因为只有充分了解敌人才能确保战胜敌人。

pages.en:
(3)

However, revelations made by Morison, are not a
purely Russian emigrants affair. Foreigners are affected
in an equal degree. The statement is a sinister warning
to them.

Look : there, among yourselves, under the protection
of your laws and privileges and by utilising them against
you, a work has been conducted for the past ten years
directed towards the undermining of your own prosperity,
honour and life.

With a devilish cunning, shamelessness and cynicism
the agents of the Comintern are working against the whole
world preparing a most terrible disaster - the Bolshevist
world revolution.

Morison's letter is an indictment of the agents of
the Cominter in China. It is not a hint only or a half-
truth. Bets are placed over all "i"s. Masks have
been torn off. The curtain behind which the communist
kitchen was hidden, has been raised. It only remains to
draw the corresponding conclusion and to act ! This is
equally true in respect of both the Russian emigrants and
the foreign community.

（印：THE 48）
pages.zh:
(3)

然而，莫里森的揭露并非仅仅是俄国流亡者的事。外国人同样受到影响。该声明对他们是一个不祥的警告。

看吧：在你们中间，在你们的法律和特权保护下，并利用这些法律和特权来对付你们，过去十年一直进行着一项旨在破坏你们自身繁荣、荣誉和生命的工作。

共产国际的代理人怀着恶魔般的狡诈、无耻和犬儒主义，对抗整个世界，准备一场最可怕的灾难——布尔什维克世界革命。

莫里森的信是对在华共产国际代理人的指控。这不仅仅是一个暗示或半真半假的事实。所有的“i”上都加了点（意指细节确凿）。面具已被撕下。隐藏共产主义幕后操作的幕布已被升起。剩下的只是得出相应的结论并采取行动！这对俄国流亡者和外国侨民社区都同样适用。

（印：THE 48）

October 20, 1933.

Financial and Material Support for Chinese Red Armies.

The following is a translation of the second
report submitted by V.A. Morrison, a former employee of the
local Branch of Centrosojus, to the Chinese Military
authorities:-

In compliance with a decision of the Bureau of
Finance of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of
the U.S.S.R. made on October 26, 1931 on the subject of
work in foreign countries, all funds for the support of
communist organizations in countries of the Far East (China,
Japan and Korea) are to be transferred, nit by certain
trustworthy firms as had been done hitherto, but direct to
the representatives of the Chinese communist organizations.

This new system has been applied to China since
the end of 1932. The great lapse of time between the date
of the decision of the Central Committee of the Communist
Party of the U.S.S.R. and the date of its enforcement is due
to the fact that the Chinese communist organizations, such
as the Chinese Communist Party in the sovietized regions
have not been able to nominate, within the time designated,
the representatives to whom more or less large sums of
money might be entrusted. The delay in the selection of
representatives by the Chinese communist organizations
was due to the fact that the decision of the Bureau of
Finance of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of
the U.S.S.R. stipulates that all responsibility for the
remittance of funds to their destination shall fall
directly on the secretary-general of the Chinese Communist
Party. This condition is being insisted upon owing to
the fact that a certain sum of money destined for the
Japanese Communist Party and which was to have been remitted
by a trustworthy person----a Japanese---- had been

对中国红军的财政和物质支持。

以下是前苏联消费合作总社当地分公司雇员 V.A. 莫里森向中国军事当局提交的第二份报告的译文：-

根据1931年10月26日苏联共产党中央委员会财政局关于在国外工作的决定，所有用于支持远东国家（中国、日本和朝鲜）共产主义组织的资金，将不再像以前那样通过某些可信的公司转移，而是直接转给中国共产主义组织的代表。

这一新制度自1932年底起应用于中国。苏联共产党中央委员会作出决定的日期与其执行日期之间的巨大时间差，是由于中国的共产主义组织，如苏维埃化地区的中国共产党，未能在指定时间内提名可以托付或多或少大额资金的代表。中国共产主义组织在挑选代表方面的延误，是由于苏联共产党中央委员会财政局的决定规定，所有将资金汇至目的地的责任直接落在中国共产党总书记身上。坚持这一条件是因为，有一笔 destined for 日本共产党的款项，本应由一位可信人士——一名日本人——汇款，但该款项已被

pages.en:
- 2 -
misappropriated by the man who later sought refuge in the
Philippine Islands.
Early in the month of April, a sum made up of gold
$33.000, Mex. $45,000 and Yen 25,000 was remitted to the Chinese
Communist Party through the intermediary of N.F. Mikhailoff,
a representative of Centrosojus. The largest portion of this
money was destined for the "red" regions in China. N.F.
Mikhailoff proceeded to Tientsin early in April for this
purpose. The official object of his journey was to attend to
the sale of a stock of U.S.S.R. cotton thread. Shortly before
the voyage of Mikhailoff to Tientsin, a person named Sereguine,
manager of the Tientsin branch of Centrosojus, arrived in
Shanghai (February, 1933) to inform him that the representatives
of the Chinese soviet regions were expected at Tientsin early
in April. Another person named Saneguine, an employee of the
local branch of Centrosojus, was sent to Tientsin early in
April to secure information from the Chinese about the amount
they required. The object of his journey was at that time
stated to be the sale of U.S.S.R. textile products.
Upon his arrival in Shanghai, Sereguine, stated that
an interview could be arranged with the representatives of the
Chinese Communist Party at Tientsin in the premises of the
Chihli Trading Co., a firm which is working for the sale of
U.S.S.R. textile products, but after the journey to Tientsin,
it was found that an interview could be held only at the
office of the branch of Centrosojus. It was at this place
where Mikhailoff actually met the Chinese communists in
question and handed to them the amounts indicated above.
It is to be noted that in addition to the sums remitted to the
representatives of the Chinese Communist Party by Mikhailoff,
Saneguine also handed to them a sum of Mex. $33,000.
pages.zh:
- 2 -
被后来逃往菲律宾群岛避难的那人侵吞。

四月初，一笔由黄金33,000美元、墨西哥银元45,000元和日元25,000元组成的款项，通过苏联消费合作社中央联社（Centrosojus）代表N.F. Mikhailoff的中介，汇给了中国共产党。这笔钱的大部分是 destined for 中国的“红色”区域。为此目的，N.F. Mikhailoff于四月初前往天津。他此行的官方目的是处理一批苏联棉纱的销售事宜。在Mikhailoff启程前往天津前不久，Centrosojus天津分行经理Sereguine于1933年2月抵达上海，告知他中国苏维埃区域的代表预计将于四月初到达天津。另一名名为Saneguine的人，系Centrosojus本地分行的雇员，也于四月初被派往天津，以从中国人那里获取他们所需金额的信息。当时声称他此行的目的是销售苏联纺织品。

Sereguine抵达上海后称，可以在天津的直隶贸易公司（Chihli Trading Co.）安排与中国共产党代表的会面，该公司是一家从事苏联纺织品销售业务的公司；但在前往天津后发现，会面只能在Centrosojus分行的办公室举行。正是在这个地方，Mikhailoff实际上会见了上述中国共产党人，并将上述金额交给了他们。值得注意的是，除了Mikhailoff交给中国共产党代表的款项外，Saneguine还交给了他们墨西哥银元33,000元。

pages.en:
75% of the amounts handed to the Chinese by
Sanguine as well as by Mikhailoff consisted of forged
banknotes of the Bank of Communications. These banknotes
had been imported into Shanghai on board a soviet steamer
which arrived in Shanghai with a cargo of U.S.S.R. petroleum
in February, 1933.

It seems that Mikhailoff did not hand the full
amount of gold $38,000 to the representative of the Chinese
Communist Party because he did not want to arouse suspicion
through the appearance of such a large amount of American
dollars in the soviet regions. About gold $15,000 (all
counterfeit) were taken back to Shanghai by Mikhailoff and
handed to the deputy manager of the local branch of the
Dalbanque in the name of Tsalochhoff (Tseloukhoff).
This last named is the special agent for the distribution of
money destined for secret work in China. In 1932, this man
made a voyage to Moscow to formulate a plan for the
distribution of secret funds for the year 1933.

At about the same time, money was remitted to the
Central Committee of the Shanghai Branch of the Chinese
Communist Party. This took place not long after the
arrival in Shanghai of Waldmann, representative of the
Vneshtorg (foreign commerce of the U.S.S.R.) This
person was formerly a procurator of Moscow who is at present
directing, for the time being, the Japanese and Korean
Sections of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of
the U.S.S.R.

A conference, for this purpose, was held with a
representative of the local Branch of the Chinese Communist
Party (in March, 1933) in house No.47 Rue Amiral Courbert.
At this conference, were present M. Markoff, manager of the
local Branch of Centrosojus, Morrison (who was, at this time,
manager of the Chemical Department of this establishment),
pages.zh:
Sanguine以及Mikhailoff交给中国人的款项中，有75%是由交通银行伪造的钞票组成。这些钞票是1933年2月随一艘装载苏联石油抵达上海的苏联轮船运入上海的。

看来Mikhailoff并没有将全部38,000美元黄金交给中国共产党代表，因为他不想因在苏维埃区域出现如此大量的美元而引起怀疑。约15,000美元黄金（均为伪币）被Mikhailoff带回上海，并以Tsalochhoff（Tseloukhoff）的名义交给了达华银行（Dalbanque）本地分行的副经理。这最后提到的人是负责分配用于在中国进行秘密工作的资金的特别代理人。1932年，此人曾前往莫斯科，制定1933年度秘密资金的分配计划。

大约在同一时间，有一笔款项汇给了中国共产党上海支部中央委员会。此事发生在苏联对外贸易部（Vneshtorg，即苏联对外贸易机构）代表Waldmann抵达上海后不久。此人曾是莫斯科的检察官，目前暂时负责领导苏联共产党中央委员会的日本部和朝鲜部。

为此目的，于1933年3月在库尔贝特海军上将路（Rue Amiral Courbert）47号举行了一次会议，与会者包括中国共产党本地支部的一名代表。出席此次会议的有：Centrosojus本地分行经理Markoff先生，Morrison（当时是该机构化学部经理），

pages.en:
- 4 -

Tzalochoff (Dalbanque) and a person named Dunn, the
representative of the Central Committee of the Chinese
Communist Party, Waldmann gave Dunn certain instructions
on the policy to be followed by the Chinese Communist Party
as a result of the Sino Japanese conflict and in view of
the possibility of a conflict between the U.S.S.R. and
Japan. Waldmann added that he would proceed to Tientsin
to issue instructions.

At the close of the meeting, Tsalochoff, on the
orders of Waldmann, handed Dunn a sum of Mex. $12,000
and Yen 15,000. The official reason for this meeting
was given out as the opening of negotiations for the
sale of the products of the Soyusneft.

After the return of Waldmann to Tientsin, he
had another meeting with Markoff, Tsalochoff, Morrison
and a Chinese named Kai Ho who works in the economics
department of the local branch of Centrosojus and who
speaks Russian. (This Chinese is short and thin and
looks like a Japanese ). Little was discussed at this
meeting; it was simply pointed out that the work done
at Tientsin was insufficient. There was a shortage
of funds and large sums were required for the intensification
of the propaganda in this city. Waldmann promised to
bring forward this question upon his return to Moscow.

At the close of the meeting, everybody left the
house except Waldmann who had a private conversation with
the Chinese Kai Ho.
pages.zh:
- 4 -

Tzalochoff（达华银行）以及一名名为Dunn的人，他是中国共产党中央委员会的代表。Waldmann就中日冲突以及苏联与日本之间可能发生冲突的情况下，中国共产党应遵循的政策向Dunn下达了某些指示。Waldmann补充说，他将前往天津发布指示。

会议结束时，Tsalochoff奉Waldmann之命，交给Dunn墨西哥银元12,000元和日元15,000元。这次会议的公开理由被称为开启关于销售苏联石油联合公司（Soyusneft）产品的谈判。

Waldmann返回天津后，又与Markoff、Tsalochoff、Morrison以及一名在Centrosojus本地分行经济部门工作、会说俄语的中国人Kai Ho举行了另一次会议。（这名中国人身材矮小瘦削，看起来像日本人）。这次会议讨论的内容不多；只是指出在天津所做的工作不足。资金短缺，需要大量资金来加强在该市的宣传工作。Waldmann承诺在返回莫斯科时提出这个问题。

会议结束时，除Waldmann外，所有人都离开了房子，Waldmann与中国人Kai Ho进行了私下谈话。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, THURSDAY, JUNE 29, 1933

TRIAL OF V. A.
MORRISON

Court Finds Russian Not
Guilty

SENSATIONAL CHARGE BY
ACCUSED'S WIFE

After a lengthy hearing featured
by statements by three witnesses for
the prosecution and several
witnesses for the defence, V. A.
Morrison, 31 year old Russian who
was until recently chief of the
chemical department of the Centro-
sojus (Soviet Trading Co.), 2
Peking Road, and who was charged
with misappropriating $25,000 be-
longing to his employers, was ac-
quitted by Judge Chien in the First
Special District Court yesterday
morning. The police, represented
by Mr. Paul Y. Ru, Assistant Muni-
cipal Advocate, reserved the right
to file an appeal against the Court's
decision. During the period of ap-
peal, Morrison will be released on
bail.

At the outset of the hearing, Mr.
Ru told the Court that a further
charge of forgery was preferred by
police against the accused. Counsel
said that the Centrosojus received
a cargo of sulphate of soda from
abroad and it was stored with G. E.
Marden & Co. At the end of April,
the accused told Mr. Markoff, man-
ager of the Centrosojus, that he had
a buyer. Mr. Markoff then signed
transferring the cargo to accused.
The accused sold the cargo to a
Chinese firm at 1634 Canton Road,
and went to Hankow with the pro-
ceeds of the sale after issuing a re-
ceipt bearing his own signature as
well as that of Zanegin, an account-
ant of the Centrosojus. Zanegin,
however, denied having signed this
receipt. The accused later surren-
dered to the police.

Admittance Refused

Accused, questioned by the Court,
said that he gave the proceeds of
the sale to Markoff in the latter's
office and that, when he was in
Markoff's office, Krassovsky, the
chief accountant, knocked at the
door, but was refused admittance by
Markoff.

The Court then questioned Mar-
koff in regard to the bills which he
had signed, authorising the accused
to take out the cargo from go-
downs. Markoff declared he did not
know until recently that the cargo
had been sold by accused to the
Chinese firm nor did he receive any
money from the accused for the
sale.

Questioned by the Judge why he
had signed four bills authorising
the accused to take the whole of the
cargo from the godowns if he had
no knowledge about the sale,
Markoff stated the accused had told
him that the would-be purchasers
would like to see samples of the
goods. Therefore he signed the
bills.

Bodyguard as Witness

Zee Ke-ming, of the Chinese firm
at 1634 Canton Road, and Zee's
bodyguard were then called to the
witness' box. Zee told the Court
that, after successful negotiations
regarding the purchase of the sul-
phate of soda, he took the money
to the Centrosojus' office on May
13, but did not hand over the money
that day owing to the fact that cer-
tain arrangements had not been
completed. The payment of the pur-
chase price was made to the accused
on May 17.

Zee Ke-ming's bodyguard stated
that on May 17, he accompanied the
accused from Mr. Zee's firm to a
native bank where the accused ob-
tained the money for the sale of the
sulphate of soda. Witness then
said that he again accompanied, in
a motor car, the accused to the
Centrosojus' office and saw the ac-
cused enter a lift with the bank-
notes.

The accused declared he was not
guilty, that he had paid the money
to Markoff, and that he left for
Hankow because he was afraid he
would be sent back to the Soviet
Russia for political reasons.

After the Court had delivered its
judgment, a mild sensation was
created in the court-room by the ac-
cused's wife who called Markoff, the
manager of the Centrosojus, a num-
ber of bad names and shouted in
Russian: "You beat me and try to
make my husband a criminal." She
also chased Markoff as the latter
left the court-room, but was stop-
ped by the court-guards.

Dr. F. Wilheim and Mr. J. E.
Badeley watched the case for the
Centrosojus.

《字林西报》，1933年6月29日，星期四

V. A. MORRISON 案审判

法院裁定俄国人无罪

被告妻子提出轰动性指控

在经过长时间的听证，期间控方三名证人及辩方数名证人分别作证后，现年31岁的俄国人V. A. Morrison被第一特区地方法院的钱法官于昨日上午宣判无罪。Morrison直至最近一直担任北京路2号苏联消费合作社中央联社（Centrosojus，苏联贸易公司）化学部主任，他被指控侵吞雇主25,000美元。警方由助理市政检察官Paul Y. Ru先生代表，保留对法院判决提出上诉的权利。在上诉期间，Morrison将被保释释放。

听证开始时，Ru先生告诉法庭，警方还对被告提出了伪造文件的进一步指控。辩护律师称，Centrosojus从国外收到一批硫酸钠，并存放在G. E. Marden & Co.仓库。四月底，被告告诉Centrosojus经理Markoff先生，他找到了一名买家。随后Markoff先生签署了将货物转让给被告的文件。被告将货物卖给了广东路1634号的一家中国商行，并在开具了一张既有他自己签名又有Centrosojus会计师Zanegin签名的收据后，带着销售所得前往汉口。然而，Zanegin否认签署过这张收据。被告后来向警方自首。

拒绝入内

被告接受法庭询问时表示，他在Markoff的办公室将销售所得交给了Markoff，并且当他在Markoff办公室时，总会计师Krassovsky敲了门，但被Markoff拒绝入内。

随后法庭就Markoff签署的授权被告从仓库提取货物的单据对他进行了询问。Markoff声明，他直到最近才知道被告已将货物卖给那家中国商行，他也未从被告那里收到任何销售款项。

法官询问他，既然对销售一事不知情，为何还要签署四份授权被告提取全部货物的单据，Markoff称被告告诉他，潜在买家希望查看货物样品。因此他签署了这些单据。

保镖作证

随后，广东路1634号中国商行的Zee Ke-ming及其保镖被传唤至证人席。Zee告诉法庭，在就购买硫酸钠成功谈判后，他于5月13日将钱带到Centrosojus办公室，但由于某些手续尚未办妥，当天并未交付款项。购货款是在5月17日支付给被告的。

Zee Ke-ming的保镖陈述称，5月17日，他陪同被告从Zee先生的商行前往一家华资银行，被告在那里取得了出售硫酸钠的款项。证人随后表示，他再次乘车陪同被告前往Centrosojus办公室，并看到被告拿着钞票进入电梯。

被告宣称自己无罪，称他已将钱款支付给Markoff，而他前往汉口是因为担心出于政治原因被遣送回苏联俄罗斯。

法庭宣判后，被告的妻子在法庭上引起了一阵轻微的骚动，她用一些难听的称呼辱骂Centrosojus经理Markoff，并用俄语高喊：“你打我，还试图让我的丈夫成为罪犯。”当Markoff离开法庭时，她还追赶他，但被法警拦住。

F. Wilheim博士和J. E. Badeley先生代表Centrosojus旁听了此案。

THE MORRISON CASE
British Registration

To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS"
SIR,—I venture to inquire whether
the British authorities, who have
registered Comintern as a British
company realize the implications of
certain revelations in the case before
a Chinese Court here this week. It
seems obvious that political acti-
vities are very much to the fore in
the minds of the employees of this
company. They are all Soviet
subjects and the only British quality
appears to be in the registration.
Is this palatable to Britain?

According to the Sing Seng News Agency,
"Ma Li Son", an ex-employee of the Soviet Russia Co-operative Company, No.2 Peking Road, who mysteriously disappeared about a month ago, has returned to Shanghai and surrendered himself to the Shanghai First Special District Court. His disappearance was the outcome of some political disputes. He has disclosed the fact that the Soviet-Russia Co-operative Company is not a commercial body but had been established for secret political activities.
"Ma Li Son" recently sent the following letter to various newspaper offices refuting the report published a certain local foreign newspaper regarding the conversation of "Mokoff"(?), Chairman of the Soviet Co-operative Companys:-
"In one part of the statement made by "Mokoff", he said 'The Soviet Russia Co-operative Company is the central federation of the Russian Production and Consumption Mutual Aid Society. The work of this Co-operative Company is beneficial to Great Britain as well as to China'. There are many errors in his statement. I can prove that this Co-operative Company has conducted many secret activities in China and other places because not long ago, I was in charge of the Import and Export Department of this Co-operative Company.
"According to "Mokoff", the object of the Company is to promote trade between China and Russia; and that the Company is a Soviet Trust Organisation, that for the past ten years, the trade between China and Russia has been in favour of China. "Mokoff" supports this statement by citing a report of the China Economic Magazine which says that the export of Chinese goods to Russia exceeded the import of Russian goods into China during the period 1923 - 1928. 《申报》：

前雇员揭露苏联商业组织的政治阴谋

据星生通讯社报道，北京路2号苏俄合作公司（Soviet Russia Co-operative Company）的前雇员“Ma Li Son”（音译）于约一个月前神秘失踪，现已返回上海并向上海第一特区地方法院自首。他的失踪是某些政治纠纷的结果。他披露了这样一个事实：苏俄合作公司并非商业机构，而是为秘密政治活动而建立的。
“Ma Li Son”（音译）最近向各报馆发出以下信件，驳斥某家本地外文报纸关于苏俄合作公司主席“Mokoff”（音译）谈话的报道：
“在‘Mokoff’（音译）的声明中，有一部分他说：‘苏俄合作公司是俄国生产与消费互助社的中央联合会。该合作公司的工作对英国和中国都有利。’他的声明中有许多错误。我可以证明，该合作公司在中国和其他地方进行了许多秘密活动，因为不久前，我负责该合作公司的进出口部。
“根据‘Mokoff’（音译）的说法，该公司的目标是促进中俄贸易；该公司是一个苏维埃信托组织，在过去十年中，中俄贸易有利于中国。‘Mokoff’（音译）引用《中国经济杂志》的一份报告来支持这一说法，该报告称在1923年至1928年期间，中国对俄国的出口超过了俄国对中国的进口。这是最荒谬的说法。我想问‘Mokoff’（音译），他是从哪里得到这本杂志的，以及为什么他没有在他关于其合作公司工作的记录中公布这些中俄贸易数据。他自己的商业报告应该比所有其他报告更可靠。由于我曾是该合作公司的部门主管，我可以证明，俄国货物对中国的进口量是中国货物对俄国出口量的数倍；而且俄国货物向中国的倾销并未给俄国带来任何利润。
“我非常清楚苏联政府在中国的商业计划。根据苏联政府的命令，每年输入中国的

Russian commodities like wood, cotton goods, chemicals, cement, fish, leather, furs, wine, and fruits, were fixed at over $22,500,000. The only Chinese export to Russia is tea which, however, has been decreasing year after year because the Russian Government is ordering its tea from Java and other places. As to the dumping policy adopted by Soviet Government, this can be proved by recalling the protest lodged by the Chinese Cement Trade Association against the dumping of Soviet cement into China, which had impaired the Chinese cement trade.
"The Co-operative Company is exerting all its efforts to combat British trade. Brunner, Mond and Company have been selling chemicals cheap in China. The Co-operative Company entered into a certain agreement with this British Company to work jointly for the suppression of the Chinese chemical trade. The Co-operative Company planned to eradicate later on the British chemical trade in China. According to "Mokoff's" statement, the Co-operative Company is a purely commercial organization to help British commerce and is registered in London under the British Commercial Law, and that no political movements are undertaken by the Company. This needs no refutation as it has been abundantly proved that it is not a purely commercial organ.
"All staff members of the Soviet-Russia Cooperative Company at Shanghai, Tientsin, Hankow and other cities in China are appointed by the Moscow authorities and act on instructions from Moscow. These members are not selected because of a knowledge of the Chinese market. They are all Communists working in the G.P.U. and most of them had formerly worked in a special service organization. That was why "Mokoff", "Papeky", "Yakuchincs", "Mehazloff", "Zeyikun", "Zakahm", "Manezingo", "Kotsloff", "Lifomhoff", "Tsaildauff", and others had been detailed to Shanghai.
"Papeky" joined the Communist Party in 1918. Between 1919 and 1925 he worked in the G.P.U. of the Special Gendarme Headquarters and was attached to Embassies abroad between 1925 and 1930. He possesses a special ability in the forgery of Chinese passports and copying the signatures of others. He is well acquainted with Chinese trade and is an expert in Chinese tea.
"Mehazloff" was formerly an Inspecting Officer and a Night Defence Commissioner of the G.P.U. Later he became an instructor of the G.P.U. in Central Asia. He joined the Communist Party in 1919 and was sent to Shanghai to assume the post of specialist in the Needle Weaving Department of the Soviet-Russia Cooperative Company.
"Zeyikun" is a Communist. He was detailed to work with the Soviet-Russia Cooperative Company as a specialist in the Spinning & Weaving Department.
"Yakuchincs" is a promoter of the Lenin's Communistic Youth and a special service member of the Special Service Department. He was sent to Shanghai to fill the post of wood specialist in the Wood Department of the Soviet-Russia Cooperative Company.

木材、棉织品、化学品、水泥、鱼、皮革、毛皮、酒和水果等俄国商品，固定超过22,500,000美元。中国对俄国的唯一出口是茶叶，然而，由于俄国政府从爪哇和其他地方订购茶叶，茶叶出口量逐年减少。至于苏联政府采取的倾销政策，可以通过回顾中国水泥同业公会针对苏联水泥倾销到中国损害中国水泥贸易所提出的抗议来证明。
“合作公司正竭尽全力打击英国贸易。布伦纳-蒙德公司（Brunner, Mond and Company）一直在中国廉价销售化学品。合作公司与这家英国公司达成了一项协议，共同压制中国化学工业。合作公司计划随后根除英国在华化学贸易。根据‘Mokoff’（音译）的说法，合作公司是一个纯粹的商业组织，旨在帮助英国商业，并根据英国商法在伦敦注册，该公司不从事任何政治运动。这无需反驳，因为已有充分证据证明它不是一个纯粹的商业机构。
“苏俄合作公司在上海、天津、汉口及中国其他城市的所有工作人员均由莫斯科当局任命，并按莫斯科的指示行事。这些成员的入选并非基于对中国市场的了解。他们都是在国家政治保卫局（G.P.U.）工作的共产党员，其中大多数人以前曾在特务组织工作。这就是为什么‘Mokoff’（音译）、‘Papeky’（音译）、‘Yakuchincs’（音译）、‘Mehazloff’（音译）、‘Zeyikun’（音译）、‘Zakahm’（音译）、‘Manezingo’（音译）、‘Kotsloff’（音译）、‘Lifomhoff’（音译）、‘Tsaildauff’（音译）等人被派往上海的原因。
“Papeky”（音译）于1918年加入共产党。1919年至1925年间，他在特别宪兵总部的国家政治保卫局（G.P.U.）工作，1925年至1930年间附属于驻外使馆。他具有伪造中国护照和模仿他人签名的特殊能力。他熟悉中国贸易，是中国茶叶专家。
“Mehazloff”（音译）曾任国家政治保卫局（G.P.U.）的检查官和夜间防卫专员。后来他成为中亚地区国家政治保卫局（G.P.U.）的教官。他于1919年加入共产党，并被派往上海担任苏俄合作公司针纺部专家。
“Zeyikun”（音译）是一名共产党员。他被派往苏俄合作公司担任纺织部专家。
“Yakuchincs”（音译）是列宁共产主义青年团的推动者，也是特务部的特务成员。他被派往上海填补苏俄合作公司木材部木材专家的职位。

MISCELLANEOUS.

A MOTOR CAR ACCIDENT: CRITICISM OF BRITONS AND THE S.M.P.

The Ningpo Daily News, a mosquito paper,
publishes the following comments:-
On the morning of August 10, two Britons named
"Pan Sz" and "Hai Ding Nga" drove a motor car at full
speed along Nanking Road and injured a Ningpo man named
Yue Gen Fu, breaking both his feet. However, the two
Britons paid no heed to the accident and went away in
their car.
At the instance of the two sons of the victim,
the Ningpo Fellow Provincials Association sent a report
to the Shanghai Municipal Police; they have also asked
the Chinese Ratepayers Association for assistance. Strange
to say, the attitude of the Police would seem to indicate
that no action would be taken against the two Britons.
The British community have always claimed to
be law-abiding and anxious for the maintenance of peace and
good order. Their indifference in this case would mean that
they treat with contempt the life of a Chinese.
We would advise the British that as the majority
of the British residents are law-abiding, they should
uphold their dignity and reputation.

一起汽车事故：对英国人和工部局警务处的批评

一家小报《宁波日报》发表了以下评论：
8月10日上午，两名名为“Pan Sz”（音译）和“Hai Ding Nga”（音译）的英国人驾驶汽车沿南京路全速行驶，撞伤了一名名为岳根福（Yue Gen Fu，音译）的宁波人，导致其双脚骨折。然而，这两名英国人对事故置之不理，驾车离去。
在受害者两个儿子的请求下，宁波同乡会向上海公共租界工部局警务处提交了一份报告；他们还请求华人纳税会提供协助。奇怪的是，警方的态度似乎表明不会对这两名英国人采取任何行动。
英国侨民社区一直声称自己守法，并渴望维护和平与良好秩序。他们在此事上的冷漠意味着他们蔑视中国人的生命。
我们要劝告英国人，既然大多数英国居民都是守法的，他们应该维护自己的尊严和声誉。

Shun Pao and other local newspapers:

CENTROSOJUS TO ENTERTAIN JOURNALISTS TO-DAY.

Recently local newspapers published reports to the effect that Centrosojus, No.2 Peking Road, a political organ, was responsible for the attempt on the life of Wang Ching Wei, President of the Executive Yuan.
Interviewed yesterday by a reporter of the Dah Kung News Agency, "Yin-Ts-Loo"(行子路), Head of the Economic Section of Centrosojus, made the following statements:-
"The report published by the various newspapers on August 30 about Centrosojus was contributed by an employee named Morrison who had been dismissed for embezzlement. This report was first made public in local Russian papers and translations were published by the Chinese newspapers. This report not only affects the Centrosojus but will seriously obstruct the relations between China and Soviet Russia. The local Russian newspapers are established by White Russians who are the political opponents of the Soviet Government and are responsible for this malicious propaganda. The Centrosojus has taken the matter in hand and is planning to give an entertainment to local newspapermen at the Metropole Hotel, Foochow Road, on September 2 in order to give them the facts. At the same time a report on the Sino-Russian trade and the trade policy of the Soviet Government towards China will also be made".

苏联消费合作社总社今日招待记者。

近日本地报纸刊登报道，称位于北京路2号的苏联消费合作社总社（Centrosojus）是一个政治机构，应对刺杀国民政府行政院院长汪精卫的未遂事件负责。
大公报通讯社记者昨日采访了苏联消费合作社总社经济部主任“Yin-Ts-Loo”（行子路），他发表了以下声明：
“8月30日各报纸发表的关于苏联消费合作社总社的报道，是由一名因侵吞公款而被解雇的名为莫里森（Morrison）的雇员提供的。这份报告首先在本地俄文报纸上公开，随后由中文报纸翻译刊登。这份报告不仅影响苏联消费合作社总社，还将严重阻碍中国与苏俄之间的关系。本地俄文报纸是由反对苏联政府的白俄建立的，他们对这种恶意宣传负有责任。苏联消费合作社总社已着手处理此事，并计划于9月2日在福州路大都会酒店（Metropole Hotel）招待本地新闻界人士，向他们提供事实真相。同时，还将发布一份关于中俄贸易及苏联政府对华贸易政策的报告”。

THE CHINA PRESS, SUNDAY, SEPTEMBER 8, 1929

Centrosojus
Denies Plot
Against China

Concern Only Interested
In Trade, Spokesman Of
Soviet Company States

Recent reports in the Chinese
newspapers to the effect that the
Centrosojus (England) Ltd., which
is the buying and selling agent for
co-operative enterprises in Soviet
Russia is carrying on secret
political activities against China
and that it is plotting on the life
of Mr Wang Ching-wei, president
of the Executive Yuan, were em-
phatically denied by Mr. M. M.
Markhoff, manager of the com-
pany, during a reception extended
to representatives of the local
vernacular press in the Metropole
Hotel yesterday.

"The Centrosojus is a com-
mercial organization indulging in
no political activities. We are here
for business. What we are inter-
ested in is to make up a balance,
and meanwhile to secure a hand-
some dividend," declared Mr.
Markhoff.

Not Political

According to the manager, who
presided at the function attended
by more than 20 representatives of
the Chinese press, the Centrosojus
was registered in England and is
carrying on business here through
Chinese merchants.

The company is not a political
group and hence it is not engaged
in any political functions, Mr.
Markhoff declared. All reports
charging the firm with secret
activities against China are absolu-
tely groundless and can be nothing
but malicious rumors purposely
spread by those unfriendly to the
company in hope to gain certain
advantages, he said.

The rumors first started a few
months ago with the so-called mys-
terious disappearance of a certain
Mr. Morrison, who represented
himself as chief of the chemical
department of the company, he
continued. The company subse-
quently "picked" up an action
against Morrison in the First Dis-
trict Court on the charge of em-
bezzlement.

An interesting angle to the case
came up when Mr. Morrison sud-
denly surrendered himself at the
Central Police Station saying that
he had just rushed back from
Hankow on hearing the embezzle-
ment charge against him in
Shanghai. The case was duly
brought up in the local tribunal,
which, however, found him not
guilty.

Never Chemical Chief

But according to Mr. Markhoff
yesterday, Mr. Morrison had never
been the chief of the chemical de-
partment in the company. In-
stead, he was just an ordinary
staff member, who left the company
a few months ago.

When reminded that Mr. Morri-
son was found not guilty in the
local court, Mr. Markhoff only said

Centrosojus Manager
(Continued From Page 3, Col. 4.)

"We have no influence with the
Chinese court."

According to Mr. Markhoff, Mor-
rison came back from his trip to
Hankow with a statement as to
what happened there, but actually
he had never been sent there.

《字林西报》，1929年9月8日，星期日

苏联消费合作总社
否认针对中国的阴谋

苏联公司发言人称
其只关心贸易利益

中国报纸近期报道称，苏联消费合作总社（英国）有限公司（Centrosojus (England) Ltd.，系苏俄合作社企业的购销代理机构）正在开展针对中国的秘密政治活动，并策划谋害行政院院长汪精卫先生。该公司经理M. M. Markhoff先生昨日在大都会酒店（Metropole Hotel）招待本地中文报刊代表时，对此予以坚决否认。

“苏联消费合作总社是一个商业组织，不参与任何政治活动。我们来这里是为了做生意。我们感兴趣的是平衡账目，同时获得丰厚的红利，”Markhoff先生宣称。

非政治性质

据主持此次有二十多位中文报界代表出席的活动的经理称，苏联消费合作总社在英国注册，并通过中国商人在此开展业务。

Markhoff先生宣称，该公司不是一个政治团体，因此不从事任何政治职能。他说，所有指控该公司从事针对中国的秘密活动的报道都绝对毫无根据，不过是那些对公司不友好的人为了获取某些利益而故意散布的恶意谣言。

他继续说，谣言始于几个月前，当时所谓的某位Morrison先生神秘失踪，此人自称是该公司化学部主任。随后，公司以挪用公款的罪名在第一特区地方法院对Morrison提起诉讼。

此案出现了一个有趣的转折：Morrison先生突然到中央捕房自首，称他听到上海方面对他提出挪用公款指控后，刚从汉口赶回。该案随后在当地法庭正式审理，但法庭裁定其无罪。

从未担任化学部主任

但据Markhoff先生昨日称，Morrison先生从未担任过该公司的化学部主任。相反，他只是一名普通职员，已于几个月前离开公司。

当被提醒Morrison先生在本地法院被判无罪时，Markhoff先生仅表示

苏联消费合作总社经理
（续自第3栏第4版。）

“我们对中国法院没有影响力。”

据Markhoff先生称，Morrison从汉口之行带回了一份关于那里发生情况的陈述，但实际上他从未被派往那里。

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Monday, September 18, 1933

Pravda Calls Attention
To Acts In Shanghai
Falsifying Centrosojus

(Tass)
MOSCOW, Sept. 17.—Dwelling on the provocational attempts frustrate the normal business activities of the Shanghai branch of the Centrosojus, "Pravda" in an editorial remark points out that the organisers of these provocations are applying the usual methods of falsification.

The Whiteguardist Morrison is used for writing sensational "exposures"; nor was it forgotten the notorious agent-provocateur white-guardist Kedrolivansky who has repeatedly "distinguished" himself in the organisation of anti-Soviet provocations.

"Pravda" emphasizes the existing intention to stage a political trial against Centrosojus by falsely and slanderingly representing this commercial organisation as a political center of the communist movement in China.

"These efforts to discredit the business prestige of the Shanghai branch of the Centrosojus will not meet with the support of the Chinese commercial circles, because the Centrosojus, being connected with the Chinese market for over 10 years, has gained already firm confidence of the business community," concludes the newspaper.

《真理报》关注上海
伪造苏联消费合作总社的行为

（塔斯社）
莫斯科，9月17日电。——《真理报》在一篇社论评论中，着重指出有人企图破坏苏联消费合作总社上海分社的正常商业活动，这些挑衅活动的组织者正在使用惯用的伪造手段。

白卫分子莫里森被用来撰写耸人听闻的“揭露”文章；也没有忘记臭名昭著的白卫分子、职业挑衅者凯德罗利万斯基（Kedrolivansky），他在组织反苏挑衅活动中多次“表现突出”。

《真理报》强调，目前存在通过虚假和诽谤性地将这一商业组织描绘成中国共产主义运动的政治中心，从而对苏联消费合作总社进行政治审判的意图。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, TUESDAY, SEPTEMBER 19, 1933

CASE AGAINST
MARKHOFF
Centrosojus' Ex-employee
Brings Counter-action

The recent action brought in the
First Special District Court by M.
Markhoff, manager of the Centroso-
jus, Ltd., 2 Peking Road, against
F. A. Morrison, former salesman of
the Centrosojus, charged with
misappropriation of over $35,000,
representing the price of a cargo of
goods allegedly sold through Mor-
rison, had an interesting sequel yes-
terday when a counter-action was
brought in the same court by Mor-
rison against Markhoff and five
other employees of the Centrosojus,
who were charged by Morrison with
false accusation, illegal detention
and forcible seizure of money. The
five accused other than Markhoff
were Yukimatsu, Moiseeva, Babich,
Krasovsky, and Bikova.
Represented by Dr. Franklin Chiu,
attorney-at-law, Morrison told the
Court yesterday that he was
formerly in the employ of the Cent-
rosojus, but was later forced to leave
his employment and went to Hankow
because he refused to engage in
political activities for the first ac-
cused and the latter was trying to
send him back to Soviet Russia.
The complainant continued that a
false charge of misappropriation
was then preferred against him by
Markhoff in the Court, but he was
found not guilty. Complainant
alleged that Markhoff also sent the
fourth, fifth and sixth accused to his
home at 374 Kiangsu Road and,
illegally detaining his wife in a
bathroom, forcibly took away from
his house Gold $11,177 and $725 in
notes, etc. Receipts for these
amounts were later issued by the
second and third accused to the
complainant, but the money had
never been returned.
All six accused were in Court and
a flat denial of the charges were
entered by them. The three accused
alleged to have invaded the com-
plainant's house declared they had
never been there and so it was im-
possible for them to take any money
from complainant's house or to
detain his wife.
The hearing was adjourned till
next Thursday, the accused being
bailed out in the sum of $5,000.
Dr. F. Wilhelm and four Chinese
lawyers were the counsel for
defence.

《字林西报》，1933年9月19日，星期二

针对
Markhoff的案件
苏联消费合作总社前雇员
提起反诉

苏联消费合作总社有限公司（Centrosojus, Ltd.，地址北京路2号）经理M. Markhoff近日在第一特区地方法院对该社前推销员F. A. Morrison提起诉讼，指控其挪用超过35,000美元，这笔款项据称是Morrison销售的一批货物的价款。昨日该案出现了有趣的后续发展：Morrison在同一法院对Markhoff及苏联消费合作总社的其他五名员工提起反诉，指控他们诬告、非法拘禁和强行劫取钱财。除Markhoff外的五名被告分别是Yukimatsu、Moiseeva、Babich、Krasovsky和Bikova。

Morrison由律师Franklin Chiu博士代理，他昨日告诉法庭，他此前受雇于苏联消费合作总社，但后来被迫离职前往汉口，因为他拒绝为第一被告从事政治活动，而后者正试图将他送回苏俄。

原告继续称，Markhoff随后在法庭上对他提出了虚假的挪用公款指控，但他被判无罪。原告指控Markoff还派遣第四、第五和第六被告到他位于江苏路374号的家中，非法将其妻子拘禁在浴室里，并从其家中强行拿走黄金11,177美元和现钞725美元等。第二和第三被告后来向原告出具了这些金额的收据，但钱款从未归还。

六名被告均出庭，并对指控予以断然否认。被指控闯入原告住所的三名被告声明他们从未去过那里，因此不可能从原告家中拿走任何钱款或拘禁其妻子。

听证会延期至下周四举行，被告以5,000美元保释金获保释。
F. Wilhelm博士和四名中国律师担任辩护律师。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, FRIDAY, SEPTEMBER 29, 1933

RECEIPT ISSUED
BY MARKHOFF

Examination Ordered by
Judge Shih

ROBBERY ALLEGED
BY MORRISON

Heated arguments regarding the genuineness of a receipt for Gold-$11,177 and £722 marked the resumed hearing, before Judge L. J. Shih in the First Special District Court yesterday afternoon, of the private criminal prosecution brought by V. A. Morrison, a Soviet citizen, against M. Markhoff, manager of the Centrosojus (England), Ltd., 2 Peking Road, and Yakimenko, Moiseeva, Babich, Krasovsky, and Bihova, all employees of the Centrosojus, who were charged with robbery, illegal detention and false accusation.

It will be recalled that Morrison was recently charged by M. Markhoff in the same Court with misappropriation of over $25,000, the value of a cargo of soda sold by Morrison for the Centrosojus. The accused was later acquitted by the Court and now he was charging Markhoff and five of his employees with false accusation, robbery, etc., it being declared by Morrison that he had never misappropriated any money of the Centrosojus and that the charge of misappropriation had been fabricated by Markhoff because he, Morrison, had refused to engage in political activities for the Soviet trade organisation.

Morrison further declared that when he was detained by police at the instigation of Markhoff, the latter sent three of his employees, the fourth, fifth and sixth accused, to his home at 374 Kiangse Road and, illegally detaining his wife in a bathroom, the invaders searched the house and took away Gold$11,177 and £722 in addition to a bank book and a cheque. The cheque and bank book, Morrison declared, were later returned by the accused, but not the money although the accused later issued a receipt for this amount to him.

Not a Receipt

At yesterday's hearing, counsel for the defence told the Court that the receipt issued by Markhoff to Morrison was not a receipt, but a letter giving Morrison permission to return to Soviet Russia and to apply to the Soviet organs for travelling expenses after his arrival at Vladivostok. This letter, counsel for defence declared, never mentioned that a sum of Gold$11,117 and £722 had been received from Morrison and the numerical characters which appeared in the letter had been added by Morrison himself.

As Morrison insisted that the numerical characters in the letter were not added by himself, the Judge ordered that the letter should be examined by an impartial official and the result of the examination would be made public at the next hearing.

Morrison further stated that he came to China in January, 1932, when he joined the staff of the Centrosojus at a monthly salary of Gold$185. The sum of Gold$11,117 and £722 belonged to his wife, Morrison told the Court, the major portion of the amount they having managed to bring from Russia while the remaining amount was his savings after arrival in Shanghai. He did not deposit the sum with a bank, Morrison told the Court.

Owing to the late hour the hearing was again adjourned. Dr. Franklin Chia represented Morrison and his wife while Dr. F. Williams and four Chinese lawyers were the counsel for defence.

《字林西报》，1933年9月29日，星期五

Markhoff出具的
收据

施法官下令鉴定

莫里森指控
抢劫

昨日下午，在第一特区地方法院，由L. J. Shih法官主持，恢复了苏联公民V. A. Morrison对苏联消费合作总社（英国）有限公司（地址北京路2号）经理M. Markhoff以及该社员工Yakimenko、Moiseeva、Babich、Krasovsky和Bihova提起的私人刑事诉讼的审理，被告被控抢劫、非法拘禁和诬告。庭审中就一张金额为黄金11,177美元和722英镑的收据的真实性展开了激烈辩论。

回想起来，Morrison最近曾被M. Markhoff在同一法院指控挪用超过25,000美元，这是Morrison为苏联消费合作总社销售的一批苏打粉的价值。被告后来被法庭宣判无罪，现在他指控Markhoff及其五名员工诬告、抢劫等。Morrison声称，他从未挪用苏联消费合作总社的任何资金，挪用公款的指控是Markhoff捏造的，因为他Morrison拒绝为该苏联贸易组织从事政治活动。

Morrison进一步声明，当他应Markhoff的唆使被警察拘留时，后者派遣他的三名员工，即第四、第五和第六被告，前往他位于江苏路374号的家中，非法将其妻子拘禁在浴室里，入侵者搜查了房屋，除了一本存折和一张支票外，还拿走了黄金11,177美元和722英镑。Morrison声明，被告后来归还了支票和存折，但没有归还钱款，尽管被告后来就这笔金额向他出具了收据。

不是收据

在昨日的听证会上，辩护律师告诉法庭，Markhoff出具给Morrison的收据并非收据，而是一封信，允许Morrison返回苏俄，并在抵达符拉迪沃斯托克（海参崴）后向苏联机构申请旅费。辩护律师宣称，这封信从未提及收到Morrison的黄金11,117美元和722英镑，信中出现的数字字符是Morrison自己添加的。

由于Morrison坚持信中的数字字符并非由他自己添加，法官下令由一名公正官员对该信件进行鉴定，鉴定结果将在下次听证会上公布。

Morrison还陈述，他于1932年1月来到中国，当时他以每月185黄金美元的薪水加入苏联消费合作总社的员工队伍。Morrison告诉法庭，黄金11,117美元和722英镑属于他的妻子，其中大部分是他们设法从俄罗斯带出来的，其余部分是他抵达上海后的积蓄。Morrison告诉法庭，他没有将这笔钱存入银行。

由于时间已晚，听证会再次延期。Franklin Chia博士代表Morrison及其妻子，F. Williams博士和四名中国律师担任辩护律师。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, SATURDAY, OCTOBER 21, 1933.

MIDNIGHT SHOTS
IN CONCESSION

Mr. Morrison's Mysterious Visitor

A midnight visitor to the flat of Mr. Z. A. Morrison, formerly connected with Centrosojus, Ltd., is engaging the attention of the French authorities at the moment. It is not thought that the visit was that of a robber, as nothing was taken, but the man was discovered bending over the bed where Mr. Morrison was sleeping.

The incident occurred some time after midnight on the night of October 19-20. Mr. Morrison occupies a flat at 363 Avenue du Roi Albert. Mrs. Morrison awoke at the sound of someone moving about the bedroom, and then saw a figure bending over the bed in which her husband lay asleep.

At the sound of her voice, the man dropped something on the floor, and ran towards the window and verandah. Mrs. Morrison screamed for help, at which the man threw a chair at her. Mr. Morrison had by now awakened, and, getting his revolver, fired at the figure, who rapidly descended by means of a rain-pipe, and succeeded in making good his escape. The neighbourhood was aroused by the sound of the shots, and a search of the garden was made, without result, no one being found.

Investigation being made, a watchman related his encounter with a foreigner that night. Shortly after hearing the shots, he saw a foreigner come out of an alley-way. He asked him his business, and the man, saying he had "nothing to do with all the noise," quickly disappeared into Route Vallee. It is thought that more than one man was involved in the midnight visitation, as a heavy ladder was found against the wall and it would tax the efforts of one man to carry it.

《字林西报》，1933年10月21日，星期六。

租界内的
午夜枪声

莫里森先生的神秘访客

一位曾在苏联消费合作总社有限公司任职的Z. A. Morrison先生公寓的午夜访客，目前正引起法国当局的关注。人们认为这次来访并非盗贼所为，因为没有物品丢失，但该男子被发现正俯身在Morrison先生睡觉的床边。

事件发生在10月19日至20日深夜过后不久。Morrison先生居住在阿尔贝国王路（Avenue du Roi Albert）363号的一套公寓里。Morrison太太被卧室里有人走动的声音惊醒，随后看到一个身影俯在她丈夫熟睡的床边。

听到她的声音，该男子将某物掉在地板上，朝窗户和阳台跑去。Morrison太太大声呼救，该男子向她扔了一把椅子。此时Morrison先生已经醒来，他拿起左轮手枪向那个身影开枪，那人迅速顺着雨水管爬下，成功逃脱。枪声惊动了邻里，人们对花园进行了搜索，但一无所获，未发现任何人。

经调查，一名守夜人讲述了他当晚与一名外国人的遭遇。听到枪声后不久，他看到一名外国人从一条小巷走出来。他询问其来意，该男子称自己“与所有的噪音无关”，随即迅速消失在瓦勒路（Route Vallee）。人们认为参与这次午夜造访的不止一人，因为在墙边发现了一架沉重的梯子，一个人很难搬动它。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, TUESDAY, OCTOBER 24, 1933

CASE AGAINST
MR. MARKHOFF

Counter-Charge Made by
Accused

Mr. Markhoff, head of the
Centrosojus, local Soviet trade organ
with its office at 2 Peking Road, and
five other employees of the company,
Yakimenko, Noisceva, Babich,
Krasovsky and Bikova, who were
charged in the First Special District
Court with false accusation, illegal
detention and robbery by Mr. V. A.
Morrison, ex-salesman of the
Centrosojus, appeared before Judge
Shih yesterday afternoon for resum-
ed hearing of the case against them.
The accused told the Court that they
would file a counter-charge of false
accusation against Mr. Morrison.

The case as outlined by Mr.
Morrison's lawyer was that Mr.
Morrison was forced to quit his job
in the Centrosojus because he re-
fused to engage in political activities
for Mr. Markhoff and that on May
20 last, Mr. Markhoff sent the
fourth, fifth and sixth accused to Mr.
Morrison's house at 374 Kiangsu
Road, and, forcibly holding his wife
in a bathroom, conducted an illegal
search of the house and robbed Gold
$11,177 and $733 in notes. A receipt
for these amounts was issued to the
complainant, it was said.

An emphatic denial of these
charges was entered by the ac-
cused yesterday. Mr. Markhoff told
the Court that once Mr. Morrison's
wife came to his place and, stating
her husband had disappeared, asked
for financial aid to enable her to
return to Soviet Russia. Mrs. Mor-
rison also brought to his place a
cheque book, etc., as she could not
cash them. Whereupon Mr. Mark-
hoff said he gave a sum of money
to Mrs. Morrison.

The fifth accused stated that Mrs.
Morrison went to her place and said
she was penniless and could not
return to Russia. Accused said she
gave her $5.

Mr. Morrison told the Court that
the accused's statement that his wife
was willing to return to Soviet
Russia was absolutely without
foundation. Mr. Morrison handed
to Court a letter which he said would
prove that the accused's statement
was untrue.

Questioned by Court as to why a
receipt had been issued to him by the
accused if the latter really intended
to rob him of Gold $11,177 and
$733, Mr. Morrison stated that the
receipt was issued by the accused
when his wife insisted she would not
return to Soviet Russia unless a
receipt was issued to her for the
amount allegedly taken by the
accused.

A further adjournment of the
hearing was ordered. Dr. F. Wil-
helm and four Chinese lawyers were
for the defence.

《字林西报》，1933年10月24日，星期二

针对
马尔霍夫先生（Mr. Markhoff）的案件

被告提出反诉

马尔霍夫先生系苏联贸易机构“中央消费合作总社”（Centrosojus）驻沪办事处负责人，该办事处位于北京路2号。他与该公司另外五名员工——亚基缅科（Yakimenko）、诺伊谢娃（Noisceva）、巴比奇（Babich）、克拉索夫斯基（Krasovsky）和比科娃（Bikova）——被前“中央消费合作总社”销售员V. A. 莫里森先生（Mr. V. A. Morrison）指控犯有诬告、非法拘禁和抢劫罪。昨日下午，上述被告在施法官（Judge Shih）面前出庭，案件恢复审理。被告告知法庭，他们将对莫里森先生提出诬告的反诉。

莫里森的律师概述案情称：莫里森因拒绝为马尔霍夫先生从事政治活动而被迫辞去在“中央消费合作总社”的职务；去年5月20日，马尔霍夫派遣第四、第五和第六被告前往莫里森位于江苏路374号的寓所，强行将其妻子关在浴室内，对住宅进行非法搜查，并抢走金洋11,177元及纸币733元。据称，被告曾就上述款项向原告出具收据。

被告昨日对这些指控予以坚决否认。马尔霍夫告诉法庭，莫里森的妻子曾来到他处，声称其丈夫失踪，并请求资助以便返回苏维埃俄国。莫里森夫人还因无法兑现支票等票据，将其带到他处。于是，马尔霍夫称他给予莫里森夫人一笔钱款。

第五被告陈述，莫里森夫人曾到她处，自称身无分文，无法返回俄国。被告称她给了莫里森夫人5美元。

莫里森告诉法庭，被告所称其妻子愿意返回苏维埃俄国的说法毫无根据。莫里森向法庭提交了一封信件，称该信可证明被告的陈述不实。

当法庭问及，如果被告真意在于抢劫其金洋11,177元及733美元，为何还要向他出具收据时，莫里森陈述称，出具收据是因为其妻子坚持，除非被告就所谓拿走的款项向她出具收据，否则她绝不返回苏维埃俄国。

法庭下令再次延期审理。辩护方为F. 威廉博士（Dr. F. Wilhelm）及四位中国律师。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, TUESDAY, OCTOBER 24, 1933

Morrison-Markoff Action
Awaits Judgment

Sequel To Earlier Case Nears End In First
Special Court; Experts Declare A
Receipt To Have Been Forged

Judgment will be delivered to-
morrow in the case in the First
Special District Court in which M.
Markoff, manager of the local
office of Controsoju, (China)
Limited, a Russian organization
on Peking Road, and five of his
assistants are charged with false
accusation, illegal search and
robbery by Mr. N. Morrison, a
former employee of the firm. This
was announced yesterday by Judge
Shih after he had listened to
heated argument between lawyers
for the two sides.

The case is a sequel to a dis-
missed case in which Mr. Morrison
was charged by Mr. Markoff with
having taken a large sum of the
company's money. Now Mr. Morri-
son has charged Wakimanko and
Mrs. Moiseeva, two of the accused,
with having robbed his wife of
G.$11,470 and £700 by forcing her
to give the money to them during
his absence. The money was never
returned although Mrs. Morrison
had received a receipt for it, he
said. The accused denied the
charges. The money, according to
the plaintiff, represented the sav-
ings of his wife and himself and
he dared not deposit it in a bank
because the Russian law did not
allow him to do so.

Many Counsels

At the last hearing attention
was directed to a receipt which
the Morrisons were supposed to
have obtained from the manage-
ment of Controsojas in exchange
for their cash. The case was then
adjourned pending examination by
experts of the typewriter used to
type out the receipt. It was stated
by the Court yesterday that accord-
ing to examination made by the
Ministry of Justice the receipt was
forged.

Speaking for defendants, four
Chinese lawyers and one foreign
lawyer, Mr. F. Wilhelm, all denied
the charges made by the Morrisons.
One Chinese lawyer argued that no
punishment did not mean false
accusation meaning that Mr.
Morrison simply escaped punish-
ment in the last case.

Savings And Russian Law

Mr. Wilhelm stressed that com-
plainant could produce evidence to
support his second charge, that of
illegal search. Accused did not
commit robbery, because otherwise
he would not have issued a receipt,
he said. The only other witness
for the plaintiff, the maid, might
have been influenced by her master
and mistress.

In cross-examining plaintiff, Mr.
Wilhelm said that it would have
been a miracle for them to bring
such a big sum of money from
their country to Shanghai if the
Russian law was strict. He assert-
ed that it was an imaginary sum.
He also said that it was ridiculous
that plaintiff did not arrange to
have it deposited with any one of
the Shanghai banks. He accused
the Morrisons of forgery of the
receipt.

Counteracting certain state-
ments, M. Markoff said in the
Court that there was nothing
political involved in the case. He
explained that his firm was of more
than 10 years' standing and that
it was a purely commercial
organization aimed at promoting
friendly relations between China
and the U.S.S.R.

《上海泰晤士报》，1933年10月24日，星期二

莫里森诉马尔霍夫案
等待判决

第一特区法院早期案件的后续审理接近尾声；专家宣称收据系伪造

第一特区法院审理的一起案件将于明日宣判。该案中，位于北京路的俄罗斯组织“全苏消费合作社联合社（中国）有限公司”（Controsoju (China) Limited）本地办事处经理M. 马尔霍夫（M. Markoff）及其五名助手，被该公司前雇员N. 莫里森先生（Mr. N. Morrison）指控犯有诬告、非法搜查和抢劫罪。施法官（Judge Shih）在听取双方律师激烈辩论后，于昨日宣布了这一消息。

本案是此前一起已被驳回案件的后续。在那起案件中，马尔霍夫先生指控莫里森先生侵吞公司巨额资金。如今，莫里森先生指控两名被告瓦基曼科（Wakimanko）和莫伊谢耶娃夫人（Mrs. Moiseeva），称她们在他不在家期间，强迫其妻子交出金钱，从而抢劫其妻子金洋11,470元及英镑700镑。他说，尽管莫里森夫人收到了收据，但钱款从未归还。被告否认了这些指控。据原告称，这笔钱代表了他和妻子的积蓄，由于俄国法律不允许，他不敢将其存入银行。

众多律师

在最近一次庭审中，注意力集中在一张收据上，据称莫里森夫妇用现金从“中央消费合作总社”（Controsojas）管理层换取了这张收据。当时案件休庭，以待专家对打印该收据的打字机进行检查。法庭昨日声明，经司法部检查，该收据系伪造。

代表被告发言的四位中国律师和一位外国律师F. 威廉先生（Mr. F. Wilhelm）均否认莫里森夫妇提出的指控。一位中国律师辩称，未受惩罚并不意味着诬告，意指莫里森先生只是在上一案中逃脱了惩罚。

储蓄与俄国法律

威廉博士强调，原告未能提供证据支持其第二项指控，即非法搜查。他说，被告并未实施抢劫，否则他们不会出具收据。原告方的唯一其他证人女仆，可能受到了其男主人的影响。

在交叉询问原告时，威廉先生说，如果俄国法律严格，他们能将如此巨款从本国带到上海简直是个奇迹。他断言这笔金额是虚构的。他还说，原告不安排将钱款存入上海任何一家银行，这是荒谬的。他指控莫里森夫妇伪造收据。

为了反驳某些陈述，M. 马尔霍夫在法庭上表示，本案不涉及任何政治因素。他解释说，他的公司已成立十余年，是一个纯粹的商业组织，旨在促进中国与苏联之间的友好关系。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS. THURSDAY, OCTOBER 26, 1933

SOVIET CITIZENS
ACQUITTED

Centrosojus' ex-Salesman
Loses Suit

The case against Mr. Markhoff,
head of the Centrosojus, local Soviet
trade organisation, and five other
employees of the company, Yaki-
menko, Moiseeva, Babich, Krasovsky,
and Bikova, charged by Mr. V. A.
Morrison, ex-salesman of the
Centrosojus, with false accusation,
robbery and illegal detention, came
to a conclusion in the First Special
District Court yesterday when Judge
L. J. Shih delivered his judgment
acquitting all the accused. The
Judge also dismissed the counter-
charge of false accusation filed by
the accused against Mr. Morrison.
The most important evidence pro-
duced in Court by the complainant
was in the form of a letter from the
complainant Gold $11,177 and $722.
The complainant declared these
amounts of money had been seized
from his house by the fifth and sixth
accused at the first accused's in-
stigation, and that the above letter
had been issued as a receipt.
The accused emphatically denied
having committed robbery and
asserted that the numerical charac-
ters in their letter to the complain-
ant had been added without their
knowledge. The letter, the accused
told the Court, was issued by them,
authorizing the complainant to
return to Russia and apply to Soviet
organisations for travelling ex-
penses after arrival at Vladivostok.
It was not a receipt, accused said.
After having the letter examined
by official experts, the Court upheld
the accused's contention and acquit-
ted them of the robbery charge. As
to the other two charges, they were
also branded as groundless by the
accused who maintained they had
not been to the complainant's house
and consequently it was impossible
to illegally detain his wife in a
bathroom as alleged.
Counsel in the case were Dr.
Franklin Chiu for complainant and
Dr. F. Wilhelm and four Chinese
lawyers for the defence.

《字林西报》，1933年10月26日，星期四

苏联公民
被判无罪

“中央消费合作总社”前销售员
败诉

针对“中央消费合作总社”（Centrosojus，当地苏联贸易组织）负责人马尔霍夫先生（Mr. Markhoff）及该公司另外五名员工——亚基缅科（Yakimenko）、莫伊谢耶娃（Moiseeva）、巴比奇（Babich）、克拉索夫斯基（Krasovsky）和比科娃（Bikova）的案件，于昨日在第一特区法院审结。施L. J. 法官（Judge L. J. Shih）作出判决，宣告所有被告无罪。法官还驳回了被告针对莫里森先生提出的诬告反诉。

原告在法庭上提出的最重要证据是一封信件，涉及金洋11,177元和722美元。原告宣称，这些钱款是在第一被告的唆使下，由第五和第六被告从其家中搜走的，而上述信件是作为收据出具的。

被告坚决否认实施抢劫，并坚称信件中的数字字符是在他们不知情的情况下添加的。被告告诉法庭，这封信是他们出具的，授权原告返回俄国，并在抵达符拉迪沃斯托克（海参崴）后向苏联机构申请旅费。被告称，这不是收据。

在经过官方专家对信件进行检查后，法庭支持了被告的主张，并宣告他们抢劫罪名不成立。至于另外两项指控，被告也斥之为毫无根据，他们坚持未曾去过原告家中，因此不可能像指控所称那样将其妻子非法拘禁在浴室内。

本案代理律师为：原告方富兰克林·邱博士（Dr. Franklin Chiu），被告方F. 威廉博士（Dr. F. Wilhelm）及四位中国律师。
