THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, TUESDAY, NOVEMBER 28, 1933

V. A. MORRISON
APPEALS

Dissatisfied with District
Court Decision

The legal battle between Messrs.
Marknoff and Morrison, Soviet
citizens, in connection with alleged
misappropriation of funds belong-
ing to the Centrosojus and robbery
of G.$11,177, was carried to the
Second Branch Kiangsu High Court
yesterday when Morrison appealed
against a recent decision of the
First Special District Court, ac-
quitting Markhoff and five other
Centrosojus employees of charges
of robbery, false accusations and
illegal detention. The hearing was
adjourned.

The battle started several months
ago when Markhoff, as head of the
Centrosojus, charged Morrison in
the First District Court with hav-
ing misappropriated over [□]□□□
through the sale of a quantity of
goods on behalf of the Centrosojus.
After he was found not guilty,
Morrison charged Markhoff in the
same Court with malicious accusa-
tion, and further with having sent
men to his home, illegally detained
for several hours his wife in a
bath-room, and robbed her of
G.$11,177 and £722. After a num-
ber of hearings, this case was like-
wise dismissed.

In the High Court yesterday,
Morrison declared he was dissatis-
fied with the Lower Court's decision
because there had been sufficient
evidence against the six Centrosojus
employees. Having sold goods for
the Centrosojus, Morrison said he
handed over the money to Mark-
noff and the G.$11,177 and £722
forcibly taken away from him
belonged to his wife whose father
was a well-to-do merchant in
Russia before the revolution.

Morrison addressed the Court for
the major portion of yesterday's
hearing. In answer to the Court,
he stated that he was ordered to
return to Russia several months
ago and the reason was that,
according to instructions, a Soviet
citizen assigned to duty abroad
must go back after one or two
years. If a Soviet citizen ordered
to return refused to obey the
order, force would be employed to
bring him back and have him shot,
Morrison told the Court.

《字林西报》，1933年11月28日，星期二

V. A. 莫里森
上诉

对地方法院判决不满

苏联公民马尔克诺夫（Marknoff）先生与莫里森先生之间关于涉嫌挪用“中央消费合作总社”资金及抢劫金洋11,177元的法律斗争，于昨日延续至江苏高等法院第二分院，莫里森就第一特区法院近期作出的宣告马尔霍夫（Markhoff）及其他五名“中央消费合作总社”员工抢劫、诬告和非法拘禁罪名不成立的判决提起上诉。听证会延期举行。

这场争斗始于数月前，当时身为“中央消费合作总社”负责人的马尔霍夫在第一特区法院指控莫里森在代表“中央消费合作总社”销售一批货物过程中挪用了超过[□]□□□ [原文不清]。在被判无罪后，莫里森在同一法院指控马尔霍夫恶意起诉，并进一步指控其派人到莫里森家中，将其妻子非法拘禁在浴室内数小时，并抢劫其金洋11,177元及英镑722镑。经过多次听证，该案同样被驳回。

在昨日的高等法院庭审中，莫里森宣称他对下级法院的判决感到不满，因为有足够的证据反对这六名“中央消费合作总社”员工。莫里森说，他在为“中央消费合作总社”销售货物后，将钱款交给了马尔克诺夫（Marknoff），而被强行夺走的金洋11,177元及英镑722镑属于他的妻子，其父亲在革命前是俄国的一位富裕商人。

莫里森在昨日的大部分听证时间里向法庭陈述。在回答法庭询问时，他表示，几个月前他曾接到命令返回俄国，原因是根据指示，被派往国外任职的苏联公民必须在一两年后回国。莫里森告诉法庭，如果被命令回国的苏联公民拒绝服从，将会动用武力将其带回并处决。

MORRISON APPEAL
CASE

Centrosojus' Account Book
Produced in Court

other employees of the Centrosojus,

Morrison.

of the law firm of Fischer &
Warden, appeared for the
Centrosojus employees, while
Morrison was represented by Dr.
Franklin Chia.

《字林西报》，1933年12月9日，星期六

莫里森上诉案

苏联消费合作社总社账簿呈堂

昨日，江苏高等法院第二分院继续审理一起上诉案件。该案源于第一特区地方法院驳回了V.A.莫里森（V.A. Morrison）对马克洛夫（Markoff）及苏联消费合作社总社（Centrosojus）其他五名雇员提起的私人刑事起诉，指控罪名包括抢劫、诬告和非法拘禁。庭审占据了昨日上午的大部分时间，随后休庭至下周。

莫里森昨日提交了文件，显示他于6月12日从青岛抵达此处。苏联消费合作社总社雇员的辩护律师指出，这与莫里森在先前庭审中声称其于6月12日从汉口抵达此处的陈述相矛盾。

苏联消费合作社总社的账簿也在法庭上出示，揭示了该公司除一笔价值60,000美元的货物销售外的所有交易记录；下级法院中，苏联消费合作社总社经理曾指控莫里森侵吞该笔款项。

法庭就侵吞指控对莫里森进行了讯问，而莫里森则对马克洛夫及苏联消费合作社总社其他五名雇员提出了诬告、非法拘禁和抢劫的指控，但此案已被地方法院驳回。莫里森针对下级法院的判决提起了上诉。

费希尔与沃登律师事务所（Fischer & Warden）的O.费希尔博士（Dr. O. Fischer）和沃登先生（Mr. Warden）出庭代表苏联消费合作社总社雇员，莫里森则由贾 Franklin 博士（Dr. Franklin Chia）代理。

“莫里森”案

由于上诉人患病，江苏高等法院第二分院昨日下令对莫里森提起的上诉案进行不定期的进一步延期。莫里森为苏联公民，他就第一特区地方法院宣判六名被控诬告和抢劫的苏联公民无罪一事提起上诉。六名被告分别为马克洛夫（Markoff）、巴比奇（Babich）、克拉索夫斯基（Krasovsky）、亚基缅科（Yakimenko）、莫伊谢耶娃（Moiseeva）和比科娃（Bikova）。

莫里森指控几名被告去年前往他在江西路附近的住所，抢劫了他一定数量的美元和英镑，并非法拘禁了他的妻子。在此案审理之前，马克洛夫曾指控莫里森侵吞共产国际当地苏联贸易组织的一笔款项，但他被判无罪。

THE CHINA PRESS, TUESDAY, FEBRUARY 13, 1934
No. D—

Morrison Case
Withdrawn By
Prosecution

Long-Drawn-Out Affair
Involving Centrosojus
Comes To Abrupt End

Misappropriation Charge
Tossed Into Discard

The appeal of A. V. Morrison, former employee of the Centrosojus (England) Limited, against the judgment of the lower court in dismissing the private criminal prosecution brought against the manager and five other employees of the local offices of the Soviet firm, on charges of false accusation, illegal detention and robbery, came to an abrupt end in the Second Branch of the Kiangsu High Court last Saturday when Morrison, through his attorney Mr. Franklin Chiu, filed an application withdrawing the appeal on the ground that he did not want to proceed.

The Morrison-Centrosojus legal tangle dates back to May of last year when Morrison was acquitted by Judge Dalem in the First Special District Court of the charge of misappropriating $25,000 from the Centrosojus local office.

Started New Case

After being acquitted of the misappropriation charge Morrison, who was formerly connected with the local office of the Soviet organization as a salesman, started a private criminal prosecution against the manager and five other employees of the company. Following a long trial Judge Shih dismissed all the charges brought against the members of the Soviet firm, including the alleged robbery of U.S. $11,177 and £722 from Mrs. Morrison by two of the employees of the company, while Mr. Morrison was confined in jail pending the trial of the misappropriation case.

Following the acquittal of M. Markoff, local manager of the Centrosojus, Mr. Wakimenko, Mrs. Moiseeva, J. N. Babich, V. Krasovsky and Belova, Morrison filed an appeal and it was this appeal that he withdrew on Saturday.

Morrison charged Mr. Markoff and Mr. Babich with falsely accusing him of misappropriation in connection with which he was previously charged. It was alleged that Mrs. Morrison was forcibly detained by Mr. Babich and Mrs. Belova in her flat on Kiangsi Road, and that Wakimenko and Mrs. Moiseev robbed Mrs. Morrison of U.S. $11,177 and £722.

The appeal proceedings, which lasted several hearings and which were adjourned from time to time, were characterized by heated arguments between the opposing counsels and various allegations flung by both parties. At the last hearing on Saturday 10, the court ordered the books of the company and various documents presented by Morrison to be examined by experts. Dr. O. Fischer, Dr. F. Wilhelm and three Chinese lawyers appeared on behalf of the manager and the employees of the Centrosojus.

《大美晚报》，1934年2月13日，星期二
编号 D—

检方撤回
莫里森案

涉及苏联消费合作社总社的
漫长纠纷突然终结

侵吞指控
被弃置一旁

前苏联消费合作社（英国）有限公司（Centrosojus (England) Limited）雇员A.V.莫里森，针对下级法院驳回其对这家苏联公司在本地办事处的经理及其他五名雇员提起的私人刑事起诉（指控罪名包括诬告、非法拘禁和抢劫）之判决所提出的上诉，上周六在江苏高等法院第二分院突然终结。莫里森通过其律师邱 Franklin 先生（Mr. Franklin Chiu）提交申请，以不愿继续诉讼为由撤回上诉。

莫里森与苏联消费合作社总社的法律纠葛始于去年五月，当时莫里森在第一特区地方法院被达勒姆法官（Judge Dalem）宣判无罪，免于承担从苏联消费合作社总社本地办事处侵吞25,000美元的指控。

发起新诉讼

在侵吞指控被判无罪后，曾任该苏联机构本地办事处销售员的莫里森，对该公司经理及其他五名雇员提起了私人刑事起诉。经过漫长的审判，施法官（Judge Shih）驳回了针对该苏联公司成员的所有指控，其中包括指控该公司两名雇员抢劫莫里森太太11,177美元和722英镑，而在侵吞案审理期间，莫里森先生一直被关押在狱中。

随着苏联消费合作社总社本地经理M.马克洛夫、瓦基缅科先生（Mr. Wakimenko）、莫伊谢耶娃太太（Mrs. Moiseeva）、J.N.巴比奇、V.克拉索夫斯基和贝洛娃（Belova）被判无罪，莫里森提起了上诉，而他于周六撤回的正是这一上诉。

莫里森指控马克洛夫先生和巴比奇先生就此前对他提出的指控有关事宜对他进行诬告。据称，莫里森太太被巴比奇先生和贝洛娃太太强行拘禁在她在江西路的公寓内，且瓦基缅科和莫伊谢耶夫太太抢劫了莫里森太太11,177美元和722英镑。

上诉程序历经多次庭审，并不时休庭，其特征是双方律师之间的激烈辩论以及双方抛出的各种指控。在上周六的最后一次庭审中，法庭命令专家审查公司账簿及莫里森提交的各种文件。O.费希尔博士、F.威廉博士（Dr. F. Wilhelm）和三名中国律师出庭代表苏联消费合作社总社的经理及雇员。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT
（印：SPECIAL BRANCH File No... 2041 SECTION 2 D 5024 KIANGNAN Date February 16, 1934）

Subject (in full) Case of V.A. Morison vs Centrosojus.

Made by D.S.I. Prokofiev. Forwarded by

The appeal of V.A.Morison, former employee of the local branch of the Centrosojus (England).Id., against the judgement of the Shanghai Special District Court in dismissing his private criminal prosecution for false accusation, illegal detention and robbery against M.N.Karkoff, manager of the Centrosojus, and five other employees of the same concern in the Second Branch Kiangnan High Court, came to an end on or about February 12, the appellant having filed an application withdrawing his appeal on the ground that he did not want to proceed with the case.

According to our information this was the result of a certain understanding which had been reached between the parties concerned outside the court.

Attached herewith I forward a memorandum containing all information in our possession regarding V.A.Morison as well as an outline of the circumstances of the case referred to above.

G. Prokofiev
D. S. I.

Officer i/c Special Branch.

COMRADES FROM THE CENTROSOJUS DECIDED TO " BEAT IT ".

It is rumoured that Markoff has been recalled.

In connection with the application filed by V.A.Korison
in the Chinese court a few days ago, in which he stated that he
did not want to proceed with the case against the principal
employees of the Centrosojus, remarkable developments have taken
place:

The day before yesterday the following persons left Shang-
hai in a certain vessel :-
I.N, Babitch , A.Z.Yakimenko and Mrs Moiseeff, Secretary
of the Centrosojus.
Recently Mr. Sanegin also left for Hankow.
Thus, out of all individuals who appeared as accused in the case
of Korison vs. the Centrosojus, only Markoff and Mrs Bykoff remain
here. Of these the latter played an insignificant part in the af-
fair.

It is said that Markoff has been ordered to hand over his
post to a new manager and to be ready to leave Shanghai for the
U.S.S.R.

This sudden departure of important personages involved in
the sensational case in question leaves one to wonder whether or
not it was due to the possibility of some unexpected developments
in the case, likely to produce some unexpected effects, to avoid
which all comrades mentioned above hastened to depart from the
"inhospitable" Shanghai.

鉴于V.A.科里森（V.A.Korison，音译，应指Morison/Morrison）几天前向中国法院提交的申请，他在申请中表示不想继续起诉苏联消费合作社总社的主要雇员，随之发生了一些引人注目的发展：

前天，以下人员乘坐某艘船只离开上海：
I.N.巴比奇（I.N, Babitch）、A.Z.亚基缅科（A.Z.Yakimenko）和苏联消费合作社总社秘书莫伊谢耶夫太太（Mrs Moiseeff）。
最近，萨涅金先生（Mr. Sanegin）也前往汉口。
因此，在科里森诉苏联消费合作社总社案中作为被告出现的所有人中，只有马克洛夫和贝科夫太太（Mrs Bykoff）仍留在此地。其中后者在该事件中扮演的角色微不足道。

据说，马克洛夫已接到命令，要将职位移交给新经理，并准备离开上海前往苏联。

这些卷入上述轰动案件的重要人物的突然离去，不禁让人怀疑是否是因为案件中可能出现某些意想不到的发展，从而产生某些意外后果，为了避免这种情况，上述所有同志都匆忙离开这“不友好”的上海。

Subject (in full). Letter addressed to Mr. Franklin Chiu, Attorney at Law, from

Made by D.S. Tcheremshansky. Forwarded by [签名]

I forward herewith for information copy of a translation
from Russian of a letter dated February 22, 1934, addressed to
Mr. Franklin Chiu from his client Mr. V. A. Morison. Morison,
it will be recalled, was formerly connected with the Centrosojus
but severed his connections with this establishment and left
secretly to Hankow on May 18, 1933. On May 24, 1933, Mr. M.M.
Markoff, manager of the Centrosojus, reported to S.M.P. that
Morison had absconded taking with him $25,000. On June 19,
1933, Morison voluntarily surrendered himself to the Shanghai
Municipal Police in order to rehabilitate himself. Morison
appeared before Shanghai Special District Court on June 14, 1933,
on a charge of misappropriation. He was remanded until 26.6.33
when he was acquitted. Morison thereupon instituted private
criminal proceedings against M. Markoff, manager of the Centro-
sojus, and five other employees on a charge of false accusation,
illegal detention and robbery. The sum alleged stolen was
@$11,470 and £700.00. On October 25, 1933, all accused were
acquitted, following which a counter charge of false accusation
was filed by them against Morison. This case was also dismissed.
Morison then filed an appeal against judgment of Shanghai Special
District Court. The appeal was commenced in the Second Branch
High
Kiangsu Court on November 27, 1933, and continued until December 8
1933 when for various reasons not mentioned, it was remanded
"sine die".
On February 7, 1934, Morison withdrew his appeal as a result
of secret negotiations between him and I.N. Babitch, Assistant
Manager of the Centrosojus, and I.I. Angarsky, member of the
U.S.S.R. Embassy. It is reported that Morison withdrew his
appeal on condition that a certain sum would be paid to him by

Markoff 先生向上海公共租界工部局警务处报告称，Morison 携款25,000美元潜逃。1933年6月19日，Morison 为恢复名誉，主动向上海公共租界工部局投案。Morison 于1933年6月14日因挪用公款指控在上海特区法院出庭。案件被押后至1933年6月26日，届时他被宣告无罪。随后，Morison 对中央消费合作总社经理 M. A. Ya. VEINERMAN SUMMONED TO ATTEND COURT.
SUIT FOR $40,000 promised to Morison.
----------------------------------------

A. Ya. Veinerman, Soviet citizen, owner of the
"Astrid" Provision Store, French Concession, was
summoned to attend the British Consular Court yesterday
in connection with V.A. Morison's suit against the
Centrosojus,Ltd. for $40,000, which had been promised
to him for dropping his case against that concern.

A. Ya. Veinerman was summoned to give evidence
because, according to Morison, he had acted as an
intermediary in negotiations between Morison and
Babitch and other local Soviet officials, which had
been carried with a view to an amicable settlement of
the affair. The above sum was not paid to him,
Morison states, therefore he has instructed Mr. Newman,
his legal adviser, to institute court proceedings
on his behalf. Mr. Wilhelm appeared for the
Centrosojus. The examination of Veinerman took
place in camera and newspaper reporters were not
admitted.

A. Ya. VEINERMAN 被传唤出庭。
承诺支付给 Morison 的40,000美元诉讼案。
----------------------------------------

A. Ya. Veinerman，苏联公民，法租界“Astrid”食品店店主，昨日因 V.A. Morison 诉中央消费合作总社有限公司索赔40,000美元一案，被传唤至英国领事法院。这笔款项据称是作为撤销对该企业诉讼的条件而承诺支付给他的。

A. Ya. Veinerman 被传唤作证是因为，据 Morison 称，他在 Morison 与 Babitch 及其他当地苏联官员旨在和平解决此事的谈判中充当了中间人。Morison 称，上述款项未支付给他，因此他指示其法律顾问 Newman 先生代表他提起诉讼。Wilhelm 先生代表中央消费合作总社出庭。对 Veinerman 的审讯不公开进行，报社记者不得入内。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, SATURDAY, OCTOBER 26, 1935

CENTROSOJUS CASE
DELAYED

Letters of Request Not Yet
Sent to Russia

An order that letters of request
and other documents pertaining to
the action of A. Y. Morrison and
V. A. Morrison v. Centrosojus
(England) Ltd., be filed in the
Registry by October 31, was made
by Judge P. Grant Jones in H.M.
Supreme Court yesterday morning.
Counsel for both parties—Mr. K. E.
Newman for the plaintiffs, and Mr.
John McNeill and Dr. F. Wilhelm
for the defendants—consented to
the order.

Permission to use letters of re-
quest to the Soviet Russia in this
case was granted by the court on
April 13. These letters concerned
lengthy interrogatories between coun-
sel for both parties. Counsel for the
plaintiffs held that the defending
counsel had unreasonably delayed
proceedings by not replying to his
third set of interrogatories.

Mr. McNeill replied that there had
not been undue delay. The final
documents were all ready, he said,
by September 28 but they were not
filed because one of the plaintiffs
had been in touch with Dr. Wilhelm
with a view to a peaceful settlement
out of court. Mr. Newman said he
knew nothing of such negotiations
for a peace still being entertained.
Further that he did not know one
of his clients had been visiting Dr.
Wilhelm's office.

Judge Jones said that to him it
appeared that whatever negotiations
were going on it did not relieve
defending counsel for the defendants
from pushing forward the letters
of request as quickly as possible. At
the same time, he said, such negotia-
tions were highly irregular procedure
on the part of the client of Mr. New-
man. Concerning Mr. Newman's
motion, Judge Jones said he was
not prepared to authorise counsel to
set down a day for trial because he
thought there had been contraven-
tion by the client of counsel for
the plaintiff for the delay. He
understood, however, that all the
documents were now ready to be
forwarded and, by mutual consent
of counsel, he ordered that they be
filed by October 31 in the Registry.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE

11257
《字林西报》，1935年10月26日，星期六

中央消费合作总社案
延期

请求书尚未
发送至俄国

昨天上午，P. Grant Jones 法官在英国最高法院下达命令，要求与 A. Y. Morrison 和 V. A. Morrison 诉中央消费合作总社（英国）有限公司一案相关的请求书及其他文件须于10月31日前提交至登记处。双方律师——原告方律师 K. E. Newman 先生，以及被告方律师 John McNeill 先生和 F. Wilhelm 博士——均同意该命令。

法院已于4月13日批准在本案中使用向苏维埃俄罗斯发出的请求书。这些请求书涉及双方律师之间 lengthy 的质询。原告方律师认为，被告方律师因未回复其第三套质询书而不合理地拖延了诉讼进程。

McNeill 先生回答说，并未出现不当延误。他说，最终文件在9月28日已全部准备就绪，但未提交，因为其中一名原告一直与 Wilhelm 博士联系，试图达成庭外和解。Newman 先生说，他对这种仍在进行的和平谈判一无所知。此外，他也不知道他的一名客户曾访问过 Wilhelm 博士的办公室。

Jones 法官表示，在他看来，无论正在进行何种谈判，都不能免除被告方律师尽快推进请求书的义务。同时，他说，此类谈判对于 Newman 先生的客户而言是极不规范的程序。关于 Newman 先生的动议，Jones 法官表示，他不准备授权律师确定审判日期，因为他认为原告方律师的客户对延误负有责任。然而，他了解到所有文件现已准备好发送，并经双方律师同意，他命令这些文件须于10月31日前提交至登记处。

（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处

pages.en:
Mr. Franklin Chiu,
Attorney at Law,
225/229 Nanking Road, room 527.
Shanghai.

As you are well aware, during my prosecution before the
District Court of Mrs. Moisseieff, Mrs. Bykoff & Messrs. Markeff, Ya-
kimenko and Babitch, the employees of the Centrosojus (England)ld.,
for executing an illegal search in my apartment, 374 Kiangsu Road,
appropriating my money and discrediting me by prosecution me before
the Shanghai District Court by the Centrosojus, I was acquitted.

On the 8th. January 1934 the Centrosojus attempted through
its representative Mr. A. J. Weinerman (Mr. Weinerman was employed by
Centrosojus during my service there and has his own office in
Henan Road) to begin negotiations with me regarding an amicable
arrangement regarding my prosecution in the Court against the above-
mentioned persons. Having informed the local authorities as well as
you of this case I received on the 9th. January in my apartment
201/94 Avenue Dubail a visit of the said Mr. Weinerman. The mission
of Mr. Weinerman according to the request of Centrosojus was to obtain
information could I stop the prosecution against the representatives
of Centrosojus, in case all my lawful claims would be indemnified,
and secondly if I would immediately after the arrangement of this
matter with the Centrosojus leave China for any other country,
except Japan.

In case I would agree, the said departure would be settled
with the assistance of the Consulate of USSR in relation of procu-
ring passport, and visas. I have to add moreover that Mr. Weinerman
suggested that it would be desirable that my departure would take
place as soon as possible to America or France preferably.
pages.zh:
富兰克林·邱先生，
律师，
南京路 225/229 号，527 室。
上海。

如您所知，在我于地方法院被莫伊谢耶夫夫人（Mrs. Moisseieff）、比科夫夫人（Mrs. Bykoff）以及马尔克夫先生（Mr. Markeff）、亚基缅科先生（Mr. Yakimenko）和巴比奇先生（Mr. Babitch）起诉期间——上述人员均为英商“Centrosojus”有限公司（Centrosojus (England) Ltd.）的雇员——指控我在江苏路 374 号的公寓内遭受非法搜查、我的钱财被侵占，且“Centrosojus”通过在上海地方法院对我提起诉讼而损害我的名誉，我已被宣告无罪。

1934 年 1 月 8 日，“Centrosojus”试图通过其代表 A. J. 韦纳曼先生（Mr. A. J. Weinerman）（韦纳曼先生在我服务于“Centrosojus”期间受雇于该公司，并在河南路设有自己的办公室）与我开始谈判，就我对上述人员在法院提起的诉讼达成和解。在将此案告知地方当局以及您之后，我于 1 月 9 日在我的公寓（杜拜尔路 201/94 号）接待了上述韦纳曼先生的来访。根据“Centrosojus”的要求，韦纳曼先生的使命是获取信息：如果我所有的合法索赔得到赔偿，我能否停止对“Centrosojus”代表的起诉；其次，在与“Centrosojus”安排此事后，我是否立即离开中国前往除日本以外的任何其他国家。

如果我同意，上述离境事宜将在苏联领事馆协助办理护照和签证的情况下予以解决。此外我还须补充，韦纳曼先生建议，最好能尽快前往美国或法国。

pages.en:
A I answered that I would consult my advocate, but he replied that
the conversation must be strictly confidential, nobody must know of it
as well as the advocate. After these words Mr. Weinerman left me on the
condition that I would think over his proposal and after two days would
give him a definite answer.

On the 13th. January Mr. Weinerman telephoned me again requesting
a rendez-vous if I could answer all questions which were put before me.
I appointed our meeting on the next day i.e. 14th. January at the Cafe
Kleiner-man where I met Mr. Weinerman at 6.p.m. Answering the questions of
Mr. Weinerman I declared that I agree in principle to stop my prosecution
in Court in case all my lawful claims would be immediately indemnified.
As to my leaving for any other town or country I did not yet determine
but expressed my desire in the view of my safety I would prefer to stay
in Shanghai. Mr. Weinerman was not satisfied with my last declaration
but expressed a hope that this question would be settled satisfactory
and that the fact that I in principle agree to stop the prosecution in
Court is most important.

At the end of our conversation he reminded me again that he wishes
our conversation to be confidential and asked me if I agree to sign an
application to the Soviet Consulate for returning to USSR. He added
that this does not oblige me, certainly, to return to USSR in reality,
but it is necessary for rehabilitation of the Centrosojus and resto-
ring the authority of Soviet Circles in China and in general in order to
draw attention of Hostile Countries and especially of White Emigration
to the fact that Mr. Morissen regrets and again asks permission to
return to USSR. Besides Mr. Weinerman added that instead of my departure
to USSR I silently could leave for any other country making a hint that
it was for America, and that all concerning passport and visas for my
leaving would be done.

I flatly refused this proposal and we interrupted our meeting,
after which Mr. Weinerman observed that my rejection will be known to
USSR Consulate as well as to Mr. Babitch, who is authorised by the Am-
bassadorship to settle all questions with me.

After a few days Mr. Weinerman again telephoned to me and we
pages.zh:
我回答说我会咨询我的律师，但他回答说，谈话必须严格保密，包括律师在内的任何人都不得知晓。说完这些话后，韦纳曼先生离开了，条件是我将考虑他的提议，并在两天后给他一个明确的答复。

1 月 13 日，韦纳曼先生再次给我打电话，要求见面，问我是否能回答之前向我提出的所有问题。我约定第二天即 1 月 14 日下午 6 点在克莱纳曼咖啡馆（Cafe Kleiner-man）与他会面。在回答韦纳曼先生的问题时，我声明，如果我所有的合法索赔立即得到赔偿，我原则上同意停止在法院的起诉。至于前往其他城市或国家，我尚未决定，但出于安全考虑，我表示更愿意留在上海。韦纳曼先生对我的最后声明不满意，但表示希望这个问题能得到圆满解决，并且我原则上同意停止法院起诉是最重要的事实。

在谈话结束时，他再次提醒我希望我们的谈话保密，并问我是否同意签署一份向苏联领事馆申请返回苏联的文件。他补充说，这当然并不强迫我真的返回苏联，但这对于恢复“Centrosojus”的名誉以及恢复苏联圈子在中国乃至一般的权威是必要的，以便引起敌对国家特别是白俄流亡者的注意，让他们看到莫里森先生（Mr. Morissen）感到后悔并再次请求允许返回苏联。此外，韦纳曼先生还补充说，我可以悄然前往任何其他国家以代替前往苏联，暗示去美国，并且有关我离境的护照和签证事宜都将办妥。

我断然拒绝了这个提议，我们中断了会面，随后韦纳曼先生指出，我的拒绝将为苏联领事馆以及巴比奇先生所知，后者已获大使馆授权处理与我有关的所有问题。

几天后，韦纳曼先生再次给我打电话，我们

pages.en:
3.
appointed again a meeting in the Cafe Kleinerman. At the same time Mr.
Weinerman once more confirmed that all the money due to me could be returned in full, but to obtain it requested: 1) that a paper should be signed by me that I have no claims to the Centrosojus, 2) I must immediately leave Shanghai, and 3) I must sign an application to the Soviet Consulate which was proposed during our former conversation. Two last proposals I rejected, but as to the paper that I shall have no claims, I agreed on condition that my advocate should attend and personally would certify the paper which would be signed by me. I took in consideration that any could be given to me, as you warned me and that no papers, receipts and applications I must sign without your presence or direction in order to avoid disappointment.
Mr. Weinerman was not satisfied with my answer and our conversation was interrupted again.
On the 5th. February Mr. Weinerman telephoned again and asked me to meet him at 12.30 p.m. same day. After I have informed you I came to the office of Mr. Weinerman where I met Mr. Babitch with whom I began to converse as he took the place of the Manager of Centrosojus.
I began negotiations regarding the forms and the character of liquidating the affair in Court and the satisfaction of my claims.
Mr. Babitch declared that the Centrosojus cannot return the money taken from me on the 29th. May 1933 by Yakimenko, Moisseieff & Bykoff being afraid that having received the money I could endeavour to obtain a conviction of the said persons and that this circumstance will appear as loss of credit not only by Centrosojus as an official English firm, thanks to which case many disappointments would be for the USSR which is the real proprietor of the Centrosojus in fact. Therefore continued Mr. Babitch, I will compensate you materially in full on condition if you stop the prosecution officially what from the view of the public opinion will restore the "lost face" of the official representatives of Centrosojus and as soon as the prosecution will be stopped all my lawful claims will be indemnified which proposal I am officially permitted to tell my advocate, and that Mr. Babitch and one responsible employee of the USSR Ambassadorship can meet together for the formulation of the conditions between me and Centrosojus. Mr. Babitch declared further that they have no other
pages.zh:
3.
再次约定在克莱纳曼咖啡馆（Cafe Kleinerman）见面。同时，韦纳曼先生再次确认，欠我的所有款项可以全额退还，但为了获得这笔款项，他要求：1）由我签署一份文件，表明我对“Centrosojus”没有任何索赔要求；2）我必须立即离开上海；3）我必须签署我们在上次谈话中提出的向苏联领事馆提交的申请。我拒绝了后两项提议，但关于签署无索赔要求的文件，我同意在我的律师出席并亲自认证我将签署的文件的前提下进行。我考虑到正如您警告我的那样，可能会对我设下圈套，因此在没有您在场或指示的情况下，我不签署任何文件、收据或申请，以避免失望。
韦纳曼先生对我的回答不满意，我们的谈话再次中断。
2 月 5 日，韦纳曼先生再次打电话，要求我在当天中午 12:30 与他见面。在通知您之后，我来到韦纳曼先生的办公室，在那里我见到了巴比奇先生，他开始与我交谈，因为他接替了“Centrosojus”经理的职位。
我开始就结束法院案件的形式和性质以及满足我的索赔要求进行谈判。
巴比奇先生声明，“Centrosojus”无法归还亚基缅科、莫伊谢耶夫和比科夫于 1933 年 5 月 29 日从我这里拿走的钱，因为他们担心一旦收到钱，我可能会努力使上述人员被判有罪，而且这种情况将被视为不仅作为官方英国公司的“Centrosojus”信誉丧失，这将给事实上作为“Centrosojus”真正所有者的苏联带来许多失望。因此，巴比奇先生继续说道，如果您正式停止起诉，从舆论角度来看，这将恢复“Centrosojus”官方代表的“面子”，我将全额补偿您的物质损失，一旦起诉停止，我所有的合法索赔都将得到赔偿；他获准正式告知我的律师这一提议，并且巴比奇先生和苏联大使馆的一名负责员工可以共同会面，以制定我与“Centrosojus”之间的条件。巴比奇先生进一步声明，他们没有其他

pages.en:
4.
was for arranging all the misunderstandings and that they will request no
more applications and that I must tell my advocate of the liquidation of
the affair in Court and the receiving of all money due to me.
Once more Mr. Babitch observed that the Centrosojus would have paid
the money a long time ago , but Mr. Wilhelm, the advocate of Centrosojus,
assured them that in case of returning the money it would serve as argument
that a search was really made in my apartment, otherwise the Chinese Court
could not inspect. Danger comes out from this fact in case my claims are in-
demnified, Centrosojus inflicts itself to a criminal liability.
I answered that I will reply as soon as I consult my advocate.
After consulting you, we came to the conclusion that Centrosojus at the
beginning of the process attempted to liquidate the matter peacefully, but
was afraid that if I were indemnified in full of my lawful claims I could
continue criminal prosecution before the Court against the abovementioned
responsible persons of Centrosojus for illegal search in my apartment as
well as appropriation of the money belonging to me. Finally we have deci-
ded to agree to discontinue the pursuit in the Shanghai District Court
and to begin conversation on the question of indemnifying my material
claims.
On the 6th. February the second meeting took place with Mr. Weinerman
whom I informed that I discontinue the pursuit in the Court on condition
if Mr. Babitch confirms his view to my advocate, and in case I will be set
wrong I shall be forced to make the matter a scandal. Mr. Weinerman assured
me that Centrosojus sincerely wishes to regulate the affair between us as
the process still continued does not only discredit Centrosojus, as an
official English firm, but even this case puts Centrosojus in the such
terms that the firm cannot continue business in the proper way.
On the 7th. February you as my advocate had a conversation with
Mr. Babitch and afterwards at the same day both I and you signed an appli-
cation to discontinue the pursuit and sent it in the District Court. In
confirmation of our conversation with Mr. Babitch and the discontinuing the
pursuit in the District Court both I and you signed and sent an official
pages.zh:
4.
意图，只是为了消除所有误会，他们将不再要求任何申请，并且我必须告诉我的律师关于结束法院案件以及接收所有欠我的款项的事宜。
巴比奇先生再次指出，“Centrosojus”本可以在很久以前支付这笔钱，但“Centrosojus”的律师威廉先生（Mr. Wilhelm）向他们保证，如果退还这笔钱，这将作为确实在我的公寓进行了搜查的证据，否则中国法院无法进行检查。如果我的索赔得到赔偿，“Centrosojus”将面临刑事责任，危险由此产生。
我回答说，在我咨询我的律师后会尽快回复。
在咨询您之后，我们得出结论，“Centrosojus”在诉讼初期试图和平解决此事，但担心如果我所有的合法索赔得到全额赔偿，我可能会继续在法院对上述“Centrosojus”负责人提起刑事诉讼，指控他们在我的公寓进行非法搜查以及侵占属于我的钱财。最终我们决定同意停止在上海地方法院的追诉，并开始就赔偿我的物质索赔问题进行对话。
2 月 6 日，我与韦纳曼先生进行了第二次会面，我告知他，如果巴比奇先生向我的律师确认他的观点，我将停止在法院的追诉，如果我受到欺骗，我将被迫使此事成为丑闻。韦纳曼先生向我保证，“Centrosojus”真诚希望规范我们之间的事务，因为持续进行的诉讼不仅损害了作为官方英国公司的“Centrosojus”的声誉，而且使“Centrosojus”处于无法正常开展业务的境地。
2 月 7 日，您作为我的律师与巴比奇先生进行了谈话，随后在同一天，我和您都签署了停止追诉的申请，并将其送交地方法院。为了确认我们与巴比奇先生的谈话以及在地方法院停止追诉一事，我和您签署并向“Centrosojus”的巴比奇先生发送了一封正式

pages.en:
5.
letter to Mr.Babitch in the Centresejus.
On the 13th.February according to our agreement I met in the presence of Mr.Weinerman, Mr.Babitch and after telephening you we came to your office in order to visit the Ambassadorship of USSR and speak to the adviser Mr.Angarsky. During the conversation Mr.Babitch declared that the principles for the arrangement of the matter between us were attained but as to the formation of the material claims of Morison as to the punishment of the persons who are guilty in the illegal search and of taking my material belongings this matter is concentrated in the hands of Mr.Angarsky.
As you are aware this interview passed in explaining to Mr.Angarsky all the details of the affair as he declared that he knows the case exclusively.
My second meeting with Mr.Angarsky in your presence took place on the 17th.February when the principal question of my leaving Shanghai was decided. The proposal of Mr.Angarsky to return to USSR I rejected and you with my accord declared that I can leave for any other country for instance South America or Turkey, but it is necessary to pay immediately all the money due to me.
Mr.Angarsky told that he has to meet me once more in order to think and choose any country for my leaving if I do not wish to go to USSR.
We terminated the meeting on condition that the next one will take place on Monday 20th.February.
At this day, as you remember, you have telephoned to Mr.Angarsky and directed the time and place of meeting, but Mr.Angarsky answered that he would like to speak to me separately. On the 21st.February in the morning being in your office I telephoned in your presence to Mr.Angarsky who replied to me that the meeting must take place without your presence.
After I have informed you and asked if I may agree upon his proposal you advised to me to agree upon condition that after conversation I should inform you and explain to you the contents of my conversation with Mr.Angarsky.
During this conversation Mr.Angarsky took back all his promises as well as all obligations which were given to me by Messrs.Babitch and Weinerman.
pages.zh:
5.
信函。
2 月 13 日，根据我们的协议，我在韦纳曼先生和巴比奇先生在场的情况下会面，并在给您打电话后，我们来到您的办公室，以便拜访苏联大使馆并与顾问安加尔斯基先生（Mr. Angarsky）交谈。在谈话中，巴比奇先生声明，安排我们之间事务的原则已经达成，但关于莫里森的物质索赔形成以及对非法搜查和拿走我的财物负有责任的人员的惩罚问题，此事集中在安加尔斯基先生手中。
如您所知，这次会见是在向安加尔斯基先生解释此事的所有细节中度过的，因为他声称独家了解此案。
我在您在场的情况下与安加尔斯基先生的第二次会面发生在 2 月 17 日，当时决定了我离开上海的主要问题。我拒绝了安加尔斯基先生返回苏联的提议，您经我同意声明，我可以前往任何其他国家，例如南美洲或土耳其，但必须立即支付所有欠我的款项。
安加尔斯基先生说，如果他不想去苏联，他需要再与我见一次面，以便思考和选择我要离开的国家。
我们结束会面时约定，下一次会面将于 2 月 20 日星期一举行。
在这一天，如您所记得，您给安加尔斯基先生打了电话，确定了会面的时间和地点，但安加尔斯基先生回答说他想单独与我谈话。2 月 21 日上午，我在您的办公室，在您面前给安加尔斯基先生打了电话，他回复我说，会面必须在没有您在场的情况下进行。
在我通知您并询问我是否可以同意他的提议后，您建议我同意，条件是谈话后我应该向您通报并向您解释我与安加尔斯基先生谈话的内容。
在这次谈话中，安加尔斯基先生收回了他之前的所有承诺，以及巴比奇先生和韦纳曼先生向我做出的所有义务。

pages.en:
6.

Taking in consideration that both you as well as I were set
wrong and that thanks to the discontinue of the pursuit against Cent-
rosojus the defendants of this affair Ms. Yakimenko, Mrs. Moisseieff
and Mr. Babitch went on the board a ship and left for USSR I beg to
request you to take measures for delivering to the suitable authorities
my prosecution against the Centrosojus re questing summons for the es-
caped by way of deceive Mrs. Moisseieff, Mr. Yakimenko and Mr. Babitch.

In case you are not interested in this affair any more and would not
refuse my request I have honour to inform you that I shall be compelled
to apply to an other advocate..

V.A. Morison.

22nd. February 1934.
pages.zh:
6.

考虑到您和我都受到了欺骗，并且由于停止了对“Centrosojus”的追诉，此案的被告亚基缅科女士、莫伊谢耶夫夫人和巴比奇先生登船前往苏联，我恳请您采取措施，向有关当局提交我对“Centrosojus”的起诉，要求传唤通过欺骗手段逃跑的莫伊谢耶夫夫人、亚基缅科先生和巴比奇先生。

如果您对此事不再感兴趣且不拒绝我的请求，我很荣幸地通知您，我将不得不聘请另一位律师。

Date December 2, 1935
Subject Departure of V.A. Morison, ex-Soviet employee to Paraguay.
Made by D.S. Tcheremshansky Forwarded by D.B. Rao D.I.

V.A. Morison (File No. 5024), ex-employee of the
local branch of Centrosojus (England) Ltd. and member of
the Communist Party, who severed his connections with the
Soviet on May, 1933, left for Paraguay via Marseilles
on November 16, 1935 by s.s. "Chenanceaux", travelling
4th Class. Morison was employed as bookkeeper with
Chibunovsky & Co., No. 424 Route Pere Robert from January 1,
1935 until October 1, 1935, but later was unemployed
and his financial state became very bad. His departure
came unexpectedly to both his wife and friends; he did
however leave a letter to Mr. K.E. Newman, his attorney,
in connection with the civil proceedings instituted by
him in H.B.M. Court against Centrosojus for recovery
of money alleged to have wrongfully taken by Centrosojus.
The suit is for U.S. $11,739.31 plus £722 purported to have
been obtained illegally in Shanghai.

Morison stated in this letter he was unemployed
and had no chance of obtaining any work here. His case
has been remanded and as he was unable to remain in
Shanghai, his friends had given him money and he had gone
abroad where he hoped to find employment. In his letter
he also requested Mr. K.E. Newman to help his wife by
assisting her to find some employment. In conclusion
he stated that he wished his wife to act on his behalf
in the civil proceedings against Centrosojus and desired
Mr. Newman to continue with the case.

V.A. Morison（档案号 5024），系英国“Centrosojus”有限公司上海分公司前雇员及共产党员，于1933年5月断绝与苏联的关系，于1935年11月16日乘坐四等舱位，搭乘“Chenanceaux”号轮船经马赛前往巴拉圭。Morison 自1935年1月1日至1935年10月1日期间受雇于 Pere Robert 路424号的 Chibunovsky & Co. 公司担任簿记员，此后失业，经济状况恶化。他的离境令其妻子和朋友均感意外；但他确实给他的律师 K.E. Newman 先生留了一封信，涉及他在英国陛下法院（H.B.M. Court）对 Centrosojus 提起的民事诉讼，旨在追回被指控由 Centrosojus 非法占用的款项。诉讼金额为11,739.31美元，外加据称在上海非法获取的722英镑。

Morison 在信中表示他已失业，且在此地无望找到任何工作。他的案件已被延期审理，由于他无法继续留在上海，朋友们资助了他，他便出国寻求就业机会。他在信中还请求 K.E. Newman 先生帮助其妻子寻找工作。最后，他表示希望其妻子在针对 Centrosojus 的民事诉讼中代表他行事，并希望 Newman 先生继续处理此案。

V.M. Morrison, ex-employee of the local branch of
the Soviet concern "Centrosojus", who left Shanghai for Marseil-
les on November 16, 1935, returned here recently from South Ame-
rica where he is reported to have been engaged in commercial ac-
tivities. He resides at 101 Route Vallon at which address his
wife, Mrs M.Ye. Morrison, conducts a boarding house.
It will be recalled that in 1933 Morrison renounced
his Soviet citizenship and took out emigrant's papers. Subse-
quently he became prominent in connection with the controversies
between him and his former employers during the course of which
Morrison exposed the alleged connections between the Centrosojus
and the Chinese communist party.

Subject MORRISON, William Allum alias MORISON, Vladimir Alexandrovitch
alias KURUGASH alias SHERWAK - ex-employee of "CENTROSOJUS".
Made by D.S. Henchman Forwarded by D. I. Crawford

V.A. MORISON, ex-Soviet citizen - now citizen
of U.S.A., was born in 1901 in Kiev of Jewish
parents. He first came to the notice of the
Municipal Police in 1932 following his arrival
in Shanghai from Dairen in company with his wife
Adelina Yakovlevna MORISON. At the time of his
first arrival in Shanghai he was in possession of
Soviet passport No.8173 issued in Moscow on
December 8, 1931.

Morison, a chemist by profession, was sent
from Moscow ostensibly to take over the managership
of the chemical department of "Centrosojus",
centre of communist activity in Shanghai which then
operated at No. 2 Peking Road. In actual fact his
his task was of a political nature which involved,
among other duties, the necessity of keeping
observation over the activities of other Soviet
agents in China.

Approximately a year after his arrival in
Shanghai Morison quarrelled with his Soviet
co-employees at "Centrosojus" who, satisfied neither
with business dealings nor with his political
activities, desired to have him sent back to Moscow.
In order to avoid compulsory expulsion he fled to
Hankow but soon returned in order to rehabilitate
himself following charges of misappropriation
preferred against him by "Centrosojus". Morison,

事由：MORRISON, William Allum，别名 MORISON, Vladimir Alexandrovitch，别名 KURUGASH，别名 SHERWAK - “CENTROSOJUS”前雇员。
呈报人：D.S. Henchman 转呈人：D. I. Crawford

V.A. MORISON，前苏联公民 - 现为美国公民，1901年出生于基辅，父母为犹太人。他于1932年与其妻 Adelina Yakovlevna MORISON 一同从大连抵达上海后，首次引起工部局警务处的注意。初次抵达上海时，他持有1931年12月8日在莫斯科签发的苏联护照，号码为8173。

Morison 职业为化学家，从莫斯科被派来，表面上是接管“Centrosojus”化学部的经理职务，该机构是当时位于北京路2号的上海共产主义活动中心。实际上，他的任务具有政治性质，其中包括监视其他在华苏联特工活动的职责。

抵达上海约一年后，Morison 与“Centrosojus”的苏联同事发生争执，后者既不满意其业务往来，也不满意其政治活动，希望将他遣返莫斯科。为避免被强制驱逐，他逃往汉口，但不久后返回，以洗清“Centrosojus”对他提出的挪用公款指控。Morison，

in turn, instituted charges of false accusation
against "Centrosojus"; both charges, however, were
eventually dismissed by the Shanghai Special
District Court.

Shortly after the trial an attack, alleged
to have been an attempt at assassination, was made
upon Morison who, however, escaped unharmed and
subsequently stated that his assailant, who was
not arrested, was a Russian in the employ of
"Centrosojus".

Morison's next move was to institute civil
proceedings against "Centrosojus", but when this
firm offered to pay him certain compensation, he
agreed to drop the case and leave Shanghai.

In November, 1935, leaving his wife in
Shanghai. Morison left for Paraguay where he is
reported to have travelled in a commercial capacity
on behalf of his brother, a U.S. citizen. In
1938 and again in 1939, he paid short visits to
Shanghai, on the first occasion stating that he
was acting on behalf of his brother's firm; the
"Keystone Readers' Service" of San Francisco.
His visit in 1939 which was only of a few days
duration, he desired for some reason, to keep secret
and though he is known to have visited his wife
she, nevertheless, denied his presence in Shanghai.
Mrs. Morison is reported to have left Shanghai for

反过来对“Centrosojus”提出诬告指控；然而，这两项指控最终均被上海特区法院驳回。

审判结束后不久，有人袭击 Morison，据称是一次暗杀未遂，但他幸免于难，随后表示袭击者（未被逮捕）是一名受雇于“Centrosojus”的俄国人。

Morison 接下来的举动是对“Centrosojus”提起民事诉讼，但当该公司提出支付一定赔偿金时，他同意撤诉并离开上海。

1935年11月，Morison 将妻子留在上海，前往巴拉圭，据报道他是代表其身为美国公民的兄弟以商业身份前往那里。1938年和1939年，他曾短暂访问上海，第一次声称是代表其兄弟的公司——旧金山的“Keystone Readers' Service”行事。1939年的访问仅持续数天，出于某种原因他希望保密，尽管已知他探望过妻子，但她仍否认他在上海出现。据报道，Morison 夫人已离开上海前往

the States aboard the s.s. "President Cleveland"

Perusal of the records concerning Morison
leave one in no doubt regarding his general
untrustworthiness. Though he maintained that
his reasons for severing his connections with
"Centrosojus" were based on political difference of
opinion. there is no reason to suppose that this
was the case. In actual fact it appears that his
disagreement was due to quarrells over pecuniary
matters and not as he alleged, over his disillusion--
ment in the Communist doctrine.
